cards.title: Retire keyword `const`; one binding keyword is `comptime`

log.text: Note: criteria #2 text is stale (says comptime); law is bare bind per D-VERDICT-1231-2. Text was correct; wording not editable post-meet.
Independent re-review APPROVE after finding fixes; criteria verified; scoped proof green
Fixed review findings: tree-sitter const_def removed; Persist ::/:= preserved; E0349 Meta copy drop const
Implementer: const retired (E0146), Persist bare bind landed. Scoped proof green. Awaiting independent criteria verify.
Owner correction: Persist host is bare binding (`#Persist name := …`), not `#Persist comptime`. Redirected implementer.

Verdict recorded (D-VERDICT-1231-2): #Persist is a marker on a bare module binding (name :: / name :=), not on comptime. Example: `#Persist counter := 0`. Keyword const remains retired in favor of comptime for former const cases; Persist does not use the comptime keyword form.

Verdict recorded (D-VERDICT-1231-1): User-facing `const` is retired. The only module immutable binding keyword is `comptime` (S57). `#Persist` is a marker on a binding that preserves that binding across jet-dev reloads; it is not tied to a `const` keyword. `#Static`/`#Inline` attach to `comptime` bindings. Writing `const` gets a teaching diagnostic pointing at `comptime`.

cards.title: Cut pasted lines: fenced-name expansion
cards.body:
Sixteen of the twenty-nine body lines in `examples/features/memory/shared_transact.jet` are the same spawn and the same wait, eight times each, differing only by handle name. Owner wants one written line to stand for several: `<: t1, … t8 :> :: tasks.spawn(…)` expands to eight bindings, `<: t1, … t8 :>.wait()` to eight waits.

This is statement expansion, not mapping — nothing is collected and no list type appears. S75 `f.[a, b, c]` and `taskgroup` are untouched.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement both ratified rulings on this card:
- D-FANOUT3=C: ship `tasks.join_all(handles)` on `core.tasks`.
- D-EACH1=C: fenced-name expansion plus numbered names from a range (`<: t1..t8 :>`).

Then rewrite `examples/features/memory/shared_transact.jet` to stop pasting eight spawn/wait lines.

## Law (ratified)
### join_all
- `tasks.join_all([Task<T>]) => [T]`: wait in list order; consume each handle.
- Docs state when to use it vs `g.all` inside a taskgroup.
- Does not replace taskgroups for structured ownership.

### fenced names (D-EACH1=C)
- `<: … :>` expands a statement once per entry; lock-step when multiple fences appear.
- Range form `<: t1..t8 :>` in a binding target generates `t1`…`t8`.
- Not a list value; not S75 fan-out; not destructuring.
- Lexer: `<:` / `:>` longest-match digraphs; `:>` in `suppresses_terminator`; neither in `ends_statement`.
- Allowed in binding targets and expression statements; not in if/loop/switch headers or item decls in this pass.
- Diagnostics (I4): empty fence; duplicate name; disagreeing fence counts; rejected position; double-bind; each with UI snapshot.
- Spans: every expanded copy points at original line + entry.
- Formatter emission + fmt stability; wrapping rule for wide fences.
- Tooling: jump-to-definition / search must understand generated range names.

## Scope
In: lexer/parser expansion, sema, fmt, diagnostics+snapshots, `join_all`, example rewrite, Syntax.rs + syntax-decisions + grammar regen.
Out: changing S75; adding `g.borrow`; reopening D-FANOUT3 to drop join_all.

## Owned paths
- `crates/jet-foundation` Syntax + lexer/terminator tables
- parser expansion + span mapping
- `core.tasks` `join_all`
- formatter + grammar packages
- `examples/features/memory/shared_transact.jet`
- dedicated fence + join_all examples (I5)
- diagnostic registry + UI snapshots
- `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`

## Steps
1. Syntax.rs entries + syntax-decisions log for fence digraphs, range form, and `join_all` library surface as required by verify skill.
2. Lexer digraphs + terminator behavior; parser expansion with lock-step and range binding; per-copy spans.
3. Implement `tasks.join_all`; tests for order, consumption, L1101 interaction.
4. Diagnostics + UI snapshots for every fence error class.
5. Formatter + grammar regen + snapshot bless.
6. Rewrite shared_transact: prefer either range fences + expanded waits, or list + `join_all` (both legal; pick the form that best teaches the demo’s `#Transact` point without eight pasted lines). Add a second small example if one form would otherwise go unshown.
7. Verify skill closeout; independent review.

## Acceptance / proof
Existing syntax criteria plus behavioral proof: shared_transact golden unchanged in output; fence and join_all tests green; grammars regenerated.

## Blockers
blockedBy: none. D-EACH1 and D-FANOUT3 both ratified (=C).

cards.body:

After #1248 (json_coerce stderr capture @ be52c9a76), cranelift_three_way_differential_battery passes serde/json_coerce then fails on stem `serde/serde_generic`:

  assertion failed: JIT vs AOT divergence
  JIT:  stdout `{"value":7}\n42\n{"value":"{\"value\":42}"}\n{"raw":9}\n3\n`
  AOT:  stdout `{"value":7}\n42\n{"value":"hi"}\n{"raw":9}\n3\n`
  both stderr empty, exit 0

Third print is `json.to_string(Wrap<String>.{value: "hi"})` — JIT emits a nested JSON string of the prior Wrap<Int> decode payload instead of `"hi"`.

  JET_THREE_WAY_STEM=serde/serde_generic scripts/agent/jet-env full cargo test --test dev cranelift_three_way_differential_battery -- --nocapture

cards.title: I2 violation: Debug interpolation on core IOError breaks generated Rust
cards.body:
Writing `"{e#Debug}"` where `e` is a core `IOError` passes sema, then emits Rust that calls `jet_debug` on a type that does not implement it. rustc rejects the generated code.

This breaks invariant I2: rustc rejection of generated code is an internal compiler error, never something a user can reach from ordinary Jet source. Sema must own this check.

Found while building card #771 slice 1; not caused by it.
cards.plan: Implement S55/D-DISPLAYDBG1 capability parity: add the missing IOError JetDebug bridge, add a separate same-source AOT/default-dev exact-output regression, and canonicalize the TIR evaluator's IOError/IOContext Debug rendering without changing generic user Debug. Preserve the broad IOError fixture, migrating only its retired value-if spellings. blockedBy: none.

log.text: Closed after fresh-context review and repair. Exact AOT/default-dev IOError Debug parity passes; ordinary user Debug passes; commits d5b9806be and 6c6b38492.
Implementation complete in d5b9806be + 6c6b38492. Root reran the exact two-lens regression: 1 passed, 182 filtered. Broad fixture reaches only known #1254.
Implementation started on the missing core JetDebug bridge and the existing two-lens IOError regression.

Authority check resolved the card choice without a ballot: S55 auto-derives Debug for qualifying core values. IOError derives Rust Debug and sema correctly admits it; codegen/runtime omitted its JetDebug bridge. Fix capability parity, not rejection.

Scope is wider than first recorded. Confirmed independently while building #1253: '{e#Debug}' on an IOError does not only break the dev lens. It ICEs under AOT as well, with 'no method jet_debug found for enum IOError'. So both lenses reject generated code from ordinary Jet source, which is an I2 violation on the shipped path, not a JIT-only defect.

criteria.evidence: Fresh review: authority requires support, AOT bridge is complete, and the focused AOT proof passes 1/1.

criteria.evidence: Reviewer found and forced repair of literal-order divergence; recheck passes reordered/populated IOError parity 1/1 and ordinary user Debug regression 1/1.

criteria.text: The pre-existing broad IOError behavior fixture remains intact apart from current ratified conditional spelling and reaches only its separately tracked #1254 dev limitation.
criteria.evidence: Reviewer confirmed the broad fixture was not weakened; root reproduced only the existing #1254 E3412 dev limitation after AOT success.

cards.title: JIT: zero-arg ProcessSpec builders missing from the host table
cards.body:
Default `jet run` deopts to the interpreter for any zero-argument ProcessSpec builder, because the JIT host table has no entry for `env_clear`, `detached`, or `terminal`. The interpreter then raises E0956 on `process.cmd`, so the program fails under `jet run` while it works under `jet build`.

Repro on untouched code: `process.cmd(["echo", "x"]).detached().run()`.

This is a JIT/AOT lens gap of the kind D-LENS-RUN1 forbids: a program must not succeed under AOT and fail under default `jet run`. Found while building card #771 slice 1.
cards.plan: Add the missing zero-argument ProcessSpec builders to the JIT host table so they lower like their siblings. Reuse the existing runtime implementations; do not write a second copy. Prove the repro passes under default jet run and under jet build with identical output, and keep the shrink-only gap ratchet from growing. blockedBy: none.

log.text:

The fix follows the c485d5f17 pattern: a ProcessSpec method is gated by two tables, and the missing safety.rs residency entry was the actual E0956 cause, since the planner deopted before lowering ran.

Correction to the gap-set reading I gave in the brief. The jit_try_compile_manifest_matches red is currently 372 covered against a 370-entry manifest, with extras comptime/comptime_block and modules/generic_modules. It is no longer crypto_suite and generic_constructor_inference. Card #1210's frontend fixes are landing new coverage faster than the manifest is moved. #1254 owns that.

Two defects found while fixing this and carded rather than absorbed: #1255 (env, env_remove and cwd missing or silently ignored in the JIT host table) and #1252 (Debug interpolation on IOError, now confirmed to ICE under AOT as well as failing under dev).

cards.title: Tier-0 deopt target runs only a pure subset, so jet run fails where jet build succeeds
cards.body:
D-LENS-RUN2=A says missing tier-1 coverage deopts per function to the canonical tier-0 interpreter with identical observable behavior. It does not hold. The tier-0 target is the comptime evaluator, which by its own diagnostic evaluates only a pure subset of Jet. Any construct Cranelift cannot compile and comptime does not implement fails under default jet run while jet build succeeds.

Two live repros, both exit 0 under jet build and exit 1 under jet run:

examples/features/crypto/crypto_suite.jet — trace shows 'run tier0 interp (body stmt 6: Let[0] init=OtherExpr)', then E0956 'jet.crypto.sha512_bytes() at comptime can't run at compile time yet'.

examples/features/types/generic_constructor_inference.jet — E0956 'static Box.new can't run at compile time yet'. AOT prints '7 jet 2 9'.

The diagnostic text is also wrong for this path. A user who typed jet run is told the work cannot happen at compile time, and is advised to compute the value at runtime, which is what they asked for.

Both examples reached the compile attempt only after frontend fixes landed on 2026-07-28, so the defect was previously masked rather than introduced.
cards.plan: Decide the correct law first: either the tier-0 deopt target must cover every executable construct, or deopt must route to a full runtime interpreter rather than the comptime evaluator. Then close the gap so a program that succeeds under jet build succeeds under default jet run with byte-identical output. Separate the user-facing diagnostic fix: E0956 must not tell a jet run user that their work cannot happen at compile time. blockedBy: none.

log.text: Integrated reviewed parity work as 8a1bae4dd. Merge 94331874d adds the pending raw NO_COLOR regression. Exact raw environment test and the 378-example strict JIT/AOT corpus gate pass; run_tier_broken remains empty.

Review cycle closed: independent reviewer rechecked all material fixes and verdicted CLOSE. SplitViews write-through verified across three lenses on five probes (both-window writes, offset windows, retire, aliasing peek) against AOT ground truth; EventLite reset, mono-lookup guard, run_tier_broken hard floor (cannot be laundered by manifest regen in CI), diagnostic rewrite pins (E0956/E3412/E0951 + dual-role comptime voice), and EventMethod routing all hold. Final corpus gate: 378 classified, 355 AOT-oracle, 0 run_tier_broken. Every AOT-green examples/features program now runs green under default jet run. Work is uncommitted in the shared tree pending owner integration (tree carries a parallel epoch-3 stream); owned paths: Source/RunCache.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/jit/deopt.rs + ambient_interp.rs + DB.rs + Crypto.rs + lib.rs, crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/{AmbientRuntime,ArgsLite,EventLite,mod,Methods/core_calls}.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/*, tests/{dev.rs,jit_corpus_gate.txt,run_tier_diagnostics.rs}.

Fresh-context review complete: 1 blocker (SplitViews mutable windows materialize as owned copies in the evaluator — writes don't reach the owner list; dynamic-array-view example masks it by never printing the owner), 4 should-fixes (EventLite thread-local stores never reset between runs; static mono lookup can fall back to a colliding bare name; run_tier_broken shrink-only not enforced in code; diagnostic rewrite covers E0956/E0951/E3412/E3410 but tests pin only E0956), 3 nits. Warm-argv fix, event ordering, and manifest reclassifications verified clean. Fix worker launched for blocker + should-fixes + dual-routing nit; reviewer will recheck material fixes.

Wave 3 complete: core.event ported to shared evaluator (EventLite + event_ops glue); ui/events byte-identical to golden under default jet run. run_tier_broken manifest is EMPTY. Post-close sweep of the original behavioral audit found one more true lens gap: warm run-cache hits executed cached modules without installing program argv, leaking raw CLI argv into core.io.args (concurrency/parallel_scan scanned 'run' as a file). Fixed in Source/RunCache.rs try_warm_run by wrapping run_cached_module in with_program_args, mirroring the cold path; cold/warm now identical and JIT==AOT for parallel_scan. memory/returned_views + web/web_wasm_callback verified lens-parity OK (their golden mismatches are stale goldens from concurrent tree edits, owned elsewhere). comptime/embed*, comptime/find, types/dimensional_quantities fail identically under both lenses (frontend, not parity). Gates green: run_tier_diagnostics 3/3, c727 corpus gate pass.

Wave 2 complete (TIR-eval family): SplitViews and generic static Box.new now evaluate in the shared engine; collections/dynamic-array-view and types/generic_constructor_inference byte-identical to golden under default jet run. io/terminal_parity independently verified green (fixed as side effect of wave-1 ambient runtime) and shrunk out of run_tier_broken. Corpus gate + run_tier_diagnostics green. Manifest run_tier_broken down to 1 row: ui/events. Wave 3 (core.event evaluator port) launched — the final gap.

Wave 1 complete (core-call family): io/args_audit, io/args_spec, io/dir_entry, io/db, crypto/crypto_suite now green under default jet run, byte-identical to AOT expected .out. Runtime core-call dispatch via Comptime/AmbientRuntime.rs + ArgsLite.rs; runtime-role E0956 rewrite covered by tests/run_tier_diagnostics.rs (3/3 pass). c727 corpus gate green on rebuilt tree; run_tier_broken manifest 9 -> 4. Wave 2 (TIR-eval SplitViews + static Box.new) launched.

gate-policy slice landed (uncommitted): CorpusGateClass::RunTierBroken in tests/dev.rs, shrink-only run_tier_broken manifest section (9 rows, codes only), output-mismatch downgraded from hard assert to ratchet row, JET_DUMP/WRITE_CORPUS_GATE regen; gate passes 2x (184s). Reconciliation: comptime/embed*+find*+dimensional_quantities stay frontend_rejected because the gate's Run-mode front end fails where real jet run --release passes — that mode divergence is itself #1254 scope, still on the burndown. lowlevel ffi/inline rows were audit env artifacts (gate FFI lock; parity holds). parallel_scan/returned_views/web_wasm stdout diffs escape normalize_for_parity — triage later. Verdict recorded (D-VERDICT-1254-1): Full JIT/AOT parity required: no case may work under jet build/--release and fail under default jet run. Interpreter-tier parity is a lower concern; implementation may close gaps or route around the interpreter, but the user-visible law is byte-identical default-run behavior. Root causes + full table: docs/audits/jit-run-tier-vs-aot-parity-audit-2026-07-28.md. False-green mechanism: tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt deopt_interp class accepts Problems outcomes; comptime/embed* rows hide in frontend_rejected. Policy fix: DeoptInterp-with-error on an AOT-green example must fail the c727 gate behind a shrink-only burndown list.

cards.title: JIT: ProcessSpec env, env_remove and cwd missing or silently ignored
cards.body:
The JIT host table has no working entry for the argument-taking ProcessSpec builders. `env` and `env_remove` are absent. `jet_jit_process_spec_cwd` exists but silently ignores its argument.

The silent case is the worse one. A program that sets a working directory under `jet run` runs in the wrong directory and reports no error, so the failure surfaces later as a missing file or a wrong result. A missing entry at least fails loudly.

Same lens-gap class as #1253, which fixed the zero-argument builders `env_clear`, `detached` and `terminal`. These need real environment and path storage on JitProcessSpec, so they did not fit that card.

Found while building #1253.
cards.plan: Follow the pattern proved by c485d5f17 and 534a49fbd: a ProcessSpec method needs an entry in the safety.rs residency list and in the lower_ctx.rs dispatch, plus a host shim that reuses the existing launch behavior. Store the environment edits and the working directory on JitProcessSpec and apply them at launch exactly as jet_process_command does. Reuse the existing runtime; never a second copy. Prove a program that sets cwd and edits the environment gives byte-identical stdout, stderr and exit under jet run and jet run --release, and add a test that fails if either table entry is removed. Do not grow tests/jit_gaps.txt. blockedBy: none.

log.text: Closed after independent review and a separate root rerun. ProcessSpec env, env_remove, and cwd now match default and release lenses, share the locked logical environment, preserve raw values, validate child input, and do not mutate the host environment. Commits: 7813d1166, cbf0ba8a7.
Independent reviewer found no issues in 7813d1166 plus cbf0ba8a7. Root independently reran jit_run (4/4) and the focused env_overlay codegen law test (1/1); tests/jit_gaps.txt is unchanged.

[handoff] Commit cbf0ba8a7 is ready for independent review and verification. Re-run cargo test --test jit_run -- --nocapture without RUST_MIN_STACK. Inspect the logical environment lock, raw OsString preservation, Windows key identity, child composition, and direct default-versus-release proof. The broad env_overlay target has a pre-existing default-stack overflow; its focused codegen law-shape test passes.

Repair commit cbf0ba8a7 replaces the JIT host environment with one raw, locked logical snapshot. core.env get, set, unset, vars, and ProcessSpec launches now share it. Child launch validates names and values, uses platform-aware key identity, and never changes the host environment. Proof: cargo test --test jit_run -- --nocapture passed 4/4 on the default Rust stack. The focused env-overlay law-shape test passed 1/1. The broad env_overlay target remains out of scope because its existing mutation_enumeration_and_child_snapshot_run test overflows the default Rust test-thread stack before assertions.

Repair started after rejected review. I will unify JIT core.env and ProcessSpec launches on one locked logical environment, replace the false-green test with a direct lens comparison, and remove platform-specific helpers.

[handoff] Commit 7813d1166 landed but independent review rejected closeout. Fix four findings: JIT must use one locked raw-preserving logical environment shared with core.env and atomically snapshot/validate/compose it for child launch; test must directly compare default and --release stdout/stderr/exit; targeted test must pass without a stack override; replace or explicitly gate Unix-only pwd/sh helpers. Review evidence: literal resident JIT passes only with RUST_MIN_STACK=33554432; default stack overflows.

cards.title: Codegen panics during jet check on a sema-rejected program
cards.body:
`jet check` on `ui_fixed_dynamic_size.E0103.jet` reaches `unreachable!()` at crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/method_calls.rs:944 and panics.

Sema reports E0103 correctly, so the program is already rejected. A lowering path still runs afterwards and crashes on it. The user sees a compiler panic instead of the diagnostic that sema already produced.

The underlying question is ordering: why does lowering run at all on a program sema has rejected? That is a design call, not a guess, which is why the worker who found it did not patch it.

Present since b30168788 (2026-07-17), which added the fixture. Found while building #1210.

cards.title: Polyglot binder goldens fail under the default JIT lens on E0956 ModuleCall
cards.body:
The polyglot binder goldens run correctly under AOT and fail under the default `jet run` lens with E0956 on `ModuleCall`.

This is the lens gap D-LENS-RUN1 forbids: a program that succeeds under `jet build` must succeed under default `jet run` with byte-identical output.

Same family as #1254, which owns the general problem that tier-0 is the comptime evaluator and runs only a pure subset of Jet. This card is the concrete ModuleCall instance, which may be fixable on its own without waiting for the tier-0 law.

Found while building #1210.

cards.title: Auto-derive defaults: reject and override
cards.body: Pragmatism gap (seed for pragmatism-audit): beginner path should auto-derive useful built-in traits by default; experts need an explicit reject path and a hand override path. Amend or extend S55 / D-MARK-DEBUG1 family so default-on + reject + override is one mechanism.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-AUTODERIVE1=E — default-on auto-derive, a package-level kill switch, per-type reject, and per-type hand override. One mechanism, three scopes.

1. Keep the S55 silent auto-derive as the default (Printable, Equatable, Debug when every field qualifies).
2. Add the per-type reject path so a type opts out of one derived trait without writing an impl.
3. Keep the hand-written impl as the override. It already wins today; make sure reject and override do not fight.
4. Add the package policy knob. Auto-derive is on by default; a package may turn it off, and inside that package auto-derive becomes opt-in. Type reject and hand override still work there.
5. Syntax chores: Syntax.rs row, syntax-decisions.md log line under S55, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.
6. Ship one example that shows all three scopes and the docs entry beside it.

cards.title: HTTP JSON, static directory, and CORS defaults
cards.body: Pragmatism gaps from the 2026-07-28 audit (findings 8 and 14). The most common service jobs re-glue what the stack already knows. (1) JSON: client reads resp.body().text(limit) then decodes separately; server handlers hand-build JSON strings and headers. #Codable already owns typed encode/decode. (2) Static: static_file ships; serving a directory (static_files(root)) is owner-gated open. (3) CORS: a browser front plus Jet API needs hand-rolled OPTIONS and headers. Three ballots on this card: D-HTTP-JSON1, D-HTTP-STATIC-FILES1, D-HTTP-CORS1.
cards.plan:
Three ratified rulings, one slice, one HTTP surface. D-HTTP-JSON1=A, D-HTTP-STATIC-FILES1=A, D-HTTP-CORS1=A.

1. JSON both ways, over the existing #Codable path. Add `resp.json<T>(limit)` on the client, `req.json<T>()` on the server, and `server.json(status, value)` for responses. Each is one Result. `server.json` sets Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8. `req.json<T>()` honours the framing cap already ratified for bodies. The raw text and byte paths stay for experts.
2. `static_files(root)` mounts a directory under a prefix. Defaults: normalize the path, refuse escapes, hide dot-files, refuse symbolic links that leave the root, serve index.html for a directory request or 404. Content types come from the existing mime table. Range requests reuse the shipped per-file machinery. Named options carry index, dotfiles, and follow_links for experts.
3. `server.cors(policy)` middleware. CorsPolicy names origins (a list or .Any), methods, headers, credentials, and max_age. No policy installed means no CORS headers at all. The constructor rejects .Any with credentials and says why. The middleware answers OPTIONS preflight and stamps allow headers on matching routes.
4. Update docs/reference/core-library.md and extend examples/features/net/http_rest_service.jet to use the typed JSON calls, a static mount, and a CORS policy.

Owned paths: the http client and server modules under crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib, docs/reference/core-library.md, examples/features/net/.

Proof: targeted http tests for each of the three; a hostile-path test proving the static mount refuses escapes, dot-files, and link escapes; a constructor test proving .Any plus credentials is rejected; example golden; independent review closes.

cards.title: Game frame loop beyond the 3-frame transcript
cards.body: Pragmatism gap from the 2026-07-28 audit (finding 10): games graded blocked. game.run hardcodes 3 headless frames (Game.rs:246-247); scene.query returns marker strings, not component data; the raylib bridge draws one frame with no loop example and no audio. Builds on ratified D-GAME-BACKEND1 (typed game.Backend value) and D-GAME-ECS1. Ballot on this card: D-GAME-LOOP1 — a real backend drives on_frame until window close (frame-count override kept), or the surface stops implying playability.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-GAME-LOOP1=A — a real backend drives on_frame until the window closes; headless keeps a deterministic frame budget.

1. Give the backend contract `should_continue()` and `present()`. Headless returns false once its budget is spent; a windowed backend returns the negation of window-should-close.
2. Rewrite game.run to loop on that contract instead of the hardcoded three frames at Game.rs:246-247. Frame pacing, vsync, and any FPS cap are backend policy.
3. Keep the headless default budget small and deterministic so the existing three-frame goldens keep passing unchanged.
4. Make scene.query return component data, not marker strings, so on_frame has something to work with.
5. Extend the raylib bridge example into a real loop with input and audio, so the surface stops implying playability it does not have.

Builds on ratified D-GAME-BACKEND1 (typed game.Backend value) and D-GAME-ECS1.

cards.title: Compile-checked literal regex patterns
cards.body: Pragmatism audit 2026-07-28, smaller notes. Every one-shot regex call on a string literal pays a Result plus ?? panic tax (regex.jet:8-28), though the pattern is known at compile time and the engine is linear-time by construction. Ballot: D-REGEX-LIT1.

Ratified: D-REGEX-LIT1=D — a regex is always a typed literal, and the head is inferable at a pattern-typed argument.

2. Sema compile-validates the literal with the linear-engine parser. The diagnostic carries the offset inside the pattern. A validated literal call returns the match directly, with no `??`.
3. `Regex.{"..."}` with the explicit head is the same construct. It works everywhere, and it is how a named reusable pattern value is written.
4. A bare string literal where a pattern is expected is a compile error whose fix text shows the `.{"..."}` form. Register the code and its UI snapshot (I4).
5. Runtime-built patterns keep today's fallible Result signature through the compiled-pattern path. Nothing there changes.

cards.title: Open dimension algebra to user-declared dimensions
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F1 (top-ranked). PHYSICAL_DIMENSIONS is a closed 5-row [i32;3] table (Syntax.rs:261-267); a user #UnitFamily(Mass) gets no algebra — kg * meter is plain E0109 while meter / second derives Speed (live probe). SI needs 7 base dimensions; real programs need domain axes. Fix: families opt in to minting a dimension; exponent vectors become open-length over declared bases; the 5 built-ins become prelude declarations. Pay-up-front: generalize the vector representation before it is serialized into unit facts and snapshots. Ballot D-DIMENSION-OPEN1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-DIMENSION-OPEN1=D — open dimensions plus a full SI prelude written in ordinary Jet, with no compiler table. Derived-name spelling pending D-DERIVED-DIMENSION-CLAIM1 (owner leans A; question q0w4b9xl answered 2026-07-30 — see ballot explainer).

Precision and speed law (answers q0w4b9xl): a derived family's base member is coherent — exactly 1 of the product of its base dimensions' base units (1 newton = 1 kg*m/s/s). Every other unit of a dimension is an exact arbitrary-precision rational scale from that anchor (D-QUANTITY-DECL1). No pairwise conversion tables: any conversion is one ratio of two exact rationals folded at compile time; implicit conversion only when exact, lossy conversion only through the explicit rounded form (D-UNIT-CONV1) — at most one rounding, only on request. Units erase after sema; a conversion is one runtime multiply (plus one add for affine), same-unit math costs zero.

1. Replace the closed PHYSICAL_DIMENSIONS [i32;3] table at Syntax.rs:261-267 with an open exponent map keyed by declared base dimensions. Do this before unit facts and snapshots serialize the old shape; that is the pay-up-front reason this ranked first.
2. Let a #UnitFamily opt into minting a dimension, so a user axis takes part in the same algebra as the built-ins.

cards.title: Marker argument types become real prelude enums
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F2. Policy::APPLIED_RULES types every #Rule signature over 14 parameter types (TaintKind, ObligationMode, InlineMode, Maturity, Layout, Target, ABI, FfiLanguage, NamingCase, PolicySetting...) that no user can name; E0930 renders them in type syntax; TypeInfo.markers is strings. Fix: declare them as ordinary enums in a reserved prelude namespace, generated from the registry with a drift-guard test; diagnostics, jet explain, LSP, and TypeInfo read the same declarations. No S26 contact — marker args are already comptime-evaluated values. Ballot D-RULEARG-TYPES1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-RULEARG-TYPES1=A — the fourteen marker argument types become ordinary enums in a reserved prelude namespace, generated from the registry.

Open gate: the namespace name. The ratified ballot calls `core.lang` a working name, and I7 makes the path a user-typeable surface. D-LANGNS-NAME1 is on this card for that pick. Everything below is ready to build the moment the name is chosen.

1. Generate the enum declarations from the `Policy::APPLIED_RULES` signatures: TaintKind, ObligationMode, InlineMode, Maturity, Layout, Target, ABI, FfiLanguage, NamingCase, PolicySetting and the rest.
2. Add the drift-guard test so the generated declarations and the registry cannot fall out of step.
3. Point every reader at those declarations: E0930 and its siblings, `jet explain`, LSP hovers and completion, and the docs.
4. Dot-literals such as `.Track` resolve by the normal expected-type rule, so a marker argument needs no import.
5. Upgrade `TypeInfo.markers` from marker-name strings to typed argument records. Keep the string form during this epoch for compatibility.
6. No new type category. Marker arguments are already comptime-evaluated values, so S26 is untouched.
7. Syntax chores: I7 rows for the namespace path and the generated enum names, syntax-decisions.md log line, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.

cards.title: One fact model behind tags, states, taint kinds, effect leaves
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F3. Four mechanisms spell one behavior (erased named facts with set/tree matching): tag, state, taint kinds, effect leaves. D-EFFTREE1 already reuses D-TAG1's subtree matching for effects. Fix layer 1 (ships regardless): one internal fact registry, one subsumption algorithm, one TypeInfo reflection surface. Fix layer 2 (owner picks): (a) facts are comptime-consumed enum declarations reusing D-TAG1 machinery, (b) tree-bodied tags (amends D-QUAL2 'exactly two qualifier kinds'), or (c) internal-only. User taint kinds stay gated on deferred IFC. Ballot D-FACTMODEL1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-FACTMODEL1=A — facts are enums. Four mechanisms spell one behaviour today: tag, state, taint kinds, and effect leaves.

Layer 1 ships regardless of surface:
1. One internal fact registry behind all four.
2. One subsumption algorithm. D-EFFTREE1 already reuses D-TAG1 subtree matching for effects, so there is one algorithm to keep.
3. One TypeInfo reflection surface for facts.

Layer 2 is the ratified surface:
4. States, taint kinds, and declared effect leaves become enum declarations that markers consume at compile time. Enum groups already give trees, subtree matching, exhaustiveness, and payloads, so facts reuse all of it.
5. `#State`, `#Transition`, `#Tainted`, and `#Caps` argument positions resolve against those enum declarations.
6. Amend the S26-adjacent spec text explicitly: facts classify values and erase; they never select types and never drive dispatch.
7. The `tag` keyword stays for flat one-off qualifiers, or retires into the same story once card #1295 lands its surface.

User taint kinds stay gated on the deferred IFC decision. A kind with no sink checks nothing, so do not open that door here.

cards.title: Unified tags: checking behavior chosen in the declaration
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F4b, generalized by owner question q8jh0b7a: tags and taints are two polarities of one erased-fact mechanism. New ballot D-TAG-UNIFY1 decides whether each tag declares its own checking mode — plain (documentation), strict (positive fact, blessed in via #Blesses), taint (negative fact, spreads by dataflow, blocked at sinks, sanitized out via #Sanitizer) — with built-in taint kinds respelled as prelude taint-mode tags. Supersedes ballot D-TAG-STRICT1 (deleted; strict is now one mode of the unified mechanism). Builds on ratified D-FACTMODEL1=A; depends on card #1289 (undeclared tags must error).
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-TAG-UNIFY1=A and D-TAG-SURFACE1=A. D-TAG-SURFACE1 is the later and wider ruling, so it sets the shipped surface; D-TAG-UNIFY1 supplies the semantics that carry over.

1. Tags declare as a small struct body: `tag Name { deny: [...], from: [...] }`. `deny:` is required and non-empty and lists the effects a tagged value must not reach. `from:` is optional and lists origins whose outputs are born tagged.
2. Entries resolve by ordinary name lookup against effect leaves (card #1299 and D-FACTMODEL1=A) and against module and function paths. Typos get did-you-mean.
3. Spread is D-TAINT1 dataflow: a derived value keeps the tag. `#Scrub(Tag) fn` is the one way to remove it and the one grep an audit needs. `#Scrub` validates that the signature consumes the tagged type.
4. Retail sources apply the marker directly on a field, a return type, or an expression.
5. Retire the old spellings: bare `tag Name` is an error carrying the fix, and strict mode, `#Tainted`, and `#Sanitizer` all go. E0721 and E0722 semantics carry over with "denied at" copy. An empty or missing `deny:` is a teaching error.
6. Respell the built-in taint kinds (Input, PII, Secret, Credential) as prelude tag declarations, so the beginner writes nothing and keeps full protection and the expert reads the prelude as ordinary code.
7. Migrate or retire the existing plain-tag examples. This is greenfield, so migrate where the example still teaches something.
8. User-declared sinks stay gated on the deferred IFC ruling.
9. Syntax chores: Syntax.rs rows for the tag body fields and `#Scrub`, syntax-decisions.md log line, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.

Blocked on #1289: undeclared tags must error before a tag body can be trusted to name real things.

Owned paths: crates/jet-foundation/src/Traits.rs, crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, the tag and taint checkers in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema, the prelude tag declarations, tests/ui, examples/features/, docs/spec/.

Proof: targeted tests for a tagged value reaching a denied effect, a `from:` origin marking a value at birth, a `#Scrub` clearing it, a bare `tag Name` erroring with the fix, and a typo in `deny:` getting did-you-mean; all retired spellings error with teaching copy; independent review closes.

cards.title: TaskGroup becomes a nameable parameter type
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F6. fn f(g: TaskGroup) is E0119 and g.task outside the lexical block is E1110 — structured concurrency cannot be factored into helpers (live probe). Fix: publish TaskGroup as a nameable parameter type with a soundness rule priced honestly: spawns through a group received as a parameter require owned captures (~x moves/copies, no view captures), extending D-DETACH1. Jet has no lifetimes; the lexical rule is what makes view captures safe today, so the parameter path must close that hole itself. Typed Capability<E> handles were considered and demoted to a post-v1 note. Ballot D-TASKGROUP-PARAM1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-TASKGROUP-PARAM1=A — TaskGroup is nameable in parameter position, and spawns through a parameter group must own their captures.

1. Publish TaskGroup as a type that can be written in a parameter. `fn f(g: TaskGroup)` stops being E0119.
2. Spawns through a parameter group require owned captures: move or copy, never a view. Spawns inside the group's own block keep today's freedom. This is what keeps the parameter path safe without lifetimes, so price it honestly in the diagnostic.
3. TaskGroup stays second-class: legal as a parameter, illegal in struct fields, in returns, and in closures that escape. It flows down the call stack only.
4. Escape checking stays lexical per frame. Owned captures cannot dangle, so no interprocedural analysis is needed.
5. Update the E1110 copy to teach the parameter path instead of only refusing.
6. Extend D-DETACH1's owned-capture discipline to cover non-local spawns.
7. Typed `Capability<E>` handles are a post-v1 note, not this card.

Owned paths: the concurrency checker in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema, the TaskGroup type in the core prelude, tests/ui, examples/features/concurrency/, docs/spec/.

cards.title: Ranges become values: one Range type in core
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F7. a..b is legal in exactly five slots (loop source, arm head, slice, view arg, distinct constraint) and no Range type exists — bands :: [0..<10, 10..<100] has no type to be. Fix: one nominal Range over Int; both spellings construct it; the value carries end-exclusivity; .start/.end/.contains(x). No second RangeExclusive type. Loops keep specializing to jumps (zero-cost lowering is codegen, not surface). Accepted asymmetry stated in spec: distinct Int(0..10) stays literal-only. Ballot D-RANGE-VALUE1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-RANGE-VALUE1=A — one nominal Range type in core, over Int, in v1.

1. Add `Range` to core with `start`, `end`, `contains(x)`, and end-exclusivity carried in the value. An inclusive and an exclusive range are the same type with different end behaviour. There is no second RangeExclusive type.
2. Both spellings construct it, so `bands :: [0..<10, 10..<100]` has a type to be.
3. Every position that takes a range today keeps working with literals and also accepts a Range value: loop source, slice, and view argument.
4. Lowering specializes exactly as it does now. No iterator object, no allocation. Zero-cost lowering is a codegen matter, not a surface one.
5. Arm heads keep accepting range literals as today. Range values in arm heads are a later question and are out of scope here.

cards.title: Optional effect-leaf declarations kill typo leaves
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F8. Effect roots are a closed 10-set (right call) but leaves are freeform strings: =[FS.Raed]=> silently mints a new leaf; pkg.jet budgets compare the same undeclared strings. The effect keyword is reserved and unminted (D-EFF4/5) — the slot exists. Fix: effect FS.Read declarations; once any leaf is declared under a root, undeclared leaves under that root become resolution errors with did-you-mean; never-declared roots keep today's freedom; the prelude declares stdlib leaves so day-one users get typo protection free. Ballot D-EFFECT-DECL1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-EFFECT-DECL1=A — optional `effect FS.Read` declarations, and a root becomes checked once anything is declared under it.

1. Mint the reserved `effect` keyword into the D-EFF4/D-EFF5 slot.
2. Add the declaration form `effect FS.Read`. Declarations are package-scoped facts.
3. Once any leaf is declared under a root in a package's view, an undeclared leaf under that root is a resolution error with did-you-mean. A root nobody declared under keeps today's mint-on-use freedom.
4. The checked flag is per root, per package view, over the package's own declarations plus its dependencies' declared leaves.
5. `pkg.jet` budgets and `#Caps` and `#Grant` arguments resolve against the same names, so a typo cannot silently mint a budget line either.
6. Declare the stdlib's own leaves in the prelude, so a day-one user gets typo protection on the common roots having written nothing.
7. Tree matching is unchanged.
8. Register the resolution error with what/why/fix text and its UI snapshot (I4). Syntax chores: Syntax.rs rows for the keyword and declaration, syntax-decisions.md log line, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.

cards.title: Marker/trait name-collision law
cards.body: Type-unification audit 2026-07-28, F10. Comparable is a trait, a #Comparable marker, and a capability bundle; #Codable = Encode+Decode; 'tag' means three things (tag keyword, serde #Tag, D-TAG1 enum groups); #Task fn vs Task<T>. Fix: spec states that a type-site PascalCase marker IS a trait/derive reference (one namespace — user derives already work this way), plus a rule for future markers: a rule that derives trait X is spelled #X; a non-derive rule may not take a trait's name. Optional renames for serde #Tag and scheduled #Task if the owner wants them. Ballot D-MARKER-NAME-HYGIENE1 attached.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-MARKER-NAME-HYGIENE1=A — adopt the naming law and rename the two offenders.

1. Write the law into the marker-authoring section of the spec: a type-site PascalCase marker is a trait or derive reference, in one namespace, exactly as user derives already work. A rule that derives trait X is spelled `#X`. A non-derive rule may not take a trait's name.
2. Add the registry lint that enforces it, so the next marker cannot break the law quietly.
3. Rename serde's `#Tag` to `#Discriminant`, the standard term for the variant field.
4. Rename the scheduled `#Task` to `#Job`, a scheduled unit of work, distinct from the `Task<T>` handle.
5. Both old spellings error with fix text pointing at the new name. Add retirement rows in the registry and register the E-codes with their snapshots (I4).
6. Switch the D-TAG1 spec prose to "variant groups" in the same pass, so "tag" shrinks to two meanings.
7. Syntax chores: Syntax.rs rows for the renames, syntax-decisions.md log line, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.

Owned paths: crates/jet-foundation/src/Traits.rs and the marker registry, crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, the serde and scheduling checkers, tests/ui, examples/features/, docs/spec/.

cards.title: Vec3 and builtin structs print a different shape on each lens
cards.body: print(Vec3(1.0, 2.0, 3.0)) gives 'Vec3([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])' under jet build and 'Vec3 { 0: 1.0, 1: 2.0, 2: 3.0 }' under jet run. The AOT spelling comes from a hand-written JetShow in the linalg prelude (Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/MathTaskMem.rs); the interpreter has no declared fields for a builtin struct and falls back to a generic renderer. Card #1270 removed the user_ mangling from both, so only the shape now differs. Same class applies to Vec2/Vec4/Mat3/Mat4. Pick one spelling and make both lenses use it.
cards.plan:
Two lenses print one value two ways. `jet build` gives `Vec3([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])` from a hand-written JetShow in the linalg prelude; `jet run` gives `Vec3 { 0: 1.0, 1: 2.0, 2: 3.0 }` from the generic interpreter renderer, because a builtin struct declares no fields to it. One compiler, two lenses, and never a difference the user can see.

No ballot is needed: the house shape is already ratified. S55 and D-DISPLAYDBG1 auto-derive Debug for a struct, and a probe confirms a user struct prints `P { x: 1.0, y: 2.0 }` today. Vec3 exposes named fields `.x`, `.y`, `.z`, so the shape that follows the existing law is `Vec3 { x: 1.0, y: 2.0, z: 3.0 }`.

1. Give the builtin math structs declared field names on the interpreter side, so the generic renderer stops falling back to positional indices.
2. Delete the hand-written JetShow spellings in MathTaskMem.rs and let the same derived shape serve both lenses.
3. Cover the whole family: Vec2, Vec3, Vec4, Mat3, Mat4, and any sibling builtin struct with the same shape problem.
4. Add a parity test that prints each of them on both lenses and requires the two to match, so this class cannot come back.

Card #1270 already removed the `user_` mangling from both sides, so only the shape differs.

cards.title: One widening law across the numeric menu (implicit lossless widening)
cards.body:
Ratified 2026-07-28. D-INTLIT-WIDTH1=F: a whole number moves on its own into a wider whole number that holds every one of its values; nothing ever narrows on its own; a mix with no common wider type stays an error. D-VERDICT-1304-1 extends the same law to decimals: an F32 moves on its own into a Float, amending D-FLOATW1, which today makes that a compile error with a convert fix-it.

This replaces the card's original narrow framing. It started as one red test — tests/cffi.rs cffi_named_pure_callback_has_stable_c_symbol writes `x + 1` where x is an I32 and sema answers E0109 — and the ballot turned it into a language rule. That test is now one of this card's regression proofs, not its scope.

Probed on the current binary 2026-07-28: `I32 + Int` is E0109; `I32 + I16` is E0109; `F32 + Float` is E0109; `U8.{ 300 }` is caught at compile time as E1003; `increment(2)` already compiles, so a numeral already takes the width an argument asks for.

Open gate: D-NUMWIDEN-CROSS1 — whether widening crosses between whole numbers and decimals. The ruled law does not say, and read strictly it answers by accident, allowing I32 into Float while refusing Int. Amends S42 (named widths never mix) and D-FLOATW1.
cards.plan:
Ratified: D-INTLIT-WIDTH1=F and D-VERDICT-1304-1. One widening law across whole numbers and decimals. Gated on D-NUMWIDEN-CROSS1 for the boundary between the two kinds; everything below is the within-kind work, which the cross-kind pick does not change.

1. Order each numeric family by value containment: a type widens into another when every one of its values is held exactly. Whole numbers: I8 into I16 into I32 into I64, U8 into U16 into U32 into U64, and each unsigned type into the next wider signed one. Decimals: F32 into Float.
2. Apply that ordering as an implicit coercion at operators, at arguments, at returns, and at assignment. The type of a mixed expression is the wider of the two.
3. Refuse a mix with no common wider type, such as U8 with I8, and keep today's E0109 for it with copy that says why neither holds the other.
4. Never narrow on its own, anywhere. Narrowing stays destination-owned and fallible per D-SHAPE-CONVERT1.
5. A numeral takes its narrowest holding type and then widens by the same rule. Keep the compile-time range check: an out-of-range numeral is an error naming the width and the limit, as E1003 already does for a typed head.
6. Leave overflow alone. D-NUMOPS1 traps at every width, and widening never changes where a trap happens, because a widened value is exact.
7. Delete the conversion ceremony this makes unnecessary in the stdlib and the examples, so the corpus teaches the new law rather than the old one.
8. Amend the spec: S42's separation of named widths, D-FLOATW1's F32-with-Float error and its convert fix-it, and the E0109 copy that currently says the two sides must match. Register the amended texts with UI snapshots (I4).
9. Syntax chores: syntax-decisions.md amendment rows with the decision ids, regenerate devtools grammars, rebless snapshots.
10. Once D-NUMWIDEN-CROSS1 is ratified, implement its pick as the one boundary rule and state it in the same spec entry.

Owned paths: crates/jet-sema (numeric typing, coercion, E0109 and E1003), crates/jet-codegen (widening at lowering, both lenses), crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md, tests/ui, tests/cffi.rs, examples/features/.

Proof: targeted tests for each widening pair, for a refused mix with no common wider type, for a refused narrowing, and for an out-of-range numeral; cffi_named_pure_callback_has_stable_c_symbol passes without weakening what it tests; a trap test proving overflow still stops at the declared width; both lenses agree; independent review closes.

Reviewer-fix commit d637e253b centralizes non-Write numeric argument coercion across ordinary/static/trait methods, function values, inline and imported modules, fan-out, builtin/variadic and specialized call finishers. Bare operator literals now use a containing typed peer or the narrowest holding integer type, so I8/U8 + 1 stays beginner-friendly while U8 + 256 joins at U16; destination-owned U8.{256} still reports E1003 and lexer limits retain E0007. The one destination-wide law therefore still changes by syntactic context. Also remove the stale CheckerInfer/binary.rs comment that says widths never mix implicitly. Centralize widening across calls and typed bindings, then rerun the complete matrix.

Verdict recorded (D-VERDICT-1304-1): Implicit lossless widening covers floats as well as whole numbers. An F32 moves on its own into Float, exactly as a narrow whole number moves into a wider whole number; nothing ever narrows on its own. This amends D-FLOATW1, which today makes mixing F32 and Float a compile error with a convert fix-it. Owner words (2026-07-28): "Ok, again we want beginner magic out of the box and full expert control. So let's go with option f but for both int and floats". With D-INTLIT-WIDTH1=F this is the ruled surface: one widening law across the whole numeric menu.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

cards.plan:
Eleven pre-existing reds across two test targets, all confirmed on a reverted baseline. Baselines were encoding_parity 5 passed and 4 failed, and comptime_diff 14 passed and 10 failed; the #1269 fix moved those to 7 and 2, and 15 and 9.

1. encoding_parity: collect_stream_and_unfold_whole_share_canonical_law and jsonl_csv_xml_cbor_streams_match_aot_and_default_dev. Both say a streaming path and a whole-value path disagree. Find the one shared encoder seam rather than patching each format.
2. comptime_diff, encoding group: cbor whole decode, cbor canonical typed corpus, cbor options and hostile errors, gzip golden and hostile inputs, and xml parse options. Same question as above, asked at comptime.
3. comptime_diff, width and parity group: comptime f32 width, comptime_matches_runtime, and comptime_module_calls_match_runtime. These are comptime-versus-runtime evaluation differences, which is a lens-parity failure and must be fixed, not blessed.
4. if_expr_comptime_matches_runtime may belong to the in-flight branch-surface work on #1259 and #1260. Check that first. If it does, move it to that card instead of fixing it here, and say so in the log.
5. Report the split so the remaining work is on the right card.

One compiler, two lenses. A parity red is never closed by changing the expectation.

Owned paths: the encoding modules under crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib, the comptime evaluator under crates/jet-sema/src/Comptime, tests/encoding_parity, tests/comptime_diff.

First, the new CBOR TIR branch calls the schema-aware encoder, but runtime run_program_with_structs and run_named_func both install an empty struct-definition map. Second, the bridge does not pass the root TIR argument type: cbor_encode_typed starts with no type, so a root [U8] remains CtValue::List and encodes as major type 4, contrary to the ratified major-type-2 law. cards.title: Retire comptime: implicit folding + #Known marker
cards.body:
Retire the `comptime` keyword (S57/S26 surface) per owner ruling 2026-07-28 (chat).

Ruled package:
1. Implicit comptime folding is the beginner default: the compiler folds any foldable
   expression silently; if compile-time evaluation would panic or hit an unsupported
   construct, it silently defers to runtime (R12 bit-for-bit parity makes folding
   observationally invisible; tests/comptime_diff.rs battery is the guarantee).
2. The explicit demand form moves to the marker plane as `#Known` (bindings and blocks),
   beside #Track/#Unsafe/#Impure/#Region; `#Track x :: expr` is the marker-on-binding
   precedent. Demand semantics = fail the build if the value cannot be computed now.
   Required at the sites that semantically need compile-time values: `[T#N]` lengths,
   `mem.Fixed.new(size:)`, static assertions, guaranteed baking.
3. `when` as the conditional-compilation spelling is REJECTED. The conditional form
   (today `comptime if`, D-WHEN1) keeps if-based spelling; exact replacement spelling
   still open (leading candidate `#Known if`) — needs owner confirmation before parser work.
4. `fn build` / BuildPlan (D-BUILDENTRY1) remains the separate effectful buildtime
   mechanism; unchanged by this ruling.

Migration scope: KW_COMPTIME in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs (+ decision ID),

cards.title: Portable on_click across UI backends
cards.body:
Ratified scope from D-WEB-CLICK-OWN1=D (option B is the destination, not an idea). One portable `on_click` that works the same on the GTK, web, and terminal backends, and on future mobile backends. Card #1274 shipped the interim form: the flagship browser demo binds the click with `web.on` and holds the count in a reactive signal.

This card owns the design of the portable form. It must answer three things.

1. Stable node identity across renders on the DOM backend. A handler is attached to a node in the tree. The tree is rebuilt on every render, so each node needs an identity that survives the rebuild, or the listener is lost or duplicated. The DOM runtime already keys painted elements by render path (`jetDomBoxRegistry` in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/DomRuntime.js). Decide whether the render path is the identity, or whether the node carries an explicit key.

2. The event dispatch channel from JavaScript to the wasm side. A DOM `click` arrives in JavaScript. The handler is Jet code compiled to wasm. Decide how the event crosses that boundary, how the handler is addressed, and what happens when the handler is gone.

3. The portable event set. Decide which events every backend must support, and what a backend does with an event it cannot produce. GTK, DOM, and terminal do not agree on hover, focus, or key repeat.

Flagship respell: when this card lands, examples/features/web/ui_web_click.jet moves to the portable form. The `web.on` selector call and the manual bind ordering go away, and the button node carries its own handler:

    button :: ui.button("Click me", on_click: () => count.set(count.get() + 1))

The GTK backend already has `on_click` (`GtkBackend.on_click`), so the design must fold that surface into the portable one instead of adding a second mechanism (I8).
cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship one portable `on_click` on GTK, web, and terminal (D-WEB-CLICK-OWN1 destination B). Fold GTK's existing `on_click` into that one mechanism (I8). Move `examples/features/web/ui_web_click.jet` off `web.on` to node-carried handlers.

## Ratified law
- D-UI-NODE-ID1=C — render path is identity by default; optional author `key` overrides for lists and reorders.
- D-UI-EVT-DISP1=E — default hot path is O(1) node-keyed handler slots (`jet_ui_dispatch`); unmount clears the slot; experts opt the same handlers into the shared UI scheduler for ordered/coalesced drain. Never selector identity.
- D-UI-EVT-SET1=D — portable core is click/activate; richer events require an explicit capability module (for example `ui.web.hover`).

## Build steps
1. Write identity, dispatch, and event-set law into the UI/runtime docs this card owns.
2. Implement Prelude/DOM/GTK marshalling to those rules only. No second click mechanism. No policy re-encoded in an engine (I9).
3. Respell the flagship web example to portable `on_click`. Prove default `jet run` and AOT when the example is runnable. Keep GTK click parity.
4. Add capability-module path for one rich event only if needed to prove D; otherwise document the import rule and leave wider events for follow-on cards.

## Acceptance / proof
- Flagship click demo uses portable `on_click`, not `web.on`, for the counter path.
- Remount after re-render keeps the handler (path identity); a keyed list reorder keeps the keyed handler.
- Unsupported rich event without the capability module is a clear diagnostic or compile gate, not a silent no-op.
- Targeted UI/runtime tests + example golden green on applicable tiers.

## Owned paths
`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/DomRuntime.js`, `UiGtk.rs`, UI Prelude surface, `examples/features/web/ui_web_click.jet`, related UI docs under `docs/spec/`.

cards.title: Trait-object list variable is not boxed for AOT
cards.body: AOT codegen accepts a struct literal in a trait-object list but fails when the same implementing value comes from a local variable. Repro: trait Sink { fn take(self, value: Float) => Float }; struct Holder { impl Sink { ... } }; fn run() { holder :: Holder.{}; sinks :: [Sink].{holder} }. Front-end accepts it, then generated Rust contains `let user_sinks: Vec<Box<dyn user_Sink>> = vec![user_holder];`; rustc E0308 expects Box<dyn user_Sink> and suggests Box::new(user_holder). Discovered while proving #1304 call seams on 2026-07-29. Existing literal form `[Sink].{Holder.{}}` works. Scope is the AOT trait-object collection coercion only; do not fold it into numeric widening.
cards.plan: Fix trait-object coercion at the shared list-element lowering seam. Add a regression that uses a local implementing value and proves AOT emits a boxed trait object. Keep literal and non-trait lists unchanged.

cards.title: Compile stack: a nested program must never overflow
cards.body: Sema and the TIR evaluator recurse per nesting level with large frames. `jet::compile` called from a 2 MB thread aborts with `fatal runtime error: stack overflow` on a ten-line program (`shared_is_the_safe_mutation_control_case`, `composite_lambda_capture_walks_if_prefix_and_fallback_values`, `local_cell_full_surface_runs_through_default_tier`). The `jet` binary survives only because a process main thread gets 8 MB. Confirmed on master both before and after the core-five merge, so it predates that work. tests/dev.rs already works around it by setting RUST_MIN_STACK=8388608 for child runs. A stack overflow is an abort, not a diagnostic, so this also violates the spirit of I2/I4: rustc is hidden and every refusal is a product diagnostic. Ballot D-COMPILE-STACK1 attached.
cards.plan:
1. Add one scoped stack runner in `Source/lib.rs`. Give its worker a 32 MiB stack and an active-thread marker. Route each public root entry that loads, parses, checks, lowers, or evaluates through it exactly once. Keep all current synchronous signatures and values. Resume worker panics on the caller thread. Report worker creation failure as an internal compiler error.

2. Keep hook lifetimes correct across the boundary. Initialize the process-wide `TirBridge` in the worker. Keep JIT native-call and ambient runtime scopes on their execution thread. Prove compile-time TIR bridge paths still work after the move. Do not add a second evaluator or caller configuration.

3. Put `MAX_SOURCE_NESTING = 256` and one diagnostic constructor in `crates/jet-foundation/src/Diagnostics.rs`. Add one depth field to `Sema::Checker`. Guard recursive statement and expression entry in `CheckerCore/statements.rs` and `CheckerInfer/expr.rs`. Always restore depth after success or error.

4. Add the same source-depth field to TIR `EvalCtx` in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs`. Guard `exec_stmt` and `eval_expr` in `eval/stmts.rs` and `eval/exprs.rs`. Keep function-call depth and fuel as separate limits. Initialize the field at every evaluator constructor.

5. Add `tests/compiler_stack.rs`. Spawn a 2 MiB embedder thread and compile the three known regression programs. Add boundary checks for nesting 256 and 257. Add a direct TIR evaluator unit test so sema cannot mask evaluator coverage.

6. Add `tests/ui/source_nesting_limit.jet` and its exact `.stderr` snapshot. Register the code and published limit in `docs/spec/diagnostics.md`. Confirm `jet explain` resolves the registry entry.

7. Run focused tests during work: `cargo test --test compiler_stack`, the filtered UI snapshot, TIR evaluator unit tests, diagnostics coverage, and affected comptime/JIT tests. Run the verify skill and full suite once at close.

Owned paths: `Source/lib.rs`; `crates/jet-foundation/src/Diagnostics.rs`; `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/mod.rs`; `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs`; `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/statements.rs`; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs`; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/exprs.rs`; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/stmts.rs`; `tests/compiler_stack.rs`; `tests/ui/source_nesting_limit.jet`; `tests/ui/source_nesting_limit.stderr`; `docs/spec/diagnostics.md`.

cards.title: Comprehension surface coherence: loop-header split, labels, map duality
cards.body: Comprehension-surface coherence analysis (owner-requested). Three wobbles found; each has a ballot drafted and waiting in the decide lane: D-LOOP-HEADER3 (loop-header split), D-LOOPLABEL4 (label placement), D-LOOPMAP1 (map/comprehension duality). Implementation is owner-gated: do NOT start until the owner ratifies the ballots in the Tower UI. After ratification, implement the full ruling + acceptance terms (verify skill owns syntax chores). Background: analysis of composition/surface/structure coherence versus Python comprehensions; goals are versatility, flexibility, simplicity, expressiveness, power.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement the three ratified rulings on one card. Do not reopen the ballots.

### D-LOOP-HEADER3=D — one meaning for three slots
Header shape is binding; source; step rule. Slot three is an Int stride or a step rule (s => s * 2) on a range source. Retire the old counter form with a teaching diagnostic. Pointer-chase loops use a Core generated-sequence helper (Swift sequence(first:next:) shape); settle the helper name in code and document it. Yield arrows keep working.

### D-LOOPLABEL4=A — no change
Keep binding-as-label for effect loops (Void binding). Optional: suppress unused-binding lint for Void loop labels used as break/next targets. No grammar change required beyond staying compatible with the header work.

### D-LOOPMAP1=B — eager adapters; opt-in lazy
values.map(f) returns a List. Lazy pipelines require values.lazy().map(f).... Iterator sources (files, channels) stay lazy. Eagerness applies to in-memory collections only.

## Acceptance
- Syntax.rs + syntax-decisions.md for each ruling that changes surface law.
- Grammars regenerated; snapshots blessed (verify skill).
- Teaching diagnostic for retired counter form (I4 snapshot).
- Example(s) covering: range+step rule, Int stride, labeled effect loop, eager map vs .lazy() pipeline.
- I9: default jet run and AOT match goldens for new examples.
- No second loop mechanism; no second map plane without .lazy().

## Steps
1. Header rewrite in parser/sema; diagnostic for old counter form.
2. Step-rule lowering on ranges; Int stride unchanged in law.
3. Core generated-sequence helper for pointer-chase; document name.
4. Adapter eagerness + .lazy() entry; update collection method law/docs.
5. Examples + goldens; syntax chores; Sol review.

## Owned paths
parser/sema/codegen loop + collection adapters, Syntax.rs, syntax-decisions.md, Core sequence helper, examples, snapshots.

cards.title: TIR evaluator diagnostics have no spans
cards.body:
`EvalCtx::span()` in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs returns `Span::new(0, 0)` unconditionally, so every diagnostic the canonical TIR evaluator raises points at line 1 column 1. Since #777 made that evaluator the comptime engine, any comptime runtime failure now underlines the first byte of the file instead of the construct that failed — visible in tests/ui/comptime_panic.stderr and in every E0955/E0956 the evaluator raises.

29c90b639 works around it for build-time IO by running the same law in a sema pre-pass that has the call's span. That trick does not generalize: TIR carries no spans at all, so the fix is to thread them (TExpr or at least TStmt) and have the evaluator report against the node it is running.
cards.plan: Carry source spans as TIR statements through lowering and evaluator state, keep AOT/JIT/web adapters semantics-neutral, and snapshot a real evaluator diagnostic location.

Root cause found and fixed at 8b8e70cd3. CtValue::serialize renders every CtValue::Struct as user_<Name> { … }, but the comptime evaluator models ~40 builtins as structs with an internal field encoding, and a closure has no literal form. Sema now declines to record a folded value it cannot write back out, and also checks the literal form against the binding's declared type. cards.title: Expert view-provenance declarations: stable borrow contracts, trait lending, callback relations
cards.body: D-MEMPROVENANCE2=A made view provenance fully inferred. Three expressiveness walls remain where Rust is more capable than Jet: (1) a library's borrow contract is accidental - it shifts silently when a body is edited, a breaking API change no signature shows; (2) function/callback types have no body to infer from, so view-returning callbacks freeze every compatible non-scalar argument; (3) open trait dispatch returning a view is refused outright (E2305) because no per-body inference is possible. Rust states all three with lifetime annotations; Jet bans that notation. This card ratifies an opt-in expert declaration spelling (inference stays the beginner default) so nothing expressible in safe Rust is inexpressible in Jet. See ballot D-MEMPROVENANCE3.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship D-MEMPROVENANCE3=A: opt-in trailing `from` provenance clauses. Inference (D-MEMPROVENANCE2=A) stays the beginner default.

## Law
- Grammar: `from src (| src)*` after return types, view-typed params, trait-method returns, and function-type returns. Aggregate per-slot: `from (field: srcs, …)`.
- src = param name | `self` | `static.<path>`, with optional projections.
- Check: each return path's inferred sources ⊆ declaration; wider declaration is legal; escape teaches with fix-it.
- Trait clauses bind impls and retire E2305 for declared methods. Function-type clauses quantify per call.
- Type defs never carry owner parameters. API digests flag declared relations.

## Vertical slice order
1. Parse + Syntax.rs + syntax-decisions + example for result `from` (single/union).
2. Sema: attach declared set; check ⊆; keep undeclared = infer-only.
3. Trait method `from self` + retire E2305 on that path; callback function-type clause.
4. Parameter `from` requirements + aggregate per-slot.
5. Grammars, snapshots, golden example (returned_views / new expert example).
6. Independent review; criteria verify; done.

## Out
Pin/self-ref (D-PIN1), variance UI, mandatory notation.

cards.title: Member spread across a shared prefix (jetpack packages and beyond)
cards.body:
Owner instruction in chat (2026-07-31): 'I want to be able to have that spreading for packages and other things in jetpack in particular.'

D-VERDICT-1324-1 removed S75, which was a CALL fan-out: f.[a, b, c] meant [f(a), f(b), f(c)]. jetpack never used that meaning. env.jet and config.jet write default.[git, ripgrep] to mean MEMBER spread: [default.git, default.ripgrep]. jetpack reads the field's source text with Merge::parse_package_list, so S75 only had to parse, never to evaluate. Removing S75 therefore took away a spelling jetpack depends on while leaving its real semantics unspecified.

Scope: choose and ship the member-spread surface. The removal of the call fan-out stands.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship D-SPREAD1=A: `prefix.[a, b, c]` means member spread `[prefix.a, prefix.b, prefix.c]`. Call fan-out stays gone.

## Law
- Sigil `.[` after an expression; entries are bare idents only (E0970 if not).
- In list position: splice into surrounding ListLit.
- Elsewhere: fixed-size `[T#N]` list (S76).
- Desugar in sema before inference. Formatter emits the sugar. Migrate env.jet + jetpack fixtures.

## Steps
1. Syntax.rs + syntax-decisions D-SPREAD1=A; note E0970 (E0963 already S76).
2. Parse Expr::MemberSpread { base, names }.
3. Sema desugar; UI snapshot for non-ident.
4. Formatter + fmt STABILITY; migrate env.jet and fixtures.
5. I9: example AOT + jet run; independent verify; done.

## Owned paths
parser Expressions, AST, sema desugar, Syntax.rs, syntax-decisions, diagnostics, env.jet, jetpack fixtures, formatter, UI snapshot, example.

cards.title: Single write borrow of one place splits AOT from JIT
cards.body:
Split from #1199's third review finding. A lone `&place` write borrow never reaches the split-view planner in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/statements.rs split_view_plan, because a plan needs two or more candidates. AOT then borrows a temporary clone and silently drops the write; the JIT applies it. Not taskgroup-specific — it reproduces with no concurrency at all.

Measured matrix (run = default jet run, aot = jet build). 'plan' is the one-line gate `group.len() == 1 && candidates[group[0]].write`:

  case                                   no plan (run/aot)   with plan (run/aot)   correct
  ps[0] via +=, plain local list          12 / 10 WRONG       12 / 12               12
  taskgroup child, one borrow             12 / 10 WRONG       12 / 12               12
  a :: &ps[0]; a.position = 42            42 / 1 WRONG        1 WRONG / 42          42
  &w.ps[0] through a &W parameter         1 WRONG / 1 WRONG   E0956 / 42            42
  &grid[0][1] nested index                2 WRONG / 2 WRONG   E0956 / 2 WRONG       42

Planning the lone case is therefore not the fix on its own: it corrects AOT for the simple shapes but makes the JIT wrong for `view.field = v`, and the JIT refuses nested and through-parameter owners with E0956. The gate was reverted on that evidence; the last two rows are wrong on BOTH tiers today and predate #1199.
cards.plan: Fix the JIT split-view path first so a one-region plan is lowered correctly, including `view.field = value` assignment and nested or through-parameter owners, then re-enable the lone-write case in split_view_plan. Close only when every row of the matrix above reads the correct value on AOT and default jet run, with no E0956. Add each row as a case in tests/ownership.rs or a new tier test.

cards.title: Interpolation debug-label shorthand (Python f'{x=}' equivalent)
cards.body: From the 2026-07-31 video-mining audit (Indently Python series): Python's f"{name=}" — printing "name = value" without typing the name twice — was the top debugging ergonomic across six videos. Jet has S8 interpolation and the #-selector rail ({value#Debug}, {value#Fixed(n)}), but no way to print an expression's own source text next to its value. Today users write print("count = {count}"), duplicating the name; the copies drift when the expression changes. New user-typeable syntax -> owner ballot (I7). Ballot D-FMT-INTERP2 on this card presents the options. Acceptance on ratify: Syntax.rs entry, example + golden proving identical output on AOT and default jet run (I9), snapshot for the invalid-use diagnostic (I4).
cards.plan:

Ship D-FMT-INTERP2=A: trailing equals in an interpolation hole prints expression text, then " = ", then the value. Example: print("{count=}") → count = 3.

3. Example under examples/features/ (or strings/) with golden; prove AOT + jet run.
4. Diagnostic + snapshot for misuse.
5. Verify skill syntax chores.

cards.title: Probe: can a Shared<T> ownership cycle leak in v1?
cards.body: From the 2026-07-31 video-mining audit (weakref video, top comment on C++ shared_ptr cycles). Question: is a reference cycle constructible through Shared<T> (Arc + lock handle, D-SHARED-API1=A) in v1 — e.g. Shared<A> whose payload stores a Shared<B> whose payload stores the first handle — and if so, does anything diagnose or collect it? D-OPTGC1=A's traced collector covers cycles only inside opted GC scopes; Shared<T> sits outside them. v1's no-stored-references rule blocks reference cycles, but Shared<T> is an owned handle value, so the usual argument may not apply. Deliverable: an adversarial example set (attempt cycle construction across struct payloads, lists, task captures); either (a) sema rejects each with a named diagnostic, or (b) a leak reproduces — then file the follow-up design card. No weakref surface is proposed; that would be a second mechanism (I8) vs the GC path.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Answer one question with evidence: can Shared<T> (or similar shared ownership) form a cycle that never frees in v1?

## Best path
This is a probe, not a new feature. Do not invent weak references. Jet already has GC for promoted cycles (see examples/features/memory/gc_cyclic.jet under #Policy(gc)). Shared is a different ownership path — prove whether it can leak.

## Steps
1. Build the smallest reproduction matrix: two Shared boxes that point at each other; a list that stores Shared to a parent; a Shared that captures itself in a closure/task if the type system allows it.
2. Run each case under default jet run and AOT. Watch process memory or a free/drop counter if one exists; otherwise use a finalizer/drop side effect or GC stats the runtime already exposes.
3. Outcomes:
   - If every case frees (or sema rejects the construction with a named diagnostic): keep one regression example + golden, close the card.
   - If a leak reproduces: stop. File a follow-up design card. Do not add weakref here (that would be a second mechanism vs the GC path — I8).
4. No owner ballot unless the follow-up needs a new surface.

## Owned paths
examples/features/memory/ (new probe example), related Shared/GC runtime paths only as needed for measurement.

cards.title: Map merge/union API with explicit conflict rule
cards.body: From the 2026-07-31 video-mining audit (25-tips video: Python dict | union; commenter asked which value wins on key conflict). Jet's [K: V] Map has no confirmed merge/union in the spec; "merge" in code is the struct-Patch method (diff/merge pair) and "union" is the Set method. Deliverable: (1) confirm whether Map merge exists on any tier; (2) if absent, add a Core-lib Map merge with an explicit, documented conflict rule (follow the §6 structural Merge precedent; last-wins like Python unless a stronger reason emerges), full I9 tier parity, example + golden, and doc row in syntax-decisions Core table. Library API only — no new syntax expected; raise a ballot only if a genuine user-typeable surface choice emerges.
cards.plan:

Add Core `Map.merge` with an explicit conflict rule. Confirm no existing Map merge on any tier first. Library API only — no new syntax.

- Omit `conflict` → right wins (beginner overlay).

One name, one idea. Full I9 in Prelude; engines marshall only.

2. Implement `merge` in Prelude Map/CoreLib only. Label the optional arg `conflict:` at call sites.

4. Doc row in `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md` Core table. Teach apart from `Set.union` and struct Patch `merge`.

## Acceptance / proof
- `defaults.merge(user)` right-wins on shared keys.
- Callback form returns the callback value for conflicts.
- No second silent conflict policy in JIT or interpreter ambient.
- Example golden green on AOT and default `jet run`.

## Owned paths
Prelude Map/CoreLib, example under `examples/features/`, `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`, goldens.

cards.title: Function values in collections crash both engine tiers (JIT segfault / AOT ICE)
cards.body:
Sema accepts function values stored in collections, but no engine tier can run them; behavior diverges per tier (I9 violation, I3 acceptance hole).

Repro 1 — list of named fns:
  fn double(n: Int) => Int = n * 2
  fn triple(n: Int) => Int = n * 3
  fn run() { fns :: [double, triple]  loop f, fns { print(f(10)) } }
Default jet run (JIT): works, prints 20/30. jet run --release (AOT): ICE exit 101 — generated Rust fails with 'Box<dyn Fn(i64) -> i64>: Clone' on iter().cloned().

Repro 2 — string->function dispatch map:
  commands :: [String: fn(String) => String].{ "lower": lower, "quote": quote }
  ... commands.get(name) matched with .Val(f) -> f(text)
Default jet run (JIT): segfault exit 139. AOT: ICE exit 101 — Option::cloned() on non-Clone Box<dyn Fn>.

Spec intent (S47, docs/spec/spec.md:1940-1952) says named fns coerce to function values and escaping lambdas may be stored in bindings/struct fields — so these programs are meant to be valid; fix belongs in codegen (e.g. Rc/Arc<dyn Fn> or borrowed access instead of Box + .cloned()), not in narrowing sema. No new syntax, dependency, or carve-out needed — no owner gate.

Found while mining https://youtu.be/d7dhT2cBkJE (Python dispatch-table idiom smoke test), 2026-07-31.

Make function values in lists/maps runnable on every tier with one meaning (I9). Fix AOT ICE (Box<dyn Fn> not Clone) and JIT map-dispatch segfault; keep sema acceptance (S47).

## Law
- Named fns coerce to function values; storing them in collections is valid.
- No new syntax, deps, or I9 carve-outs. No jit_gaps parking.
- Prefer Rc/Arc (or borrow without clone) over Box+cloned in emit; engines marshal only.

## Steps
1. Reproduce both cards' repros on JIT and AOT; capture failure modes.
2. Fix AOT emit for function-typed list/map elements (clone/share strategy).
3. Fix JIT host path for map.get → call through function values.
4. Add golden example for string→fn dispatch; prove jet run and jet run --release.
5. Confirm no jit_gaps entry; independent review + criteria verify; done.
