cards.title: One manifest parser and the ratified manifest vocabulary
cards.body: package.jet is read by two parsers today. The compile path uses the legacy flat parser at crates/jet-pkg-model/src/PackageManifest/ (wired at crates/jet-driver/src/Loader.rs:349), which knows payload:, packages:, effects: and build: and has no vocabulary for outputs:. Tooling and Canvas read the same file with the role-typed parser at crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package.rs. This card makes the role-typed parser the only one and lands the ratified field list: bare name: and version: at the top level, the identity: wrapper deleted, and deps:, outputs:, settings:, build:, policy:, members: as the block nouns.
cards.plan: Implements D-CONF-PLANE1, D-CONF-NAME1 — ratified 2026-08-06. Read each decision verbatim (tower brief on this card's parent proposal, or tower decision show) before building; the ratified outcome text is the law, this plan is the route. Every requirement is a discrete exit criterion below: meet each with targeted proof (tests, snapshots, examples with golden output), and keep I9 tier parity inside this card — AOT, default jet run (JIT), and the interpreter must agree on every surface this card ships before it closes. Delete every superseded form the decisions retire in the same change; do not leave compatibility shims or parallel spellings. Reference: docs/proposals/build-config-one-plane.md.

log.text: Closed: single role-typed manifest parser merged to master; outputs proof 4/4 and hello smoke green after integration. Reviewer bd2-rev3 verified all nine criteria.

Fixed both reviewer blockers on bd2/manifest (commit 15f6bec8d, worktree .claude/worktrees/manifest).

BLOCKER 1: remote.rs's #[cfg(test)] callers now build DepSource::Provider{provider:Source::Path,..}/DepSource::Version values instead of string literals. cargo test -p jetpack --lib now compiles. But fixing compile surfaced 12 further failures the broken build had hidden: MemberSelect, Provider/fetch, Provider::tests, Trust::tests fixtures all still wrote payload:-wrapped pkg.jet (pre-rewrite syntax the new strict parser rejects) and Transition::legacy_plan re-read the Package root from disk (re-parsing the untranslated legacy payload: text) instead of composing from the already-translated in-memory root_facts. Migrated every stale fixture to bare name:/version: and fixed the disk re-read. Final: 556 passed, 5 failed (script_registry needs-php/needs-ruby, Shell fish pty, Store::Broker peer-creds, Store::Tests module-boundary — all env-flaky, exact same 5 that fail on master).

BLOCKER 2: outputs_build fixture rewritten. entry: run (single segment) can never prove outputs: drives anything: entry_path and legacy_run_entry run the literally identical root-file scan for that case (confirmed by testing — renaming the fn to a non-run name just fails compile with E0101, since sema independently requires a literal fn run regardless of the manifest). Used the dotted form instead: entry: service.run, where entry.jet's use service import leads entry_path into service/module.jet, a directory module the legacy fallback structurally cannot reach (it only scans root-level files). Verified manually both tiers (jet run + jet build/AOT) resolve and produce the expected output, and that deleting outputs: fails closed (can't find the file run.jet). Added entry_resolution_requires_the_outputs_block as the negative proof. All 4 tests in tests/package_outputs.rs pass.

Non-blockers taken: (1) Blocks.rs MANIFEST_SCALAR_FIELDS now also masks members:/configs: (defaults/environments/services were already in MANIFEST_BLOCKS, contra the review note; only members/configs were genuinely missing). (4) docs/spec/architecture.md:184 and tests/workspace_crates.rs:217,273 PackageManifest -> PackageFacts.
Skipped: (2) Transition.rs:1672 nameless-pkg.jet already fails closed downstream via PackageFacts::MissingName (not silent success, just a less specific message); real fix isn't a one-liner, left for follow-up. (3) auto_derive_policy_invalid stderr saying package.jet for a pkg.jet fixture: other diagnostics in the same file hardcode package.jet in fix text the same way, may be an intentional canonical-name nudge rather than a bug; skipped rather than guess.

Verified: cargo build --workspace clean; cargo test -p jetpack --lib 556/5 (matches master shape); cargo test --test package_outputs 4/4; cargo test -p jet-pkg-model --lib unaffected by Blocks.rs change (diffed with/without the edit, same failure set as master aside from one flaky FFI test). Not merged; branch left at bd2/manifest for integration.

REVIEW non-blocking notes (do not need to hold the merge): (1) MANIFEST_SCALAR_FIELDS (crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package/Blocks.rs:979) omits members, configs, defaults, environments and services, so a package.jet with a co-located fn build plus e.g. members: find("./packages") still leaks unmasked manifest text into the build-entry parse — same shape as the bug 0a2a86863 fixed, left half closed. (2) crates/jetpack/src/Transition.rs:1672 render_legacy_package_root now hand-rolls a payload:/identity: reader; it is a one-way migration splice guarded by a following canonical parse, but a pkg.jet with no name now emits name: "" and fails downstream with MissingName instead of master's explicit migration error. (3) tests/ui/auto_derive_policy_invalid/stderr now tells the user to fix package.jet while the fixture file is literally pkg.jet. (4) docs/spec/architecture.md:184 and tests/workspace_crates.rs:217,273 still name PackageManifest as a live seam touch point (comments only).

REVIEW BLOCKER 2 (criterion 4) — tests/package_outputs.rs is false-green: it cannot distinguish outputs:-driven entry resolution from the pre-existing legacy_run_entry fallback. Proof: copy examples/features/packages/outputs_build/service.jet next to a package.jet holding only name:/version: (outputs: block deleted) and jet run prints the same 'outputs: demo drives the build', while jet build emits the same build/service.rs. The docs must say plainly that stamp.at describes the lock file's history, not the moment this binary was built.

cards.title: One outcome carrier under T? and T ? E
cards.body: An outcome has three independent facts: a payload (a value, part of one, or none), a verdict (clean, succeeded with notes, or failed) and attached reports. T? is the view where absence is clean and T ? E is the view where the report matters, so the two surface spellings stay exactly as ratified while the thing underneath becomes one carrier. Success-with-notes and failure-with-partial-results are the same carrier's middle states, reached without a third type, and conversions between the views stop being ceremonies because there is nothing to convert.
cards.plan: Implements D-FAIL-CARRIER1, D-FAIL-MODEL1 — ratified 2026-08-06. Read each decision verbatim (tower brief on this card's parent proposal, or tower decision show) before building; the ratified outcome text is the law, this plan is the route. Every requirement is a discrete exit criterion below: meet each with targeted proof (tests, snapshots, examples with golden output), and keep I9 tier parity inside this card — AOT, default jet run (JIT), and the interpreter must agree on every surface this card ships before it closes. Delete every superseded form the decisions retire in the same change; do not leave compatibility shims or parallel spellings. Reference: docs/proposals/failure-one-report-three-routes.md.

log.text: Log correction: .noting() was removed in review round 1. It was an invented write spelling that duplicated the ratified ? "note" hop (D-FAIL-CTX1, card #1532). Notes are read-only on this card: they live on the outcome value, opt-in per error type like partial. Review passed after the fix. The carrier home deviation from I9's named folder is balloted as D-I9-HOME1 on card #1604.

[review-fixes] Fresh-context review raised four blocking findings on bd2/carrier; all four are fixed on commit 4e898cd4f.

B1 notes bag. jet_noting pushed into a thread-local and jet_notes drained it, so two outcomes shared one set of notes, a second read came back empty, and notes did not cross a thread. Notes now live on the outcome value, opted into per error type exactly as partial results already were: an error type carries them under the field name notes. The thread-local is deleted. .noting is deleted with it — writing a note is the ? hop D-FAIL-CTX1 ratifies, which is card #1532's; criterion 4 asks for the read, and the read is what shipped.

B2 false green. The example now holds three outcomes at once with distinct notes, reads one of them twice, and its golden output shows people, ports, then people again. The targeted test does the same and also asserts the program's actual output on the interpreter tier, so a shared bag cannot pass it.

B3 engine drift. One TIR node, CarrierFact, now carries both middle states. AOT emit spells the projection onto the report; both interpreters call one marshaller, Comptime::Builtins::carrier_fact, which hands that projection to the prelude's jet_partial or jet_notes. What a success and a failure each answer is stated once, in the prelude. The hardcoded field name in the comptime arm is gone; every path takes the name from the same Syntax constant.

B4 tautology. The erasure test imports jet::Outcome::{JetAbsent, JetOutcome} instead of declaring local copies, so it fails if either type grows a field. Source/lib.rs re-exports the module for it.

Proof after the fixes: cargo build clean. cargo test --test outcome_carrier 5 of 5. Golden 61 failures, unchanged from before the fixes, neither example among them, and the re-blessed partial_and_notes.out matches AOT and default jet run line for line. Corpus parity gate: both examples pass; its only two failures remain concurrency/shield_commit and io/terminal_parity, unrelated and pre-existing. jet fmt --check clean on all three new files. The carrier_partial_not_kept UI snapshot still matches.

[deviation] The one carrier lives in crates/jet-foundation/src/Outcome.rs, not under crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/** as criterion 1 and the I9 text say. Reason: the comptime interpreter must name the same Rust type, and jet-comptime cannot depend on jet-codegen, so jet-foundation is the only crate both sides already share. The file is still prelude part one — Codegen/mod.rs includes it verbatim, ahead of every other part, for native builds, and Codegen/Web.rs includes the same file for the wasm module. It is also a real module in jet-foundation, which is what lets the compiler's own interpreters call the very same jet_partial and jet_notes the generated program calls; that is the mechanism that keeps the tiers from drifting rather than a way around I9. Flagging it for the owner: either the invariant text should say Prelude parts may live in jet-foundation when a seam crate must share them, or the carrier needs a different home.

[handoff] All ten criteria met. Branch bd2/carrier, head e580c8064, worktree .claude/worktrees/carrier. Not merged; ready for review and integration.

COMMITS THIS SESSION
- af487b194 wip: .or_err lifts a clean absence into a failure (checkpoint of the prior session's uncommitted work)
- 3d57f72da merge: master fixture repairs into bd2/carrier. Three conflicts, each master adding a feature beside a line the carrier had rewritten; every resolution keeps master's feature and states it in the carrier's vocabulary. Rebase was not cheap: master moved 178 files with 20 overlapping this branch.
- 19e0718a5 feat(carrier): the outcome's middle states are readable from Jet
- e580c8064 feat(carrier): the web tier and the priority queue join the one carrier

WHAT LANDED
- .or_err("why"), .partial(), .noting("...") and .notes(). Semantics live only in crates/jet-foundation/src/Outcome.rs, which is prelude part one. AOT emit, the TIR interpreter and the comptime interpreter marshal onto them, and both interpreters call the very same jet_noting and jet_notes symbols.
- A failure keeps part of its work by carrying it on its report under the field name partial, at the same type the outcome carries. That is the ratified opt-in-per-error-type shape. An error type that declined gets the ordinary E0302.
- The web tier stopped spelling T? as Rust's own Option. Its wasm module now includes the same Outcome.rs file the native prelude puts first.
- PriorityQueue.remove arrived from master answering a plain Option; it now answers the carrier.

TESTS
- cargo test --test outcome_carrier: 5 of 5 pass, including the two new middle-state and web-tier proofs.
- cargo test --test golden: 61 failures, down from the 63 the branch inherited. Neither new example is among them and no example was edited to pass.
- cargo test --test dev example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate: both examples pass in the deopt_interp AOT-oracle class, so pure interpreter, default tiered run and AOT agree on each. The gate's only two failures, concurrency/shield_commit and io/terminal_parity, are unrelated and pre-existing.
- cargo test --test grammar: 18 of 18 pass. jet fmt --check clean on all three new files. cargo build clean throughout.

KNOWN UNRELATED RED, NOT THIS CARD
- tests/fmt.rs fmt_is_lossless_on_supported_source_corpus fails on examples/features/packages/outputs_build/package.jet, which the fmt corpus cannot parse. That file arrived with master's manifest work (card #1517).
- 28 ui_snapshots mismatches are master's diagnostic-text drift. A scan of the full run shows none mentions the carrier, or_err, partial or notes, so blessing them here would accept another card's change.
- 20 web test failures in web_build, web_partition and web_tir_contract. Measured with and without this card's web change: the failure sets are identical, so they are pre-existing fixture drift.

NOTE FOR LATER CARDS
The web tier's TIR support does not lower an optional inside a wasm function at all today (E-WEB-TIR-UNSUPPORTED). That is a pre-existing web gap, not one this card opened. The carrier is in place for when web lowers one.

[handoff] Branch bd2/carrier, head 78ebd8810, worktree .claude/worktrees/carrier. Build green; tests/outcome_carrier.rs passes (2/2); golden is back at the base 63-failure line with no new failure and no example edited.

- The carrier moved to crates/jet-foundation/src/Outcome.rs and is still the first PRELUDE_PART, so AOT, the Cranelift hosts and the comptime interpreter all name one Rust type. jet-comptime does not depend on jet-codegen, so jet-foundation is the only shared home. Every module that include!s a prelude file now imports it.

- Host adapters in jet-jit and jet-comptime convert at their own boundary; they re-encode no meaning.

REMAINING

About 890 call sites across jet-comptime, jet-codegen TIR eval, jet-jit ambient and Source/Compiler.rs. The shape to land: Present(payload) plus Failed(report), with a clean report for the optional view.
- c4: a failure that carries a partial payload and an outcome that carries notes, both readable from Jet, with a golden example under examples/features/errors/. No surface exists yet.
- c5: .or_err("why"). The carrier already has the method in Rust; Jet has no spelling for it. Needs sema method inference, TIR lowering, AOT emit, the Cranelift path and interpreter ambient.

- c7 to c10: Syntax.rs entries, the syntax-decisions.md log, regenerated grammars and re-blessed snapshots, all owed by c4 and c5.
- tests/corelib.rs: 134 pass, 52 fail. The remaining failures are DB JetMap/BTreeMap and a &String mismatch, neither of which involves the carrier; io/db was already failing at the base. The corelib base count was not measured, so the next owner should measure it before reading those 52 as clean.

The old => () ? form is deleted, not aliased.

cards.body: Inside a fallback expression, err simply names the failure. No lambda, no binder, no parentheses, so the upgrade from swallowing a failure to handling it costs one word. cards.title: The compile-time mark is $ and it is written at every mention
cards.body: Compile time is spelled four ways today. This card makes $ the one mark, and the mark belongs to the name, so it is written at every mention: $limit :: 1000 then print("{$limit}"). #Known, #Known if and the #Known block retire in favour of $name, $if and a bare $ block, and #Known leaves the marker plane because a stage is not a rule about a target. The rule for carrying a value out of a compile-time block disappears, because the name is the same name inside and outside, so D-CTMARKER1 retires outright.

Comptime::Interpreter::eval at crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Interpreter.rs:461 merges scope into globals, builds a TirBridge ExprEvalRequest, delegates to TirBridge::eval_expr, then copies the mutated map back into scope. The only Expr matches left in jet-comptime are Purity's no-op, the write_back I already fixed in d22b848d1, and two integer-width helpers. There is exactly one evaluator, the TIR one, so the whole fix lives there.

HALF 2 AS PRESCRIBED, and why the fold survived without a read arm. In crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/expressions.rs the arm matching ComptimeName with a stamped value lowers to CtLit, and it sits BEFORE the is_eval_fragment arm, so it shadowed it. Inside a fold fragment a marked mention lowered to a baked value and never a place, which is exactly why write-back had nothing to reach. Reordering so the fragment arm wins makes the mention a Local place.

WHAT THAT EXPOSED, measured in order:

1. With the reorder alone: three E0107, "nothing named $ct exists here", whose fix line suggests the identical spelling. That is the same self-suggesting message dollar3 measured. Cause: the lexer merges the mark into one Ident token, so take_mark never fires for a marked binding in a function body, and the binding parses through the ORDINARY path with is_comptime false. See the construction near line 117 of jet-parser Parser/Statements/bindings.rs; the is_comptime true construction near line 543 is unreachable for this spelling. A marked binding was therefore getting implicit-fold semantics, and the implicit path calls forget_ct_bindings when a fold advances a receiver. That is what deleted the marked reader from the scope between line 5 and line 6 of the reproducer.

2. Setting is_comptime from the name, with is_comptime set to Syntax::is_comptime_name of the binding name at that construction, cleared all three E0107. The mark is the demand. That single line reads correct against D-META-STAGE1=B on its own and is worth keeping when someone lands the whole fix.

3. That left four E0956, "method read_u8 can't run at compile time yet", on both marked read lines. Binding the fragment local with the folded value's type instead of None did not move it.

THE ONE REMAINING BLOCKER: as a baked CtLit the receiver was a concrete value and the TIR evaluator's handle path accepted read_u8; as a Local place it does not. The gate is in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/subset/handles.rs, the only place read_u8 is named outside jet-sema's signature table and jet-foundation's StreamCursor. Someone needs to make that handle path admit a marked Local receiver the same way it admits whatever the CtLit form presented. That is the whole remaining distance: the E0107 and the forget-the-binding behaviour are solved, and only the handle gate stands between this and the reproducer printing 7 then 9.

In crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/expressions.rs the arm  sits BEFORE the  arm, so it shadowed it: inside a fold fragment a marked mention lowered to a baked value, never a place, which is why write-back had nothing to reach. Reordering so the fragment arm wins makes the mention a Local place.

WHAT THAT EXPOSED, measured in order
1. With the reorder alone: 3x E0107,  with the fix line suggesting  — the same self-suggesting message dollar3 measured. Cause found: the lexer merges  into one Ident token, so  never fires for  in a function body and the binding parses through the ORDINARY path with is_comptime: false (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/bindings.rs, the construction near line 117; the is_comptime: true construction near line 543 is unreachable for this spelling). A marked binding was therefore getting implicit-fold semantics, and the implicit path calls forget_ct_bindings when a fold advances a receiver — which is what deleted $ct from the scope between line 5 and line 6.
2. Setting is_comptime from the name (is_comptime: crate::Syntax::is_comptime_name(&name)) at that construction cleared all three E0107. The mark is the demand; this line looks correct against D-META-STAGE1=B regardless of the rest, and is worth keeping when someone lands the whole fix.
3. That left 4x E0956 , on both $ct.read_u8() lines. Binding the fragment local with the folded value's type (env.bind(name, TLocal::user(name), value.jet_type()) instead of None) did not move it.

THE ONE REMAINING BLOCKER
As a baked CtLit the receiver was a concrete value and the TIR evaluator's handle path accepted read_u8; as a Local place it does not. The gate is in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/subset/handles.rs (the only place read_u8 is named outside jet-sema's signature table and jet-foundation's StreamCursor). Someone needs to make that handle path admit a marked Local receiver the same way it admits whatever the CtLit form presented. That is the whole remaining distance: E0107 and the forget-the-binding behaviour are solved, and only the handle gate stands between this and 7|9|7|9.

Nothing was committed from this attempt. d22b848d1 is unchanged and still builds clean.

[bd3-dollar3] Criteria 1 and 6 stay open. I tried the prescribed fix, measured it twice, and it is not sufficient — the branch is back at d22b848d1 with no net change from me, because a half-fix here is worse than none. Recording what I proved so the next worker does not spend the same two build cycles.

WHAT I CONFIRMED
The reproducer prints 7|7|7|9 on d22b848d1, as logged.

The TIR side is not missing a marked-name concept. crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/expressions.rs has three ComptimeName arms; the first, guarded on value: Some(..), lowers every mention to TExprKind::CtLit. A CtLit is a value, not a place, so no write-back can reach it — that is why the marked reader never advances while the plain one does. The plain one advances because Expr::Ident lowers a seeded comptime binding to TExprKind::ConstRef, and ConstRef both reads (eval/exprs.rs:2157) and writes back (eval/exprs.rs:5476, added for card #1602). So the shape of the fix looked obvious: give ComptimeName the same treatment Ident gets.

WHY THAT ALONE FAILS
I tried it two ways: reordering so the eval-fragment arm wins, and mirroring the Ident const branch exactly (lower_comptime_scalar, else ConstRef(name)). Both build clean and both produce the identical result — three E0107 'a name must be declared before it's used' on the marked names, instead of 7|9|7|9.

The reason is in jet-comptime, not jet-codegen. A repository search for ComptimeName across crates/jet-comptime returns exactly two hits: Purity.rs:244, which ignores it, and Methods/dispatch.rs:1601, the write_back arm added in d22b848d1. There is no read arm anywhere in jet-comptime that resolves Expr::ComptimeName to a value. Today the fold only works because sema stamps value: Some(..) on each mention and the CtLit arm hands that stamp back. The moment a marked name resolves as a place instead of the stamp, nothing can read it, the fold of  :: .read_u8() fails,  never gets a value, and its later mentions report E0107.

THE FIX NEEDS BOTH HALVES IN ONE CHANGE
First, jet-comptime needs a read arm for Expr::ComptimeName that resolves from the comptime scope by the marked name, mirroring its Expr::Ident arm — the mark is part of the identifier, so the scope key carries it. Second, once a marked name can be read as a binding, TIR lowering can resolve it as a place the way Ident does, and the write_back arm already in place closes the loop. Landing the second without the first is what I measured, twice.

Worth checking while doing it: whether the comptime scope stores the binding under the marked key or the bare one, because ConstRef lookup goes through self.globals and a key mismatch would look exactly like this failure too.

[handoff] Head d22b848d1 on bd3/dollar. Criteria 1 and 6 still open. I prescribed the fix last session and it was only half right, so here is the sharpened diagnosis with the evidence, because the next worker should not re-derive it.

WHAT I CONFIRMED
A marked name is resolved and written back on TWO independent evaluator paths, not one, and my earlier note named only the first.

1. jet-comptime's dispatcher. Its write_back matched Expr::Ident and Expr::Field but not Expr::ComptimeName, so a marked receiver never advanced. Fixed in d22b848d1: the arm now reads Expr::Ident(name, _) | Expr::ComptimeName { name, .. }, which is what D-META-STAGE1=B means by the mark being part of the identifier.

2. The TIR evaluator in jet-codegen, reached through Comptime::TirBridge. This is the one that actually folds the failing fixture: read_u8 is implemented in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/handles.rs and nowhere in jet-comptime (a repository search for "read_u8" returns jet-sema's signature table, the TIR subset gate, and jet-foundation's StreamCursor — no comptime arm). A search for ComptimeName under crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/ returns nothing, so that evaluator has no marked-name concept at all and resolves marked names by some other route without write-back.

So the remaining work is to give the TIR evaluator the same treatment: a marked name resolves and writes back as an ordinary name whose identifier includes the mark. Until both paths agree, criterion 1's second clause and criterion 6 cannot be claimed.

REPRODUCER, small and self-contained
fn run() {
    $ct :: Reader.over([U8].{7, 9, 11})
    $ct_a :: $ct.read_u8() ?? panic("ct a")
    $ct_b :: $ct.read_u8() ?? panic("ct b")
    rt :: Reader.over([U8].{7, 9, 11})
    rt_a :: rt.read_u8() ?? panic("rt a")
    rt_b :: rt.read_u8() ?? panic("rt b")
    print("{$ct_a}|{$ct_b}|{rt_a}|{rt_b}")
}
Prints 7|7|7|9. It must print 7|9|7|9. The marked reader does not advance; the plain one does.

The other two failures are the same root cause seen from different sides: comptime_loadable_matches_runtime types a module-level marked name from the folded value rather than its binding, so Loadable.Idle loses its methods; reusable_regex reports E0956 on replace_all_with. cards.title: One registration table: marker, plane, right and fact
cards.body: Four registries were proposed in one week for one job. This card builds one declaration kind in the Prelude with a target kind, so a marker rule, a knowledge plane, a right and a build fact are rows of the same table separated only by what they attach to. The declaring word is marker for rules, and a rule carries its own facts as named parameters marked with $, so $sites: [.Function, .Method] describes the rule while ordinary parameters are what a user writes. Reflection, jet inspect and the drift guards are written once and serve all four. D-FACT-LAW1=B adds the law to the table itself: every row states which way is safe and which written words move it the other way, and a drift guard fails a row that states neither. D-FACT-OWN1=A adds one row kind for facts a prover publishes, such as sendability and view provenance, which register without any plane algebra.
cards.plan: Implements D-META-REG1, D-META-NAME1, D-META-FORM1 — ratified 2026-08-06. Read each decision verbatim (tower brief on this card's parent proposal, or tower decision show) before building; the ratified outcome text is the law, this plan is the route. Every requirement is a discrete exit criterion below: meet each with targeted proof (tests, snapshots, examples with golden output), and keep I9 tier parity inside this card — AOT, default jet run (JIT), and the interpreter must agree on every surface this card ships before it closes. Delete every superseded form the decisions retire in the same change; do not leave compatibility shims or parallel spellings. Reference: docs/proposals/metaprogramming-one-compile-time-program.md.

cards.title: Users may declare rules that record facts or add code
cards.body: A user declares a rule with a signature and legal sites, exactly like a compiler rule. A rule with no body records a fact. A rule with a body adds code. This is the same power the compiler has, so #Codable and #Inline stop being special cases. Law 1 still holds: a rule adds items and facts and can never change or shadow what the user wrote, and that is checked rather than trusted.

cards.title: Derive bodies are real code with holes
cards.body:
A derive body contains Jet members, not a string. The header already names the trait and the type, so no inner impl is written, and the parser checks the body when it is written rather than after re-lexing emitted text. Splices are typed holes filled at expansion, and compile-time control flow inside the body generates one member per field when a derive needs that. b.generate takes the same block of items, so the build entry needs no separate form.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): This card builds the provider-definition meaning of `derive`, which every option on ballot D-ONCE-DERIVE1 (card #1656) preserves — proceed. Keep the definition meaning strictly separate from the request meaning in the parser, examples, and spec text, so the ballot's outcome on the request spelling lands without touching this work.

cards.title: A library may declare a checked text block
cards.body: A library may declare a block rule, the way the standard library adds SQL. Jet reads the block boundary with its own grammar and hands the inside to the library as text; the library checks it and adds code. Jet's grammar never moves, because the braces are always Jet's braces, so no library can change how anything outside the block parses.

cards.title: A compile-time value is legal anywhere a constant is legal
cards.body: An array length or an enum number may be any expression the compiler can compute, not just a literal or a bare name. Both sites call the evaluator that already exists. The rules that follow are unchanged: the value must be known and it must be an integer. Only the shape of what a person may type changes, and S26 is untouched because the value stays a value and never selects a type.

cards.title: Everything derivable is derived unless refused
cards.body:
If the compiler can derive a trait from a type's shape, it does. The default set widens from four traits to every structurally derivable trait, Codable included, so json.encode(u) works with nothing asked for. A type refuses one trait with the exclamation mark it already uses and a project refuses one everywhere through a declared setting. Traits that cannot be derived structurally stay opt-in because there is nothing to derive, and the existing eligibility gates still apply silently.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): The refusal spelling in the criteria is settled and unaffected. The spelling a type uses to *request* a derived capability is on ballot D-ONCE-DERIVE1 (card #1656) — marker form versus the body line. Nothing in this card should introduce or document a request spelling; the opt-in traits it leaves behind adopt whichever the ballot ratifies.

cards.title: Type foundation: one knowledge vector on Type
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1538. Ten kinds of compile-time fact live in ten private mechanisms in the checker. Give Type one knowledge vector and one registry instead. This is the first card of the type-system-v2 slate; every other D-TYPE2 card lands on top of it.

Add drift guards that walk every registered plane end to end, the same pattern the marker rebuild uses on cards #1457, #1458 and #1460. Under D-FACT-READ1=A the per-fact read is the $ mark, built on card #1623; reflect() stays as the aggregate view over the same typed facts, and the two never diverge.

cards.title: Inline value ranges in any type position
cards.body: A value range should not require minting a named type first. Make Int(0..100) legal wherever a type is written: parameters, returns, fields and bindings. Literals check at compile time and unproven values convert fallibly, exactly as U8 works today. The inline form is structural, so two inline types with the same base and the same range are the same type, while distinct stays the nominal wrapper for when identity matters. This only removes the requirement to pre-declare a name; the checking rules are the ones already ratified.

cards.title: The number grid: sized widths become Int plus a range, and BigInt retires
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1547. Every number type becomes one cell of a two-axis grid: the value world (whole, ratio, real, complex) and the knowledge grade (exact unbounded, exact bounded, approximate, measured). A sized width such as U8 becomes Int plus a proven range and a one-byte layout, with its spelling and behavior unchanged. BigInt retires, because the arbitrary-precision Int holds every value it held, and the four errors that police mixing Int with BigInt retire with it. The ratified widening law, value-set containment, becomes the theorem that a subset needs no conversion, and one interval prover replaces the width table, the range checks and the fixed-list index proof. This reshapes a name other open cards use, so it runs before them.

cards.title: Exact by default: decimal literals, exact division, approximation opted in
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1571. Ordinary numbers become exact. A decimal literal is an exact Decimal, so price * 3 gives 59.97 exactly and 0.1 + 0.2 equals 0.3. Division of exact values lands in exact rational territory: a result with a finite decimal prints as a decimal, otherwise it prints as a fraction and stays exact, so 1 / 3 prints 1/3 and third * 3 equals 1. Functions that truly leave the rationals, such as square root and sine, answer approximate and say so. Experts opt into Float or F32 at the declaration and hot code keeps today's machine arithmetic. Exact values use machine-word fast paths with spill, the same playbook as the bigint Int.

cards.title: Time joins the unit plane: one Time family, one literal system
cards.body: Durations and instants become ordinary unit-plane quantities. Duration is the delta quantity of a canonical Time unit family stored as a 64-bit nanosecond count, per the ratified resolution decision, and Instant is the matching point quantity, reusing the affine machinery temperatures already use. Every 500ms resolves through the one unit plane, in user code, timeouts and schedules alike, and both hidden suffix tables are deleted. Because time is on the plane, it joins unit algebra: 12meter / 2s is a speed.

cards.title: One measure substrate for list lengths, matrix shapes, lanes and exponents
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1547. Four private encodings hold compile-time numbers in types today: list lengths, matrix shapes, vector lanes and dimension exponents. Make them one thing. A measure is a compile-time number attached to a type through the plane registry, and each use declares its own combination rule: joining two lists adds lengths, matrix multiply matches inner sides and composes outer sides, multiplying quantities adds exponents. Surfaces do not change; the encodings underneath become one. Measures are declared literals or module value parameters and are never computed by user code, so the ratified wall that compile-time evaluation cannot create types still stands. Symbolic lengths from generic modules resolve at specialization exactly as today, without the placeholder-zero sentinel.

cards.title: The one law on the knowledge planes, and its sema gate
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1571 and #1624. Write the conservation law into the spec and give it teeth: knowledge grows silently, is lost only at a spelled step, and erases at runtime. The two existing spellings stay, because each names its own operation well. approx marks accepting a representation's precision, and rounded conversions name a mode because rounding direction matters there. Add the sema check the law needs, so any operation that discards range, exactness, unit, state or classification must require a spelled step. The law then binds every future surface without a new ballot.

cards.title: Measured values: the uncertainty knowledge grade
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1547. Measurement becomes the measured grade of numeric knowledge. Arithmetic and the math functions propagate uncertainty by the standard first-order rules, and exact values are zero-uncertainty, so mixing them needs no ceremony. Nothing changes for any program until a measurement enters it. Printing shows the value with its uncertainty. Propagation uses first-order linear approximation with uncorrelated inputs, and the docs must say so plainly; correlated errors are out of scope. Measured unit scales produce measured conversion results, which connects the two places uncertainty already lives.

cards.title: Dropping a bound task handle is a compile error
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1571 and #1624. The join duty becomes the same rule every single-use value follows. Binding a task handle and then never using it fails to compile, and the fix text names the three exits: join it, use its result, or call detach for fire-and-forget. Work is then never lost silently and the choice is always visible on the page. This extends D-LIN1 to Task<T> and to the list forms from D-VERDICT-1323-1, and handles are discharged by all, race and any at those calls. It amends the L1101 behavior in the task section of the spec.

cards.title: A stream is a task: one cancellation and cleanup law
cards.body:
Streams and tasks have two separately written shutdown laws, and the copies drifted. Delete the second one. A stream producer is a scheduler child: dropping the iterator cancels it, and it unwinds at its next wait point running its cleanups, exactly as any cancelled task does. yield is a wait point and drop-close is a cancel. The generator decision's separate shutdown wording is replaced by a reference to the task law, so the drift class dies by construction. Tier parity follows because all tiers already share the task cancel path.

cards.title: One gate ledger for every step off the safe path
cards.body:
Every written word that moves a fact away from safety is a gate: #Unsafe, #Impure, a dependency grant, a trust grant, .Force, a taint scrub, detach or .drop with a reason, approx and wrapping. Today each family is recorded somewhere different, so nobody can read the whole picture. Give every gate kind one ledger and one reader, jet inspect gates. Sources stay where they are: source markers, the lockfile and the trust store. The ledger is the merged read model that keeps provenance, so this adds no new write surface, and no gate gains new ceremony. The existing per-kind views keep working as filters.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): The ledger half of this card is ratified law (D-FACT-GATE1) and should be built. The ladder half is not: ballot D-ONCE-GATE1 (card #1656) decides whether `#Unsafe`, `#Impure`, and `#Nondeterministic` share one org-policy ladder and whether `--allow-impure` retires. Build the one ledger and its reader now; add the policy ladder in whatever shape that ballot ratifies, and do not mint a second impure-policy surface in the meantime.

cards.title: Retire the word capability from every user-facing surface
cards.body: Substrate first: blocked by #1501. The word capability means four different things across Jet's surfaces, so it means nothing. Take it off every surface a user reads. Borrow diagnostics say write access instead. The carried rights value takes the name Authority. The product claim manifest becomes feature claims. Docs may still say capability-based when describing the design tradition, but no user-facing message, name or identifier uses the bare word. No grammar changes; the diagnostic copy is snapshot-tested product text, so those snapshots are re-blessed in the same change. This reshapes wording that other open cards quote, including #1499 and #1501, so it runs before them.

cards.title: Prelude policy and the ratified prelude additions
cards.body: Write down what needs no import and then add exactly what the policy allows. The seven criteria become law: measured frequency, total and safe, names that never carry semantics, no better home, first-hour coverage, one fixed set, and collision-conscious names. Shadowing lets the user win with a compiler warning, and new names land only at epoch boundaries with a migration lint. Then ship the ratified additions: eprint, input, assert, assert_eq with a structural diff, the type names Clock, Instant, Date, Duration and Path, the blessed doors Clock.now() and Date.today(), and the file trio read_file, write_file and file_exists as re-exports of the file-system functions carrying the file-system effect. Random stays behind one import in core.math.random. Every entry is total or returns a result, and no implicit conversion ever enters the prelude. This reshapes the ambient name set every other card writes against, so it runs early.

cards.title: Eager collection helpers with a .lazy opt-in
cards.body:
Helpers on a real list, map or set run at once and return a plain collection, so nothing re-runs invisibly and results are inspectable in a debugger. Writing .lazy first gives the same vocabulary as a deferred view, for large or infinite work. Sources that are already streams, such as file lines, streams and channels, keep returning the deferred view because they arrive over time. The optimizer may fuse adjacent eager adapters when the intermediate is unobservable. This amends the lazy default of D-ITERTOOLS1 and touches the open Iter work on #1479.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): The eager/lazy split is independent of naming and can proceed. The verbs on the collection surface this card touches are on ballot D-ONCE-VERB1 (card #1656), which adopts one verb per job across List, Map, and Set. Do not settle a collection verb spelling inside this change; migrate any renamed verb through the retirement mechanism when the ballot lands.

cards.title: Adopt the extended Core API doctrine
cards.body:
The Core API rules stop at L8 today. Extend them with the Part A rules from docs/proposals/corelib-overhaul.md, which is the authoritative list for this card, and make them law in docs/spec/stdlib-api-laws.md: call site C1 to C3, defaults and options D1 to D4, failure F1 to F3, types T1 to T3, naming N1 to N2, layering L-A to L-D, evolution E1 to E2. Every new or changed Core API passes them in review, the same way L1 to L8 work today, and call sites are judged by reading them aloud. Options are enums, not booleans. cards.title: Benchmark agent codegen quality on Jet (strict-typing hypothesis)
cards.body: Video-mining evidence (Elm retrospective, 2026-08-06): untested hypothesis that rigid typed languages yield better AI-generated code; an experienced commenter counters that typed declarative architectures mostly reduce how much codegen is needed. Jet bets on typed diagnostics helping agents but has no measurement. Run an internal benchmark: agent codegen success rate on Jet example tasks vs a control language, measuring compile-first-try, diagnostic-guided repair rounds, and semantic correctness. Internal instrumentation only; no product claim before data.

2. Run the harness with an agent generating code for each task in Jet and in the control language, capturing raw pass/fail, repair-round counts, and diagnostic text seen.
3. Write results to docs/research/agent-codegen-benchmark-<date>.md with the raw data table alongside the summary. Internal instrumentation only: no product or marketing claim is adopted without citing this measurement.

cards.title: scope.guard is dropped: the cleanup closure never runs
cards.body: A scope.guard binding lowers to a bare unit, so its cleanup never runs. Generated Rust for examples/features/errors/must_use.jet shows 'let user__g: _ = ();' where the jet_scope_guard call should be. Reproduces at 9f2f9f2a1, before any carrier work, so it is not a regression from card #1527. Two golden examples fail on it: errors/must_use and io/scope_guard.
cards.plan:
Root cause confirmed by instrumenting and dumping generated Rust for examples/features/errors/must_use.jet (reverted after diagnosis — no debug code left in tree): the D-VERDICT-1308-1 implicit immutable-binding const-fold (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/bindings.rs:687, `evaluate_owned_with_imports_opts_collecting`) tries to comptime-evaluate every `::` binding's initializer, including `scope.guard(() => {...})`. That call routes through `Comptime::TirBridge::eval_expr` (crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/TirBridge.rs:99) into jet-codegen's TIR-eval interpreter (installed by `install_comptime_bridge`, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs:2169), which lowers the AST call to TIR and evaluates `TExprKind::CoreClosureCall { kind: TCoreClosureKind::Guard { executable, .. } }` at crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/exprs.rs:5094-5099. That handler pushes the guard's executable lambda onto `self.scope_guards` — correct for real program execution, where a block's guard_mark/drain machinery (eval/mod.rs:1488-1508) runs cleanup LIFO at scope exit — and returns `Ok(CtValue::Unit)` as a placeholder, since ScopeGuard has no literal CtValue form.

That placeholder is harmless during real execution (the guard is tracked procedurally). It is wrong when the same evaluator is reused, one-shot, purely to PROBE whether a binding can fold: there is no owning scope to drain `self.scope_guards` from, so the registered executable is discarded and the caller only sees `Ok(CtValue::Unit)`.

The actual defect is in the fold-acceptance gate: `ct_value_fits_binding` (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/bindings.rs:169-189) has no arm rejecting a `CtValue::Unit` result against a non-Unit declared type; its catch-all `_ => true` (line 187) wrongly accepts the placeholder as 'fits' a ScopeGuard-typed binding. So `b.ct = Some(CtValue::Unit)` gets recorded, and codegen serializes the folded literal `()` instead of emitting the real `jet_scope_guard(closure)` call (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/expressions.rs ~4959-4961 — confirmed correct in isolation, never reached because the fold wins first). The guard is never constructed, so its Drop (JetScopeGuard in Prelude/Core/RuntimeControl.rs) never runs, so cleanup never fires. Confirmed empirically: generated Rust for must_use.jet is exactly `let user__g: _ = ();` (the `_` type annotation is intentional/correct per D-DEFER1 — ScopeGuard is generic over its closure type; only the RHS is wrong).

Because this is a shared sema fact (I3: all checking lives in sema), the wrong fold propagates to every downstream tier that consumes `b.ct`/TIR alike — AOT rustc emit, the Cranelift JIT (`jet run`/`jet dev`), and interpreter deopt all inherit the same wrong literal. Fix once at the shared gate, then prove the guard fires on all three (I9).

Fix location (root cause, one shared gate, not a per-call-site patch): add a match arm in `ct_value_fits_binding` (bindings.rs, before the `_ => true` catch-all at line 187) rejecting `(CtValue::Unit, ty)` unless `ty` is itself `Type::Named("Unit")` — a folded Unit only fits a Unit-typed binding. This leaves the interpreter's real-execution semantics untouched (they are already correct) and needs no parallel 'closure-taking core call' exclusion list in bindings.rs.

Related discovery, not required for this card but worth a grep before closing: `TCoreClosureKind::OnCommit`/`OnRollback` (eval/exprs.rs:5100-5117) have the identical push-then-`Ok(CtValue::Unit)` shape. If any live example binds a transaction hook with `::` (immutable) instead of `:=`, it would have the same latent bug — confirm none does, or file a follow-up card.

log.text: Closed: root-cause fix proved on merged master across tiers.

prep: authored plan + 6 criteria. Root cause confirmed via direct instrumentation (temporary debug prints in bindings.rs + generated-Rust dump via jet::compile_with_path, both reverted before finishing — tree clean). scope.guard's TIR-eval Guard handler (eval/exprs.rs:5094-5099) returns Ok(CtValue::Unit) as a placeholder, correct for real execution (scope_guards drain-and-run at scope exit) but wrongly accepted by ct_value_fits_binding's catch-all (bindings.rs:187) when the D-VERDICT-1308-1 implicit fold probes this same evaluator with no owning scope. Fix: one new arm in ct_value_fits_binding rejecting Unit against a non-Unit declared type — the single shared gate every tier's fold decision routes through (I3/I9).

cards.title: core.tls ciphersuites/tlsversion: native TLS-bridge extension
cards.body: D-CORESURF-SMALL1 (ratified) explicitly defers 2 of core.tls's ledger rows — ciphersuites and tlsversion (the negotiated values, not the with_version_bounds request) — as real gaps needing a native TLS-bridge change, out of scope for that ballot. cards.plan:
Extend the native TLS bridge so TLSPeerIdentity exposes the negotiated cipher suite and protocol version. D-CORESURF-SMALL1 (ratified) names both as real gaps deferred to this card. No new syntax, no new dependency, no ballot needed.

Surface: stream.peer_identity().cipher_suite -> String (for example TLS13_AES_128_GCM_SHA256); stream.peer_identity().tls_version -> TLSVersion (the existing enum: .Tls12 / .Tls13).

Steps:
1. crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/NetTls.rs: widen JetTLSPeerSnapshot from 8 to 10 elements, appending the cipher suite name (String) and the negotiated version (i64, the same coding with_version_bounds already uses). In jet_net_tls_peer_identity_impl read conn.negotiated_cipher_suite() and conn.protocol_version(); both are present after a finished handshake; map an absent value to an Err exactly like the existing missing-chain case.
2. crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/NetHTTP.rs: update the mirrored JetTLSPeerSnapshot alias and jet_net_tls_peer_identity_from_snapshot so JetTLSPeerIdentity carries the two new fields. The tuple widening makes the compiler flag every remaining construction and destructuring site; fix each one. All tiers share this one Prelude path (I9); no engine re-encodes anything.
3. crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_types.rs: in core_struct_field add cipher_suite -> String and tls_version -> Named TLSVersion to the TLSPeerIdentity arm.
4. Docs: extend the stream.peer_identity() row in docs/reference/core-library.md and rewrite the ledger-declined note in the core.tls section so ciphersuites and tlsversion are shipped, not gaps. In docs/reference/core-surface-ledger.json give gap.network.ciphersuites and gap.network.tlsversion the shipped jetSpelling and a winning verdict, copying the shape of an already-resolved gap row.
5. Proof: extend core_tls_expert_config_peer_identity_and_directional_close_are_real in tests/corelib.rs. Pin .Tls13 version bounds in the fixture, print both new fields, assert tls_version is Tls13 and cipher_suite starts with TLS13_ (the exact suite can vary with rustls defaults, so assert the prefix). Add the same two prints to the localhost TLS harness in tests/dev.rs to prove the default jet run tier returns the same values through the same Prelude symbol.

cards.title: release_gates.rs pre-existing failures: canon.jet E0999 marker brackets, E0328 explain gap
cards.body:
Found while proving CI test-shard coverage for #211 (2026-08-06, commit
b0ad4e932): tests/release_gates.rs has 2 pre-existing failures unrelated to
CI sharding, on unmodified master HEAD (cargo test -p jet --test
release_gates):

1) canon_compiles_and_runs: examples/canon.jet:121 uses `#[Doc("port to
   listen on")] port: Int = 3000` — bracketed single-marker form, rejected by
   the ratified E0999 single-marker-bracket rule ("one marker stays bare,
   brackets group two or more"). Card #1331 (done) fixed this same pattern
   for semindex dossier fixtures; examples/canon.jet was apparently missed,
   or regressed after #1331 closed. Fix: `#Doc("port to listen on") port:
   Int = 3000`.

2) ga_every_diagnostic_has_explain: the M17 GA gate scans docs/spec/
   diagnostics.md for codes lacking a `jet explain` entry and flags E0328.
   diagnostics.md:301 marks E0328 `~~retired by D-IFDIST1=A~~` (strikethrough)
   — either the scan should skip retired codes and doesn't, or a retired
   code legitimately needs to stay explainable for old error logs and its
   explain entry was dropped. Needs a decision, not a blind fix.

Repro: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet --test release_gates
cards.plan:
Two independent fixes. No owner decision is needed; both follow existing law and precedent.

Fix 1 - canon.jet marker brackets. examples/canon.jet:121 spells #[Doc("port to listen on")] around one marker. The ratified E0999 rule says one marker stays bare; brackets group two or more. Change it to #Doc("port to listen on"). This is the same fix #1331 applied to the semindex fixtures.

Fix 2 - the E0328 explain-gate failure is a Markdown escaping bug, not a policy question. Explain::index() in crates/jet-cli/src/Explain.rs keeps only registry rows that split into exactly 3 cells, and split_cells already honors \| escapes. The E0328 row (docs/spec/diagnostics.md:301) contains raw pipes inside backticks, so it splits into more than 3 cells, the row is dropped, and E0328 never enters the explain index. Every other retired code stays in the index and passes the gate, so retired codes staying explainable is the established behavior (I4, old error logs). Fix: escape the in-cell pipes in that one row as \|. Do not change the gate scan or Explain.rs.

Proof: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet --test release_gates goes green; jet explain E0328 prints the retired notice; a grep shows no other registry row with an unescaped in-cell pipe.

A separate pre-existing divergence found on the way is card #1607: json/toml/yaml parse errors word differently on the two tiers because each tier runs its own parser.

The Reader/Cursor blocker on #1602 is implemented on branch bd3/reader (worktree .claude/worktrees/reader), commit 382de4645, and left unmerged. release_gates now runs 15 of 16 green; canon_compiles_and_runs still fails, but only on a third pre-existing gap that the Reader/Cursor fix uncovered: 'jet run' rejects json.decode_traced at examples/canon.jet:161 with E0956. That is card #1605. Under 'jet run --release' examples/canon.jet now matches tests/fixtures/canon/expected.out byte for byte, after one stale fixture line ('fanout: 3 6 9', left behind when dffe457b8 removed the S75 fan-out operator) was deleted on the same branch.

Fixed both diagnosed defects: examples/canon.jet's bracketed #[Doc(...)] moved to bare #Doc(...) per E0999 (criterion #1's marker-fix half); docs/spec/diagnostics.md:301 E0328 row's in-cell pipes escaped as \| so ga_every_diagnostic_has_explain passes (criteria #2-4 met). Fixing the marker bracket let canon_compiles_and_runs proceed further and hit a THIRD, previously-masked pre-existing failure: examples/canon.jet:130 Reader.over(packet) fails E0956 under quick-run (default jet run) — the shared ambient evaluator has ALL Reader/Cursor handle ops stubbed unsupported (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/handles.rs:856-874), not a narrow gap. Also found and fixed 3 more masked failures in the same file: edition_too_new, no_edition_field_is_accepted, supported_edition_is_accepted all built their test manifests with the retired payload:{...} wrapper (D-CONF-NAME1 retired it) — moved to bare name:/version:/edition:, all 3 now pass. Leaving criteria #1 and #5 open pending #1602.

cards.title: canon.jet: Reader/Cursor handle ops unsupported in quick-run (jet run)
cards.body: Found while closing #1597 (release_gates.rs test-health). Fixing that card's original 2 bugs (E0999 marker brackets in canon.jet, E0328 explain-gate escaping) let canon_compiles_and_runs proceed further and hit a THIRD, previously-masked pre-existing failure: 'jet run examples/canon.jet' (the default quick-run/JIT tier) fails with E0956 'handle ReaderOver isn't supported in Jet's quick-run mode yet' at examples/canon.jet:130, Reader.over(packet). This is not a narrow gap: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/handles.rs stubs ALL Reader/Cursor handle ops as unsupported() in the shared deopt/interpreter ambient evaluator — ReaderOver, ReaderReadU8, ReaderReadU16Le/Be, ReaderReadU32Le/Be, ReaderReadU64Le/Be, ReaderTake, ReaderRemaining, ReaderAtEnd, CursorOver, CursorTakeUntil, CursorSkipWs, CursorTakePattern, ReaderTakePattern (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/handles.rs:856-874). canon.jet is the flagship canonical example (I5: every feature ships an example proving the same meaning on every applicable execution tier) and its stream-parsing section (D-SHIFT1, 'the shift kernel for linear stream parsing') currently only works under AOT/full build, not the default jet run tier — an I9 gap. This is substantial implementation work (wiring a stateful byte-cursor value into the shared CtValue-based ambient evaluator, endian-aware decoding, D-PARSESTR1 pattern-match integration for CursorTakePattern/ReaderTakePattern), not a test-fixture fix, so it was left out of #1597's scope. cards.title: json.decode_traced / typed codec decode unsupported in quick-run (jet run)
cards.body: Found while closing #1602 (Reader/Cursor in quick-run). With the Reader/Cursor gap fixed, 'jet run examples/canon.jet' now reaches line 161 and fails with E0956: core.encoding.json.decode_traced() is not supported in the canonical TIR evaluator. The same gap covers typed decode<T> and decode_traced<T> for json/toml/yaml/csv: the AST comptime interpreter supports them (Comptime/Methods/dispatch/eval_method.rs routes to TypedDecode::eval_typed_decode using the call's type arguments), but TExprKind::CoreCall in the TIR evaluator carries no type arguments, so apply_core_call falls through to the 'not whitelisted' arm. The evaluator already owns the pieces: eval_datatree_decode walks a DataTree into a typed value, and apply_codec_migration replays the D-MIGRATE3 plan. What is missing is the CoreCall arm that recovers the target type from the call's resolved return type (Result<T, [FieldError]> for decode, Result<DecodeResult<T>, [FieldError]> for decode_traced), plus the DecodeResult { value, migration } shape and its migrated flag. AOT is correct today. This is the last blocker for release_gates::canon_compiles_and_runs and therefore for #1597.

R2: the D-MIGRATE4 version vocabulary was written twice — Codegen/Items.rs baked 'v{i}->v{i+1}' into the generated chain-walker while the evaluator rebuilt the same strings. Both now call Codegen/TIR/mod.rs::migration_shape_name and ::migration_step_name. Not run: the full suite, per the scoped-proof rule.

Implemented on branch bd3/reader (worktree .claude/worktrees/reader), commit 54fef177c, on top of the Reader/Cursor work for #1602. Approach: the CoreCall arm recovers the target type from the call's resolved return type, parses with the codec's own parser through apply_core_call's existing parse arm, and decodes by running the type's generated Decode TIR — the same body AOT compiles — so the evaluator adds marshalling only. apply_codec_migration now reports the MigrationStatus of the walk, and that status is an out-param only the top-level call reads, so nested fields cannot leak into a parent's status. cards.title: Marker retention for block-construct statements and expressions, and the last lexer marker names
cards.body:
Card #1456 finished the parse-path unification and the flag-shaped retention: one shared reader reads every hash-name marker, Binding keeps markers: Vec<Marker> with no derived booleans, and the two statement switch attributes share one Stmt::Switched node that carries its marker. What that pass deliberately did not change, and what this card carries:

1. Block-construct statements (#Unsafe, #Impure, #Context, #Caps, #Grant, #Transact, #Region, #Policy, #Live, #Nondeterministic, #Reactive, #Shield) keep dedicated Stmt variants. Their fields are the marker's own arguments, so the node is the construct rather than a flag derived from a marker. The same holds for #Todo, #Tainted and the open tag-prefix operator in expression position. Whether D-VERDICT-1455-1 also wants a retained Marker node on these is a design question for the owner, not a mechanical change: adding one beside the parsed arguments duplicates the same fact in two places.
2. Two marker-name references remain in the lexer, both automatic-semicolon rules rather than marker parsing: jet-lexer Scan.rs (FFI) and Terminators.rs (UnitFamily). The #1456 plan's sweep asks for all lexer marker-name knowledge to go.
3. The same plan's other sweep items are also open: the marker_sequence_leads_to_function lookahead heuristic and the function_marker_has_applicator name list, which is a shadow site table beside the registry.
cards.plan: Ballot D-MARK-BLOCK1 is ratified as option A: block-construct nodes keep their typed fields and no second marker record is stored, so nothing about the tree shape changes. The one build item from A is a registry-derived accessor that maps any block-construct node to its Policy::APPLIED_RULES row plus argument values; put it beside the existing row helper in crates/jet-foundation/src/Registry.rs (marker_row, line 133) and make the formatter and any reflection walk call it instead of matching each Stmt variant. The rest of the card is the mechanical sweep D-MARK-REG1 already demands. Remove the marker names from the lexer at crates/jet-lexer/src/Lexer/Scan.rs:59 (MARKER_FFI) and crates/jet-lexer/src/Lexer/Terminators.rs:42 (MARKER_UNIT_FAMILY) by driving both automatic-semicolon rules from the registry row instead of a name literal. Make marker_sequence_leads_to_function read the registry (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/marker_groups.rs:733, called from imports_policy.rs:436, :666, :777), and delete function_marker_has_applicator (same file, line 1271) so applicator knowledge lives only on the row that crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/mod.rs:948 already reads. Delete each replaced name list in the same change; no shadow table survives. Prove it red-then-green with scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet-parser --lib plus the targeted parser, formatter and snapshot tests, and run the D-MARK-REG1 name-literal scan over crates/jet-lexer and crates/jet-parser. No Core semantics change here, so I9 is unaffected: the parse tree is the same for every tier.

cards.title: json.parse reports different parse-error wording in quick-run than AOT
cards.body:
Found while closing #1605 (typed decode in quick-run). The two tiers run different JSON parsers, so a malformed document produces different text. Repro: a file with 'if json.parse("{oops") == { .Ok(v) -> print("ok") .Err(e) -> print("parse err: {e.message}") }'. Under 'jet run' it prints 'expected object key'; under 'jet run --release' it prints 'expected quoted text'. AOT parses with jet_std::parse_json in the emitted prelude; quick-run parses with Comptime/JSONInterp.rs::parse_json, reached through apply_core_call. Both walk their own error vocabulary. The same divergence reaches typed decode: json.decode of a malformed document reports the parse failure through the same message. Error text is snapshot-tested product copy, so one parser has to own it. Independent of #1605, whose targeted test avoids the parse-failure path for exactly this reason and covers decode-body errors instead, which do agree.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): The third criterion pins shared wording across two JSON parsers, which keeps the second copy alive and only tests that it agrees today — the same shape as the four hand-written statistics kernels and the two schedulers. The corpus law's one-source rule says delete the second parser: one implementation in the Prelude, engines marshalling onto it, and a guard that fails if a second parser appears. Restate the fix that way before implementing.
cards.plan: I9 says one home for this behavior: the parse-error wording is product copy, and today two parsers own it per format. AOT parses JSON with jet_std parse_json in the emitted prelude; quick-run parses with crates/jet-comptime Comptime/JSONInterp.rs parse_json via apply_core_call. TOML and YAML have the same split (jet_std toml/yaml parse_to_tree versus Comptime/EncodingLite.rs). Fix the family together. Approach: move each text parser (or at minimum its complete error-message vocabulary) into a shared embedded-Prelude part that jet-comptime may reach — that means jet-foundation, since comptime may depend only on jet-foundation (I6). Codegen keeps embedding the same part; comptime calls the same function. Do NOT hand-copy strings between the two parsers: a synced copy is the drift I9 forbids. Order: (1) repro both wordings with the brief fixture under jet run and jet run --release; (2) relocate the JSON parser first, prove criteria 1-3; (3) repeat for TOML and YAML; (4) add one targeted test that feeds the same malformed document to both tiers per format and asserts identical text, including the json.decode FieldError path. cards.title: Interpreter tier silently skips view-range bounds check (I9 gap)
cards.body:
Found while closing #1601 (diagnostic_snapshots drift). tests/ui/view_mut_bounds_interpreter.jet ('// @dev_interpreter', values := [1]; outside :: [&values[0..0], &values[2..2]]) expects E0953 ('can't view 1 items from 2 to 2 (inclusive)') under the forced interpreter tier (dev_iteration(path, false, true)) — this is a genuine out-of-bounds view (values has 1 element, index 2 is out of range). Confirmed default jet run (AOT/JIT) still correctly panics with this exact message (verified via probe). The forced interpreter path now returns RunOutcome::Ran with no error at all — it silently accepts the out-of-bounds view instead of rejecting it. Checked crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/{mod.rs,builtins.rs}: both view_bounds_diagnostic (mod.rs:211) and TBuiltinOp::ViewNew (builtins.rs:451-472) appear to implement the same bounds check the AOT Prelude uses (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.rs jet_view_new) — the exact interpreter code path that's skipping the check for THIS expression shape (a list literal of two view sub-expressions) wasn't pinned down; did not chase further given time budget. This is a safety-relevant I9 tier-parity gap (I1: memory-safe by default — an unchecked view bound is a wild read), not a text drift, so #1601 did NOT re-bless this fixture to '(no errors)' — it stays red pending this investigation.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): Fix the skipped bounds check regardless of the ballot: silently omitting a safety check is a defect under every option. What ballot D-ONCE-TIER1 (card #1656) settles is how much of AOT's behavior the interpreter tier must match in general — I9's blanket parity versus D-VERDICT-1254-1's lower-concern carve-out. Frame the fix as restoring the safety check, not as a general parity claim for the tier.
cards.plan: Safety-relevant tier-parity gap: the forced interpreter accepts an out-of-bounds view that AOT correctly rejects with E0953. The bounds check exists in both crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs (view_bounds_diagnostic, line ~211) and eval/builtins.rs (TBuiltinOp::ViewNew, ~451-472), so the bug is a routing gap: the failing shape is a list literal whose elements are view sub-expressions (&values[0..0], &values[2..2]). Steps: (1) rebuild jet, repro with dev_iteration(path, false, true) on tests/ui/view_mut_bounds_interpreter.jet; (2) trace how the interpreter evaluates view sub-expressions inside a list literal — find the code path that constructs the view without going through ViewNew or view_bounds_diagnostic (likely an aggregate or alias evaluation path); (3) fix by routing that path through the same bounds semantics the Prelude jet_view_new (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.rs) defines — do not add a second check with its own wording; (4) restore tests/ui/view_mut_bounds_interpreter.stderr to its original E0953 expectation and prove cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots green. Criteria already carry the acceptance; the reviewer must confirm the fix is in the shared path, not a shape-special-case.

cards.title: tir_unsafe_and_runtime: 3 remaining failures (qualified-name cascade, Clone bound, D-FLOWTYPE1 else-branch narrowing)
cards.body: Found while closing #1600. Two separate remaining tir_unsafe_and_runtime.rs failures, deeper than originally scoped: (1) foreign_struct_construction (E0113: fn make() => Note declared but note.Note.{...} construction infers Type::Named("note.Note") — check_struct_lit's import_ns qualification (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs check_struct_lit, nominal_name = import_ns.map(|alias| format!("{alias}.{type_name}"))) disambiguates same-named structs across modules but breaks THREE downstream consumers that expect bare registry-keyed names: field_type (fixed in #1600, splits qualified names back apart before struct_owner_module lookup), return-type assignability (E0113, still broken — check_type_assignable doesn't know alias.Type equals Type), and TIR subset coverage (is_covered_struct_ty/tir_covers in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/subset/entry.rs also expects bare names — using note.Note as a DECLARED return type annotation to dodge E0113 makes tir_covers wrongly return false, producing an ICE 'codegen reached a construct the typed IR does not cover (make)' since the AST-fallback path is retired). Root cause needs one fix, not three patches: either make check_type_assignable/is_covered_struct_ty also split-and-compare qualified names (matching the field_type fix's approach), or reconsider whether check_struct_lit should qualify the nominal name at all for the common case. Left the fixture at its ORIGINAL bare  return type (still red, E0113) to avoid shipping the ICE regression. (2) generic_struct_fns (E0277 rustc rejection): after fixing the real ownership-sigil bug (D-MEM1 struct-literal field fill/rebind from a read-only param needs ~a/~b/~s, not bare — this part IS fixed and committed), a new codegen gap surfaced: struct Stack<T> { items: [T] } derives a Rust  bound on the struct, but fn empty_stack<T>() => Stack<T> doesn't get that same bound propagated to its own generic parameter, so rustc rejects the generated  (I2). Needs the same bound-propagation fix generic struct-returning functions elsewhere presumably already have — or doesn't, if this is the first generic-struct-with-list-field-returning-function case exercised end to end.
cards.plan: Five criteria, four independent root causes, each already diagnosed in the body and logs — implement, do not re-investigate from scratch. (1) Qualified-name cascade: pick ONE mechanism and apply it at every consumer. Either make check_type_assignable and is_covered_struct_ty/tir_covers (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/subset/entry.rs) split-and-compare qualified names exactly the way the #1600 field_type fix does, or stop qualifying nominal_name in check_struct_lit (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs) except when two same-named structs are genuinely in scope. Do not ship three local patches. Keep the fixture at its original bare return type; it must pass without dodging E0113. (2) Clone-bound propagation: generic struct-returning functions must emit the same derived bounds the struct carries — fn empty_stack<T>() => Stack<T> gets the Clone bound Stack<T> requires; fix in codegen signature emission, prove no rustc rejection (I2). (3) D-FLOWTYPE1 else-branch narrowing: statement-position Stmt::If in CheckerCore/statements.rs gets the same swap value-position Expr::If already implements (expr.rs ~487-505: rewrite x == None to a Present pattern test and swap branches). (4) strip_vetted_prelude_modules (tests/tir_support/mod.rs): the byte-level brace counter desyncs on some token category after the format-string fix (jet_cell consumes only ~11KB from byte 843357); replace it with a Rust-aware matcher that also handles char literals, raw strings, and comments, or switch to line-based mod-boundary matching. Proof: cargo test --test tir_unsafe_and_runtime green. blockedBy: none.

cards.title: The environment-module selector flag still spells the retired word profile
cards.body:
Card #1526 renamed every profile meaning per the ratified one-word ruling, but the ruling's fold list assumed --env-profile and the env --profile select the same thing. They do not: --profile selected a declared composition (now --preset), while --env-profile selects one env.<name> module. One name cannot answer both, so --env-profile kept its spelling and only its prose moved off the retired word. The flag a user types still says profile. Ballot D-ENVFLAG1 attached.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): `--env-profile` is a surviving use of a retired word. Fold this rename into the retirement sweep rather than shipping a private teaching diagnostic for it: ballot D-ONCE-RETIRE1 (card #1656) decides whether a retired spelling errors, auto-rewrites, or both, and every retirement carries the same three parts (error, rewrite, ratchet).
cards.plan: D-ENVFLAG1=A is ratified: the flag becomes --env <name>, spelling the env.<name> axis it selects, uniform on every command; --env-profile retires and teaches the replacement. Mechanical rename plus one new retirement diagnostic. Steps: (1) rename EnvProfileFlag and its parse row to Env across the six known sites (criterion 1 lists them); (2) add the retirement diagnostic row copying the E1300 --profile pattern, with snapshot; (3) sweep help text, docs, and examples for the old spelling; (4) prove with the usage tests and the new snapshot. Greenfield: delete the old spelling outright — no alias, no fallback parse. blockedBy: none.

cards.title: One flow-fact store with one join rule
cards.body: Six stores track facts that change along control flow: moved bindings, uninit fields, typestate, optional narrowing, taint and view windows. Each hand-writes its own branch merge, and two of those merges are dead code, so typestate and partial init keep whatever branch the walker saw last. Build one store keyed by binding and plane. Each plane supplies only its join rule, and the shared walker applies joins at every merge point. Sema only; nothing a user types changes. This is substrate: it lands before any per-plane card builds on it.

Combined proof: cargo test --test typestate --test taint --test uninit_fixed --test flow_facts_tiers, all green (14/23/13/9).

Moved, uninit, narrowing, view, binding, typestate and taint facts all live on it. The two dead joins are gone as a class: State.rs join_after is deleted and its rule is now the typestate plane's join, and UninitState::merge_paths is live. New warning L0152 reports a branch that leaves a value in two different states. Green: typestate 12, uninit_fixed 13, flow_facts_tiers 9, taint 22, pin 21, arena 10, diagnostics_coverage 11. Criterion 9 is still open: the corpus run cannot give a clean signal while the shared tree carries other sessions' unfinished codegen and runtime work, so the byte-identical check is owed once the tree is quiet. Failures in ownership, single_use and sema_soundness were each reproduced on a clean HEAD build of the same tree, so they are not from this change.

cards.title: Home the orphan facts on the one registry
cards.body: Some facts the compiler holds live outside every registry. Send-safety is a stray flag on the checker. #Track origin, view provenance and unit-scale provenance are recorded but unreadable. Failure attribution and maturity are unregistered. Each fact a user can meet becomes a typed row on the one registration table and is readable like every other fact. Prover internals stay engine-side, per the ownership wall.

Delete the stray sendable flag on LocalInfo in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema (grep sendable under crates/jet-sema/src) once send-safety reads from the registry instead. Make failure attribution readable as report.$attribution, and wire every new row through the $ read surface and reflect() (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Reflect.rs). Leave uninit tracking and exhaustiveness engine-side with no row, matching the same ownership wall, and state in docs/spec which facts are user-facing versus prover-internal. Prove tier parity (I9) with one test per tier — parser, sema, TIR, AOT, JIT/dev, comptime, REPL, web — showing the same fact value, plus one targeted test per homed row exercising $ and reflect().

cards.title: The @ fact read: one act for every registered plane
cards.body:
Reading what the compiler knows becomes one act with one mark. Severity.$range, send_report.$effects, Order.$states and Meters.$dimension answer typed values from the one registry, and $build.profile is the same act with the build as its subject. The string fallback in reflection dies, and reflect() stays as the aggregate view over the same typed facts. Comptime only: a fact is a value, it never mints a type and it never dispatches.

— Reconciliation (2026-08-07, corpus audit): the read spelling ($ vs @) is now on open ballot D-ONCE-AT1 (option D would respell $range/$build reads as @range/@build) with D-ONCE-DOLLAR1 as the companion. Implement per the ratified outcome; the mechanism is glyph-neutral.

— Ratified (2026-08-07): D-ONCE-AT1 = D — prefix @ is the compile-time mark and fact-read glyph; infix @ unchanged; $ is freed. The pending-input clause above is resolved; implement this outcome.
cards.plan: Implement the fact-read act so Severity.$range, send_report.$effects, Order.$states, Meters.$dimension, and $build.* all resolve typed values from the one registry in crates/jet-foundation/src/Registry.rs, using the prefix glyph ratified by D-ONCE-AT1=D (prefix @, not $). Delete the "\0state:" string encoding and the reflection string fallback in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Reflect.rs, keeping reflect() as the aggregate view over the same typed facts. Reject a fact read outside comptime, a fact used in type position (S26), and any fact-driven runtime dispatch (D-FACTMODEL1) with registered diagnostics and targeted tests. Fold every fact read before codegen so AOT, jet run, and the interpreter see one already-folded program. Add a golden example under examples/features/reflection/ reading a fact from four different planes, add the Syntax.rs entry, and regenerate grammars and snapshots.

cards.title: One law voice: facts tighten, gates loosen
cards.body: Five words name the same one-way rule today: tighten, attenuate, narrow, conserve and erase. Diagnostics and docs adopt one pair. A fact tighten silently; a gate loosens it, and loosening is always written. Operation names are untouched: flow narrowing keeps its name, widening conversions keep theirs, and no user-typed spelling changes.
