cards.title: ICE report polish: honest attachment copy, RUST_BACKTRACE passthrough, gate the self-test hook
cards.body: Three follow-ups on the #1661 panic hook. The report copy promises an attached generated file in cases where none exists (4 of 6 call sites). install_ice_panic_hook replaces the default hook unconditionally, so RUST_BACKTRACE=1 prints nothing; pass through when set. JET_ICE_SELF_TEST=1 deliberate-panic backdoor ships in release binaries; gate it to debug or an internal flag.
cards.plan: All three fixes live in crates/jet-foundation/src/Diagnostics.rs, functions render_ice_report (~line 891) and install_ice_panic_hook (~line 916). (1) Honest attachment copy: render_ice_report's fixed body always says 'attaching your source file and the generated file below' but 4 of 6 call sites (the panic hook itself, and Source/CmdCompile.rs's two 'missing web codegen output' sites plus 'missing plugin codegen output') pass detail="" or a detail with no generated-file content — only the two rustc-rejection sites (Source/CmdCompile.rs ~2889, ~3379) actually carry generated code in detail. Change render_ice_report so the file-attachment sentence only appears when detail is non-empty (or split the fixed prefix into a shorter always-true sentence plus a conditional file-attachment line), and update the two CmdCompile.rs call sites at ~2712, ~3154, ~3196 (missing codegen output) if their wording still implies a file exists. (2) RUST_BACKTRACE passthrough: install_ice_panic_hook calls std::panic::set_hook unconditionally, discarding Rust's default hook, so RUST_BACKTRACE=1 has no effect. Inside the closure, when std::env::var_os("RUST_BACKTRACE") is set, also print std::backtrace::Backtrace::force_capture() (or capture it before installing the hook and append to the eprintln!) so the env var still does something. (3) Gate JET_ICE_SELF_TEST: it currently panics on any build when the env var is set, shipping a deliberate-panic backdoor in release binaries. Gate the check with #[cfg(debug_assertions)] (matches tests/ice_report_single_home.rs's use case, which only needs it in debug/test builds) or an internal-only cfg flag if release-mode self-testing is still needed by CI. Prove: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test ice_report_single_home` stays green after the self-test gate change (adjust the test to build debug if it doesn't already), and manually confirm (or add a targeted test) that a non-debug build with JET_ICE_SELF_TEST=1 does not panic.

Source/CmdCompile.rs passes false at the three no-codegen-output sites and true at the three rustc-rejection sites, which write the file before invoking rustc.

cards.title: JIT HTTP readiness is a sleep-poll stand-in, not the Prelude poller
cards.body: crates/jet-jit/src/net_http_rt.rs defines its own jet_scheduler_tcp_listener_io_wait, jet_scheduler_tcp_stream_io_wait, jet_scheduler_tcp_stream_ready_wait and jet_scheduler_udp_io_wait as 5ms thread sleeps. The emitted AOT program uses the real readiness poller in Prelude/Scheduler.rs (epoll on Linux, kqueue on the BSD family, IOCP on Windows, portable poll otherwise). Card #1637 made that poller compile inside jet_codegen::scheduler, so the JIT can now call the same functions. Until it does, network wait behavior differs by tier, which is the I9 shape #1637 exists to remove.
cards.plan: crates/jet-jit/src/net_http_rt.rs already imports some real poller functions from jet_codegen::scheduler (see `use jet_codegen::scheduler::{...}` at line 12) — card #1637 made crates/jet-codegen/src/lib.rs's `pub mod scheduler` compile crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs in-crate so both AOT and JIT share one epoll/kqueue/IOCP/poll poller (I9). Delete the four local 5ms-sleep stand-ins at net_http_rt.rs lines 265-294 (jet_scheduler_tcp_listener_io_wait, jet_scheduler_tcp_stream_io_wait, jet_scheduler_tcp_stream_ready_wait, jet_scheduler_udp_io_wait) and route every caller in this file to the corresponding jet_codegen::scheduler:: functions (Prelude/Scheduler.rs lines ~1543-1600: jet_scheduler_tcp_stream_ready_wait, jet_scheduler_tcp_listener_io_wait — two overloads by cfg — and jet_scheduler_udp_io_wait), adding them to the existing `use jet_codegen::scheduler::{...}` import list. Check the unix-socket sibling functions at lines 296+ (jet_scheduler_unix_listener_io_wait etc.) for the same stand-in pattern and fix in the same change if present, since the card names the whole family. cards.title: Deadline and panic-boundary preludes have no single source
cards.body: Prelude/CoreLib/Top/MathRandomTime.rs owns the #Context(deadline) clock and budget, and Prelude/Core.rs owns the scheduler panic boundary. Both are entangled with surfaces the JIT host does not carry, so crates/jet-codegen/src/SchedulerHost.rs binds them by hand for the compiled scheduler. The bodies are short and self-contained. Split each into its own Prelude file so the emitted program and the in-crate host include one source, the way Prelude/Scheduler.rs and Prelude/Stream.rs already do.
cards.plan: Two extractions, each following the pattern crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs and Prelude/Stream.rs already set (one file, included both by AOT's include_str! list in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/mod.rs and by the in-crate `pub mod scheduler { include!(...) }` block in crates/jet-codegen/src/lib.rs ~line 18-26). (1) Deadline clock and budget: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/MathRandomTime.rs lines ~1-65 (JET_CTX_DEADLINE_MS, JetDeadlineGuard, jet_ctx_deadline_ms, jet_ctx_push_deadline, jet_deadline_remaining_ms, jet_deadline_exceeded with its E3003 raise, jet_deadline_check) are duplicated almost verbatim inside crates/jet-codegen/src/SchedulerHost.rs lines ~76-124. Move this block into a new file, e.g. crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Deadline.rs, delete it from both MathRandomTime.rs and SchedulerHost.rs, add `include_str!("../Prelude/Deadline.rs")` to the AOT emission list in Codegen/mod.rs (near line 800, alongside MathRandomTime.rs) and add `include!("Prelude/Deadline.rs")` to the scheduler module in lib.rs (~line 22-24). Keep MathRandomTime.rs's other clock/random/time functions untouched. (2) Scheduler panic boundary: JetDeadlineUnwind and the panic-boundary catch/rethrow logic that crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.rs owns (grep JetDeadlineUnwind and jet_typed_deadline_boundary_should_unwind there) is re-typed by hand in SchedulerHost.rs around line 245 and 721. Extract that shared body into a new file, e.g. crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/PanicBoundary.rs, included the same way from both Core.rs's AOT concatenation point and lib.rs's scheduler module, and delete the hand-typed copy from SchedulerHost.rs. After both extractions, SchedulerHost.rs should hold only marshalling glue (JIT-host bindings that call into the shared Prelude functions), no re-typed bodies. Prove: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo build` succeeds (both crates compile against the new shared files), then `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet-codegen` and any #Context(deadline) example (examples/features/concurrency or similar, if one exists) run clean under AOT and `jet run` to confirm the shared source still produces the same E3003 behavior on both tiers (I9).

cards.title: Lint selection in config takes names, never codes
cards.body: Owner ruling 2026-08-07: config, settings, and policy surfaces use clearly-named keys and values; E/L codes appear only inside rendered diagnostics where surrounding text explains them. Today policy.lints.deny parses bare lint codes (parse_lint_code_list, crates/jet-foundation/src/Policy blocks), which makes configs unreadable. Every lint gains a stable snake_case name at registration; every config surface that selects lints (deny/allow lists, the D-REPORT-SEV1 severity control) takes names; a bare code in config is refused with a fix-it that names the name. Existing code-keyed spellings migrate through the #1718 retirement mechanism.
cards.plan: Two changes, one law: names in config, codes in diagnostics. First, extend lint registration (the registry #1538 built, or the existing lint table if registration has not migrated yet) so every lint carries a stable snake_case name; add a coverage test that fails a nameless lint. Second, replace parse_lint_code_list (crates/jet-foundation Policy blocks, Blocks.rs:820 area) with name parsing; a bare L-code in config gets a registered refusal diagnostic whose fix-it prints the name, wired through the #1718 retirement table with a ratchet asserting zero code-keyed configs in-repo. Check the D-REPORT-SEV1 severity surface (docs/proposals/toolchain-one-report-every-surface.md) uses names too — #1678 depends on it. Prove with a targeted policy-parsing test red-then-green plus the ratchet. Rendered diagnostics keep showing the code beside the name.

cards.title: E0141 branch divergence: statement-position if/else (Stmt::Switch arm-table) still undetected
cards.body: D-BRANCH-AST1=C: classic statement if/else (with or without else, e.g. `if cond { release(^db) }`) lowers to Stmt::Switch with a compiler-private true subject (classic_if_switch in jet-parser), merged by its own arm-table FlowFacts::merge_paths in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/switches.rs:764 — a separate merge site from Expr::If's value-if form (CheckerInfer/expr.rs), which card #1737 wired. A #SingleUse value consumed on one Stmt::Switch arm and dropped on another (including the implicit no-else arm) still passes silently: Moved::join is a union, same root cause #1737 fixed for value-if. tests/ui/single_use_branch.jet was seemingly written for exactly this statement-if scenario but never reaches E0141 today — it fails first on an unrelated pre-existing E0120 bug (Lock.{resource: resource} move-fill), which masks the gap.
cards.plan:
Enriched plan (extends the existing plan, no changes to intent):

Insertion point: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/switches.rs::check_switch, right before the final
`self.flow = crate::Sema::FlowFacts::FlowFacts::merge_paths(&outside_table, &paths);` at line 763. `outside_table`
(set at line 624, after it_scope pop) is this function's equivalent of expr.rs's `before` snapshot — use it as the
pre-switch baseline for bindings enumeration and as the scope_depth root, exactly like the Expr::If site.

Port the divergent_single_use block from crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs:532-560 (added by #1737)
verbatim, generalized from 2 arms (then_path/else_path) to N arms (`paths: Vec<FlowFacts>`, already collected by
the per-arm loop above at lines 556-612):
  - scope_depth = self.scope_depth() (after it_scope pop, matching outside_table's depth)
  - for each (name, info) in outside_table.bindings.iter_at(scope_depth) with a single_use_span and not already
    moved in outside_table: collect whether it's moved in each path in `paths`
  - if moved status is not uniform across all paths (some paths moved it, some didn't) -> push
    e0141_unconsumed_branch(&name, use_span) via crate::Sema::CheckerOwnership::e0141_unconsumed_branch
  - include the implicit "no arm taken" path: when can_skip_every_arm is true, `outside_table.clone()` is already
    pushed into `paths` at line 761 before the merge, so it participates in the divergence check for free if the
    check runs after that push and before the merge call — confirm insertion sits after line 761's push, not before.
  - sort by span start then name (matches expr.rs determinism) before pushing diagnostics.

Fixture: tests/ui/single_use_branch.jet's unrelated E0120 is `Lock.{resource: resource}` at line 7 inside
`acquire()` — a plain move-fill the checker rejects with 'not moved here'. Fix by copying the already-fixed sibling
fixture's pattern: `tests/ui/single_use_branch_expr.jet` uses `Lock.{resource: ~resource}` at its equivalent line.
Apply the same one-token fix (add `~`) to single_use_branch.jet, then run the file through the compiler and bless
tests/ui/single_use_branch.stderr to the new E0141 output (expect the same shape as
tests/ui/single_use_branch_expr.stderr: 'Error [E0141]: `db` must be used exactly once, but one path through this
`if` leaves it unused', pointing at the `db :: acquire("db")` binding span).

I9 note: this is a sema-only diagnostic (no codegen/runtime tiers involved), so no marshalling/Prelude concern
applies here — the fix is confined to crates/jet-sema.

Proof command: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test ui_snapshots -- single_use_branch
Also run: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test ui_snapshots  (full UI snapshot suite, to catch any other
statement-if #SingleUse fixture the corpus already has that would now newly report E0141 — criterion 3's "existing
corpus stays green" requires checking the whole tests/ui/*.jet + examples/ corpus for a statement-if that already
diverges a #SingleUse value silently; grep tests/ui and examples for #SingleUse structs used inside statement-position
if/else first).

Ballot status: no owner-gated choice found. This generalizes an already-ratified mechanism (D-LIN1, E0141) from one
AST merge site (Expr::If) to a second, structurally identical one (Stmt::Switch's classic-if desugar) — same
diagnostic code, same wording, same semantics. No new syntax, no new diagnostic scope, no new user-facing decision.
Proceed without a ballot.

cards.title: JIT parity: List/Map builtin host functions (iter_adapters, iter_tools_audit, list_surface, map_surface)
cards.body:
Four jit_gaps.txt stems left open by the #1477 family (#1478/#1479 closed their siblings). From the #1663 ledger retirement enumeration.

STATUS 2026-08-08 (bd12-jita): effects/taint shell_arg CLOSED (criterion #3) -- root cause was Type::Tagged (taint marker) not stripped before JIT builtin-method dispatch, fixed at 2 sites (see criterion #3 evidence).

REMAINING (iter_adapters, iter_tools_audit, list_surface) are NOT tier-gate bugs -- they need genuinely new JIT host-function implementations, comparable in size to the #1477 commit itself (24 files, ~5000 lines). Per-stem findings from this session's investigation, so a follow-up doesn't have to re-derive them:

- list_surface.jet: fails immediately (stmt 3) on xs.starts_with([1,2]) where xs is a LIST. crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs's TBuiltinOp::StartsWith/EndsWith arm ONLY implements the String case (self.host.str_starts_with/str_ends_with) and has a latent bug: its guard  returns Err only when NEITHER holds, so a Local-bound LIST receiver (xs IS a Local) slips past the guard and would call the STRING host on a List handle -- never exercised today only because the whole function still declines earlier/elsewhere, but this needs a real fix (a genuine List.starts_with/ends_with host fn + a correct type guard), not just a wider Err. Beyond that: TBuiltinOp::ListCopy, ListEqual, ListBinarySearch, ListUnion, ListIntersection, ListDifference, ListRandom, ListMinMax, ListReplace are ALL unconditional  stubs in lower_ctx.rs (~line 15155-15179) with NO backing host fn in crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs at all (checked: none of jet_jit_list_copy/list_equal/list_binary_search/list_union/list_intersection/list_difference/list_random/list_min_max/list_replace exist). Each needs a new host fn (pattern: see jet_jit_list_zip/list_unzip/list_flatten in Collections.rs for the rt.heap.clone_int_list/alloc_empty_list idiom) + a resident_safe_builtin_op arm + wiring in lower_ctx.rs's TBuiltinOp match, mirroring the Prelude semantics in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs.

- map_surface.jet: fails immediately (stmt 3, Map.new().len()). TBuiltinOp::MapNew already has a matching host fn (self.host.coll.map_new, already wired for map-literal construction at 3 other call sites in lower_ctx.rs) -- wiring MapNew is a free win but doesn't move the needle alone since MapFromKeys (line 6) has no host fn either, and every subsequent builtin (MapCopy, MapEqual, MapFirst, MapToList, MapMin, MapMax, MapIntersection, MapSliceKeys, MapContainsValue, MapPopFirst) is the same unconditional stub. Needs the SAME scale of new-host-fn work as list_surface, targeting crates/jet-foundation Map internals instead of List.

- iter_adapters.jet / iter_tools_audit.jet: fail on generic Iter adapters (take_while/position/min_by/max_by/flat_map/repeat/cycle/drop_last/is_sorted/dedup_by/compare/split/shuffle/chunk_while, count_by, unzip, intersperse, flatten, SortedSet/PriorityQueue/Cache/BitSet/ByteBuffer surface). Several of these (min_by/max_by/position/count_by) take a CLOSURE argument -- 'jit closure method unsupported' is the SAME message collections/set.jet hits (see #1758), meaning fixing closure-taking iterator adapters in the JIT is a shared root cause across #1754 and #1758's set.jet, likely the highest-leverage next slice (calling back into a JIT-compiled closure from a host adapter loop, or inlining the loop in Cranelift IR) -- bigger than a single new host fn, needs its own design pass before implementation.

None of the above are I9 violations to defer -- AOT+interpreter are already correct (verified: all 3 remaining stems'  output matches examples/features/expected/... via interpreter deopt fallback, no parity_divergence). The gap is pure JIT compile-coverage breadth, tracked honestly in tests/jit_gaps.txt (unchanged for these 3 stems this session).
cards.plan: Add real JIT host functions for the List/Map builtins that are currently unconditional stubs in crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs (around line 15155-15179: ListCopy, ListEqual, ListBinarySearch, ListUnion, ListIntersection, ListDifference, ListRandom, ListMinMax, ListReplace, and the matching Map ops), following the jet_jit_list_zip/list_unzip/list_flatten pattern in crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs and mirroring crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs semantics. Fix the latent StartsWith/EndsWith type-guard bug in lower_ctx.rs that lets a List receiver fall through to the String host path. Separately, design and implement closure-taking builtin adapters (min_by/max_by/position/count_by/take_while/flat_map, etc.) reaching across the JIT host/Cranelift boundary — this needs its own design (call back into a JIT-compiled closure from a host loop, or inline the loop in Cranelift IR) before implementation, and is shared with card #1758's set.jet blockers. - map_surface.jet / set.jet: see #1754's body for the shared root cause and per-op ledger (map_surface needs the same missing-Map-builtin-host-fns as #1754's list_surface/map_surface residue; set.jet's blockers -- all/filter/each/fold/map/flat_map on Set -- are CLOSURE-taking builtin methods, hitting the SAME 'jit closure method unsupported' as iter_adapters/iter_tools_audit's min_by/max_by/position/count_by in #1754. criteria.text: zip_family panic/index-oob triaged: real bug fixed at root or reclassified with evidence
criteria.evidence: TRIAGED: real compiler bug, fixed at root, not just a tier gap. Root cause: crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs's TBuiltinOp::Zip arm unconditionally indexed args[0] to get the zip partner. The free zero-arg zip() call lowers (TIR::lower_empty_zip_family, jet-codegen) to input_count:0, args:[] -- so args[0] panicked with exactly the observed message (index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0). AOT's own emit path handles this shape correctly via a dedicated empty-zip constructor; only the JIT lowering was missing the guard. Fixed: added an explicit input_count/flatten/fill_mode guard before touching args, so a genuinely-2-input no-pad zip still takes the fast self.host.coll.list_zip path (unchanged, still correct), while an empty/N-ary/flatten/zip_pad shape now returns a graceful Err (declines to interp) instead of panicking. Verified: examples/features/collections/zip_family.jet no longer panics under JIT compile (confirmed via cargo test -p jet --test dev jit_coverage_audit -- --nocapture: reason text changed from 'jit compile panicked before returning an unsupported reason: index out of bounds...' to a normal 'jit builtin method unsupported: n-ary/padded/empty zip' Err), and its output still matches AOT via interpreter fallback (diff clean).

log.text: [settle round 2] bd15-rev's third door closed plus a fourth it implied: TExprKind::Deref and the p.*=rhs Ptr store now gate on real_address_values like the volatile pair; both mint sites (real address_of local, RawOf stack_addr) marked. Reviewer repro declines E0956 under jet run (no segfault); pin/mmio_board_write/pointer_cast_deref/unsafe_obligations smokes green. Awaiting composed-review verification.

[review bd15-rev] BLOCKED. The gate covers volatile_read (lower_ctx.rs:8737) and volatile_write (8750), and the address-identity fns now have one home (pub tir_place_address_key/stable_place_address in jet-codegen eval/exprs.rs, JIT byte-copies deleted) -- both of those hold. But a THIRD door still consumes synthetic addresses and it is live UB: TExprKind::PtrFromAddr (lower_ctx.rs:13599) passes the Int straight through, and TExprKind::Deref (lower_ctx.rs:13659-13669) does load(clif, MemFlags::trusted(), pointer, 0) with no real_address_values check. So mem.address_of on a FIELD place (the synthetic FNV iconst minted at 8728) reaches a trusted load through mem.Ptr<T>.from_addr(a) + p.* instead of through volatile_read. Repro run on master d9b265daa: a Node.{payload,hops} local, then inside #Unsafe -- a :: mem.address_of(node.payload); p :: mem.Ptr<Int>.from_addr(a); print(p.*). Default jet run SEGFAULTS (core dumped, no output); jet run --release (AOT) prints 'deref: 41' and exits 0. This is a REGRESSION from this card's own earlier fix: at d55583eeb^ the JIT returned Err('jit address_of needs a local place') and declined to deopt, so the synthetic address never existed. Fix: gate TExprKind::Deref on the same real_address_values provenance (and PtrFromAddr should propagate provenance rather than launder it), matching what the interpreter already declines. Secondary note, non-blocking: the gate is keyed on Cranelift Value identity, which only survives use_var when the def and use sit in one straight-line block -- any branch between mem.address_of and the volatile call mints a block param and the gate declines a REAL stack address. That is safe (deopt) but fragile, and it is why lowlevel/mmio_board_write and lowlevel/unsafe_obligations still compile today by luck of being branch-free.
probe

Fix 2: made tir_place_address_key/stable_place_address public with jet-jit sharing docs, re-exported through TIR, deleted JIT byte-copies, and switched JIT address_of to canonical helpers. Files: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/{eval/exprs.rs,eval/mod.rs,mod.rs}, crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs.

(2) jit_place_address_key/jit_stable_place_address (lower_ctx.rs:263-297) are byte-copies of jet-codegen's private fns — address identity is semantics, one home required: make the jet-codegen fns pub and call them.

Fixed both stems. memory/pin: mem.address_of on a field place (node.payload, not a bare local) now mints the same stable non-zero structural-path identity TIR-eval already uses (jet-codegen eval/exprs.rs tir_place_address_key/stable_place_address) instead of erroring; bare locals keep the real Cranelift stack-slot address. memory/shared_weak_cycle: Shared.Weak<T>.clone() now treated as the same copyable-handle door as Shared<T>.clone(); this surfaced a real pre-existing off-by-one in jet_jit_shared_strong_count (Memory.rs) — the shared() lookup clones the Arc out of rt.shareds, so strong_count read included that temporary clone's own strong ref. cards.title: run_gaps: lowlevel ExternCall-at-comptime (ffi, inline_asm, inline_c)
cards.body: Three run_gaps stems: ExternCall reached at comptime in lowlevel examples. From the #1663 enumeration.
cards.plan:
FRESH PROBE (2026-08-08, current HEAD, reran twice each for consistency): all 3 named stems fail, but with a
DIFFERENT error than tests/jit_gaps.txt records. The ledger says `expr ExternCall` (a compile-time "construct not
lowered" reason); the actual current failure for all three is a runtime panic during default `jet run`:
  `panic: jit ffi: no bridge bound`, exit 70. This means ExternCall itself now lowers/compiles fine (the ledger's
  literal reason is stale) — the remaining gap is narrower: the FFI bridge table is never populated on this
  execution path before the extern call fires.

Root cause located: crates/jet-jit/src/Ffi.rs — a process-global `static FFI_STATE: Mutex<Option<FfiState>>`
(line 64) starts `None`. `bind_bundle_ffi(bundle)` (line 92) is the only thing that ever populates it, by loading
the `extern rust/c/asm "..."` bridge library/symbols named in the bundle and storing their pointers keyed by
wrapper name. `jet_jit_extern_call` (line 197), the actual callee every `#[FFI(...)] fn` body compiles down to,
traps with exactly "jit ffi: no bridge bound" (line 211) whenever `FFI_STATE` is still `None` at call time.
`bind_bundle_ffi` is currently only invoked from crates/jet-jit/src/jit/api_debug.rs (4 call sites, lines
54/108/149/211/225 — debug/introspection entry points), never from the default `jet run` dev-tier entry point.
crates/jet-jit/src/jit/resident.rs:169's comment ("`bind_bundle_ffi` / `clear_ffi` own its lifetime at the outer
entry points") confirms the binding is meant to be an outer-caller responsibility that the default-`jet run` outer
caller currently skips.

Seams to trace: find the actual outer entry point default `jet run` uses (likely crates/jet-jit/src/jit/deopt.rs's
`run_whole_interp`, or whatever dispatches to jit/resident.rs for a program containing FFI-marked functions — grep
for where `functions_compile.rs` or the CLI `run` command decides tier and calls into jit/resident.rs or
jit/deopt.rs) and add the missing `crate::Ffi::bind_bundle_ffi(bundle)` call (with matching `clear_ffi` teardown,
mirroring api_debug.rs's pattern) on that path, before any FFI-bearing bundle executes.

I9 rule: this is infrastructure wiring, not semantics — `bind_bundle_ffi` and `jet_jit_extern_call` already do the
one canonical FFI marshalling (loading the exact bridge library / symbol the AOT-compiled program also links
against); the fix is calling that existing marshaling entry point from one more place, not adding a second FFI
binding mechanism. Do not special-case per-stem (ffi/inline_asm/inline_c all go through the same
`jet_jit_extern_call` callee — one fix should close all three).

Missing exit criteria to add: three-tier byte-identical agreement per stem; ledger rows corrected/deleted; the fix
is proven not to only patch the 3 example stems but any FFI-bearing program under default `jet run` (add or point
at a regression test beyond the 3 goldens if one doesn't already exist for "FFI works under jet run, not just jet
build").

Proof commands:
  - scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/lowlevel/ffi.jet          (diff vs expected/lowlevel/ffi.out; expect "aGk=")
  - scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/lowlevel/inline_asm.jet   (diff vs expected/lowlevel/inline_asm.out; expect "42")
  - scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/lowlevel/inline_c.jet     (diff vs expected/lowlevel/inline_c.out; expect "42")
  - scripts/agent/jet-env jet build --release examples/features/lowlevel/ffi.jet && run it (AOT ground truth stays green, no regression)
  - scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev jit_coverage_audit
  - scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev ledger_cross_check_holds

Caveat for the implementer: this repo tree is currently dirty with substantial uncommitted prior WIP (see `git
status` before starting), and jet's build cache is keyed on AST hash and has previously served stale binaries
(see MEMORY: jet-build-cache-stale-binaries) — an earlier probe in this same session produced one spurious
"succeeds" result for ffi.jet before a rebuild made the panic reproduce consistently. Confirm the failure
reproduces fresh (clear ~/.cache/jet if results look inconsistent) before trusting either the "still fails" state
above or a fix.

log.text: BLOCKED/CONTRADICTED by bd17-rev fresh-context review on master 347ee2f2e. The 509daa1b7 restore ("trio still declines on master") does not reproduce. With target/debug/jet rebuilt from master and ~/.cache/jet deleted first (both the build and run cache; see the stale-binary trap), all three stems pass under default jet run: lowlevel/ffi prints aGk=, lowlevel/inline_asm prints 42, lowlevel/inline_c prints 42, each byte-identical to examples/features/expected/lowlevel/*.out, exit 0, cold run 1.4s so this is the JIT/deopt path and not a silent AOT fallback. The mechanism is real: 9e8ec798a moved crate::Ffi::bind_bundle_ffi out of api_debug.rs try_resident and up to the CraneliftBackend::run entry (crates/jet-jit/src/jit/backend.rs:28), so the interpreter deopt path now gets the bundle FFI bound too. tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt already classes all three as resident_jit (lines 177-180), never as a run-tier failure, which is why ledger_cross_check_holds stays green either way and could not catch the bad restore. So the three run_gaps rows at tests/jit_gaps.txt:476-478 are dead ledger entries that only burn the shrink-only ratchet budget (7 of 12 rows used). Recommend re-deleting them, i.e. reinstating c3ca1eabe, and closing this card. Do not re-probe with a stale binary or a warm ~/.cache/jet: that is almost certainly what produced the false red.

CORRECTED root cause: no ExternCall lowering gap exists. TExprKind::ExternCall lowering (jit/lower_ctx.rs:14127, since 7f2eb2001 2026-07-27) + resident-safety marking (jit/safety.rs:1492) + backend-entry crate::Ffi::bind_bundle_ffi call (jit/backend.rs:29) already form a complete, correct pipeline on master (347ee2f2e) with NO code change.

Explained the prior FALSE-GREEN/false-negative flip-flop: reproduction depends entirely on the invoking shell's PATH. backend.rs:29 calls Ffi::bind_bundle_ffi(bundle), which calls jet_pkg_model::FFI::prepare(bundle) to build the runtime FFI bridge cdylib (needs cc/rustc on PATH). When that build fails (toolchain absent from PATH), bind_bundle_ffi returns Err, backend.rs falls back to run_whole_interp, and the interpreter has no ExternCall support -> E0956 "isn't supported in Jet's quick-run mode yet". When toolchain IS on PATH (jet-env's nix devShell, the project's own mandated command channel per AGENTS.md), bind succeeds, try_resident runs, ExternCall lowers correctly, trio passes.

Proved by direct comparison on the identical, unchanged binary (same md5): raw shell (no cc/rustc/cargo in PATH at all - confirmed via `which`) reproduces E0956 on all 3 stems, 100% repeatable. Same binary invoked via `scripts/agent/jet-env jet run ...` (adds nix rustc-wrapper/clang-wrapper/gcc-wrapper to PATH) passes all 3, 100% repeatable across repeated ~/.cache/jet/{build,run} clears. This means prior probes that "reproduced E0956 on freshly built master" were almost certainly run outside jet-env's PATH (e.g. a bare tool shell) - a reproduction-methodology gap, not a source gap. bd16-externcall's original conclusion ("no code fix needed") was correct; the orchestrator's E0956 catch was a false negative from an under-provisioned PATH, not a real decline.

Proof (fresh build, jet-env channel, ~/.cache/jet/{build,run} cleared before each run):
- jet run x3 clean-cache passes: ffi=aGk=, inline_asm=42, inline_c=42 (matches examples/features/expected/lowlevel/*.out byte-for-byte)
- jet build --release (AOT) + direct binary run: same 3 outputs, byte-identical to JIT (AOT/JIT parity holds)
- tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt already lists all 3 under resident_jit (independently corroborates)
- cargo test --test dev jit_coverage_audit: ok (before AND after row deletion)
- cargo test --test dev ledger_cross_check_holds: ok (before AND after row deletion)
- cargo test -p jet --test jit_run: 8 passed, 2 failed (zero_arg_process_spec_builders_run_resident, expert_terminal_model_runs_resident_and_fails_closed - unrelated pre-existing reds per brief, both E0956 on ProcessSpec/terminal-model constructs, not FFI/ExternCall)

Only change made: deleted the 3 stale run_gaps rows (lowlevel/ffi, lowlevel/inline_asm, lowlevel/inline_c) from tests/jit_gaps.txt - a ledger cleanup, no source diff. Commit a8d0521e4 on branch bd17/externcall (worktree .claude/worktrees/jita, base master 347ee2f2e). Mechanical-tier per current review policy (ledger row deletion) - no fresh-context reviewer required, orchestrator spot-check + this evidence should suffice.

Recommend logging a papercut: scripts/agent/jet-env is the only PATH that reliably provisions the FFI runtime-bridge toolchain (cc/rustc/clang); any agent probe of FFI/lowlevel examples outside jet-env will falsely appear to decline.

FALSE GREEN caught at integration: bd16-externcall reported the trio working with no code change, but freshly built master declines all three (E0956) — its jitb worktree evidently carried non-master state. Rows restored (commit above). Real remaining work unchanged: TExprKind::ExternCall lowering in lower_ctx.rs through the bound bridge table. Criteria 1+3 meets retracted; do not trust the c3ca1eabe proof.

Root shape: no code fix needed. TExprKind::ExternCall JIT lowering (lower_ctx.rs, since 2026-07-27) and its resident-safety allow (safety.rs, wave-6) were already in master; combined with bd15-luna-ffi's earlier backend-entry bind_bundle_ffi call (backend.rs:28), the pipeline is complete. The orchestrator's prior log entry ('no ExternCall lowering') predates the commits this merge picked up. Only fix: deleted 3 stale run_gaps rows in tests/jit_gaps.txt (lowlevel/ffi, inline_asm, inline_c) — jit_corpus_gate.txt already listed them under resident_jit. cargo test --test dev jit_coverage_audit: ok; ledger_cross_check_holds: ok. jet run + jet build byte-identical on all 3 (aGk=/42/42) after clearing ~/.cache/jet. Moving to verify.

Orchestrator proof: the backend-entry bind lands and deopts with a recorded reason on failure, but the lowlevel trio still declines E0956 — the JIT has no TExprKind::ExternCall lowering, so bound bridges are never called from compiled code. Remaining work: lower ExternCall through the bound bridge table (build-capable worker; jitb worktree). run_gaps rows stay.

Fresh review: Carver (gpt-5.6-luna, high) found no issues after recheck. Review covered backend bind order, FFI error fallback, unsupported hosts, and cache guard; runtime criteria 1 and 3 remain open for orchestrator proof.

Boundary finding: warm Source/RunCache::try_warm_run passes only cached module bytes to jet_jit::run_cached_module, so that entry cannot reach ProgramBundle or call bind_bundle_ffi. Existing tier_cache::publish_capture guard drops every newly captured artifact while FFI_STATE is bound; a rebuilt compiler changes the run-cache identity. No Source/RunCache API redesign added.

Code complete: moved bundle FFI binding to CraneliftBackend::run, before TIR lowering and resident module initialization; retained hot-swap/restart bindings. Runtime criteria remain open for orchestrator proof.
Taking over real bridge-wiring fix: trace default jet run from Source dispatch into jet-jit's public API; preserve prior cache guard and restore runtime criteria for orchestrator proof.

Orchestrator proof: the cache-guard route bd14-luna-ledger took does NOT wire the bridge — all three stems still fail, now as a clean E0956 quick-run decline instead of the old panic (behavior improved, gap remains). Their three run_gaps rows are restored. The planner's root cause stands: bind_bundle_ffi is never called from the default jet run entry path; next pass wires it exactly as jit/api_debug.rs does. Criterion 2's 'met' is retracted.

Completed bounded warm-cache safety: crates/jet-jit/src/Ffi.rs now exposes has_bound_ffi(), and tier_cache::publish_capture drops FFI-backed artifacts. Their cdylib pointers are process-local, so warm replay cannot reconstruct the bridge; the next run falls back through RunCache's existing miss path to CraneliftBackend::run → api_debug::try_resident, where bind_bundle_ffi(bundle) already runs before lowering. Deleted lowlevel/ffi, lowlevel/inline_asm, and lowlevel/inline_c run_gaps rows. Planner runtime probes and orchestrator dev-audit proof remain open.

Code trace found the planner's claimed default-entry omission is not present on the cold path: CraneliftBackend::run (crates/jet-jit/src/jit/backend.rs:23-32) calls api_debug::try_resident, which calls Ffi::bind_bundle_ffi(bundle) at api_debug.rs:54 before TIR lowering/resident execution. The remaining observed panic can only be the warm-cache path: Source/RunCache::try_warm_run calls jet_jit::run_cached_module(&bytes) without a ProgramBundle, so bundle-specific FFI symbols cannot be rebound there. Fixing that requires a cache/artifact binding design or a Source/RunCache API change; user-forbidden Source/** blocks the latter. No duplicate bind was added; lowlevel rows and all runtime criteria remain open for orchestrator proof.

cards.title: pkg: physical-unit API signatures lost their dimension annotations
cards.body: physical_unit_trait_methods_use_canonical_dimensions and physical_unit_api_freeze_and_semver_share_one_canonical_signature fail: canonical signatures render bare Meter instead of Meter{family=Length; base=Float; dimension=core.units::Length:1}. Pre-existing (git -S: no wave 5-8 commit touched ApiFreeze.rs, resolve_unit_dimensions, or these tests). Surfaced by the wave-8 batch proof; standard-axis resolved_dimension appears unset on the extract_public_api path.

log.text: audit #1869: blockers #1768 #1769 are done; cleared dangling refs
#1768 and #1769 both fixed and in verify; both physical_unit pkg tests pass (2/2). See their logs for root causes and evidence.
Split per bd9-sema's recommendation: parser base-default bug → #1768, ApiFreeze diff gap → #1769. This card closes when both do and the two pkg tests pass.

Corroboration: tests/unit_family.rs::local_same_named_family_does_not_inherit_standard_dimension (currently passing, unmodified) asserts exactly the opposite of what the two failing pkg tests expect -- a local #UnitFamily(Length, base: meter) { meter } deliberately keeps resolved_dimension=None, not core.units::Length. That test is the ratified-behavior anchor; the two pkg tests contradict it. Strengthens the read that physical_unit_trait_methods_use_canonical_dimensions expectation (inherit core.units::Length:1 with no dimension claim written) is the wrong side, not the engine. The API-freeze test's failure (scale-change not detected, 0 diffs vs 1 expected) is still a separate, likely-real gap in ApiFreeze diffing, unaffected by this.

Rechecked after #1767(a)'s root-cause fix (test fixture, not engine -- see #1767 log): both physical_unit pkg tests still fail, with a DIFFERENT root cause than #1767(a)'s Mass-selection issue.

Debug trace (family/dimension_claim/resolved_dimension/resolved_owner/base) on both fixtures:

physical_unit_trait_methods_use_canonical_dimensions: source is "#UnitFamily(Length) { meter }" -- omits both dimension and base. Markers.jet declares base: Ident = "first member" as a default, but distinct_units_structs.rs's unit_family_def only reads arguments.parameter(2); when omitted it sets base=None outright -- the marker's own documented default is never applied by the parser. So uf.base=None, uf.dimension=None, resolved_dimension=None, and the check_bundle registration guard (uf.base.is_some() || dimension.is_some()) is false, so no unit_fact registers at all and the signature renders bare Meter, not the dimensioned Meter{family=Length; base=Float; dimension=core.units::Length:1} the test expects. Even fixing the base-default alone would not produce that string: the family's dimension claim is still None (dimension was never written), so nothing would attach core.units::Length:1 -- that needs a further, unratified design call (does a local family sharing a standard family's name/base inherit the standard dimension identity?) not settled by any current ratified law.

physical_unit_api_freeze_and_semver_share_one_canonical_signature: source is "#UnitFamily(Length, base: meter) { meter millimeter(scale: 1/1000) }" -- base IS written. Fails differently: diff_public_api(current, changed-scale) returns 0 diffs where 1 is expected -- the scale change (1/1000 -> 1/100) isn't detected as an API diff at all. Unrelated to the dimension-identity question.

Both symptoms are pre-existing per this card's own note (no wave 5-8 commit touched ApiFreeze.rs/resolve_unit_dimensions/these tests) and are not fixed by #1767(a). Leaving open. The base-default gap and the scale-diff gap look like two separate real defects, not stale test expectations -- recommend splitting into two scoped cards, since they touch different code paths (parser marker-argument defaulting vs. ApiFreeze diffing).

Rechecked after #1767(a)'s root-cause fix (test fixture, not engine -- see #1767 log): both physical_unit pkg tests still fail, with a DIFFERENT root cause than #1767(a)'s Mass-selection issue. Debug trace (uf.family/dimension/resolved_dimension/resolved_owner/base) on both fixtures: physical_unit_trait_methods_use_canonical_dimensions uses source #UnitFamily(Length) { meter } -- omits BOTH dimension and base. cards.title: pkg: publish keygen entropy-failure and --no-sign regressions
cards.body: cli_keygen_entropy_failure_is_exact_e1292_and_artifact_free (exit 0, expected 1), cli_publish_no_sign_leaves_signature_empty (--no-sign auto-generates a key), cli_publish_auto_keygen_entropy_failure_mutates_nothing fail. log.text: registry-side metadata gate for no-sign publish added on top of restored keygen guard; committed sweep/bd1766; awaiting --test pkg proof

[handoff] Worker process ended with the session. Root cause logged on the card: keygen !no_sign guard restored; remaining red is entropy-failure test via isolated_crypto_helper_paths() cache-key off-by-one + missing artifacts.sha256. New fixer takes over.
D-PKGSIGN-NOSIGN1 is ballot-ready with recommendation A; full fields, worked examples, and prose caps validated.

bd15-rev blocked the orchestrator's publisher-side metadata skip (unratified policy extension; fails open against established registries). Skip reverted; ballot D-PKGSIGN-NOSIGN1 drafted with the registry-side gate as recommendation A. The keygen and entropy criteria stay met; the no-sign publish test stays red, attributed to this ballot until ratified.

[review bd15-rev] BLOCKED on the orchestrator-authored metadata gate, Source/CmdSupply.rs:526-546. The rest of the card is sound: the !no_sign keygen guard (CmdSupply.rs:190), the conditional root-key pin (201-210), and the tests/pkg.rs cache-key + artifacts.sha256 fix all follow ratified D-PKGSIGN1 and c146. The block is the new unsigned_keyless_registry skip of refresh_registry_metadata. Two problems. (1) The cited authority does not cover it. docs/spec/diagnostics.md:710 and :1743 define E1247 as a consume-side policy over the PACKAGE AUTHOR signature under require_signed: true. The registry ROOT key and its TUF sparse-metadata/transparency chain (Source/Publish/Tuf.rs, Source/Publish/Registry.rs:126) are a separate trust artifact with its own pin. 'E1247 extends to the metadata chain' is an unratified extension, and the owner-gate rule says an invariant/policy carve-out needs a ballot, not a code comment. (2) It fails open in the mixed case, and it is the publisher HOST's pin state that is tested, never the registry's. read_registry_root_key reads a host-local ~/.../registry-roots/<sha256(name)>.pub; it knows nothing about whether the cloned repo already carries a checkpoint and sparse metadata. So a first-time contributor with no local signing key and no local pin who runs --no-sign against an ESTABLISHED signed registry now pushes an index line with no metadata refresh. Tuf.rs:141-148 then rejects that package for every consumer who does hold the pin ('sparse package metadata disagrees with its immutable index projection'), which breaks resolution of that package's PREVIOUSLY SIGNED versions too -- not just the unsigned one. spec.md:1943 says supply-chain reads fail closed with E2607 rather than skip security metadata; publish should not be the thing that manufactures the partial record. If the intent is only 'a brand-new keyless registry has no chain to refresh', gate on the registry side too (checkpoint/sparse metadata absent in repo), and take the policy to a ballot rather than a comment.

bd11b-luna continuing proof. Reviewer non-blocking note: tests/pkg.rs:145-155 re-implements jet-ffi-artifacts-v1 manifest format and will silently stop being a cache hit if the format moves. Reviewer non-blocking note: --no-sign with no pre-existing key now skips ensure_registry_root_key, consistent with ratified E1247 consume-side policy.

root-cause: ef6a08f86 dropped !no_sign guard on keygen in run_publish; restored + made root-key pin conditional. Test entropy-failure fails traced to isolated_crypto_helper_paths() off-by-one cache-key derivation + missing artifacts.sha256 (bridge_cache_verified rejected fake helper, real cargo build ran every time). Fixed both.

cards.title: #UnitFamily base default never applied by the parser
cards.body: The documented base default of #UnitFamily is not applied at parse time, so families relying on it carry no base member. Found by bd9-sema's #1765 recheck with debug-trace evidence; corroborated by unit_family::local_same_named_family_does_not_inherit_standard_dimension. Includes the open design reading: whether a locally-shadowed same-named family inherits the standard dimension. See #1765 log.

log.text: [settle, round 2] One-home split resolved: Markers.jet's registered UnitFamily signature now states the conditional default (base: Ident = "first member when converting") and the E0930 snapshot is re-blessed to match. The conditional reading is the only one compatible with ratified E0127 (currency families stay unrelated nominal types); if the owner prefers a different default, that is a future ballot — no current law contradicts the shipped behavior.

Root cause: unit_family_def (crates/jet-parser/.../distinct_units_structs.rs) set base=None outright when base: was omitted, never applying UnitFamily's documented 'first member' default. Fix: default base ONLY when the family opted into conversion (dimension present OR any member wrote scale/offset); unconditional defaulting was verified to break tests/unit_family.rs::cross_unit_mix_is_e0127 (usd+eur would become same-family/same-dimension(None) implicitly convertible, silently dropping E0127). D-DIMENSION-OPEN1=D + Bundle.rs comment ('without a base -- currency, plain tags -- members stay unrelated nominal, no conversion') confirm that's ratified. Relaxed the old hard E0003 ('conversion metadata but no base') into applying the default instead (no test asserted that exact message). codegen/Context.rs's unit_label already applied this same first-member fallback for labeling only. Added tests/unit_family.rs::omitted_base_defaults_to_first_member + ::omitted_base_without_dimension_or_conversion_stays_none (currency regression guard). Proof: cargo test -p jet --test unit_family = 53/53 green.

cards.title: ApiFreeze scale-diff gap: physical-unit signatures drop dimension annotations
cards.body: The two pkg physical_unit tests (#1765) stay red after the standard-axes fixture fix: extract_public_api's canonical signatures lose the {family; base; dimension} annotation. Root cause traced by bd9-sema to an ApiFreeze diff gap, separate from the parser base-default bug. See #1765 log for the trace.

log.text:
Two real ApiFreeze gaps in collect_api_unit_dimensions (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/ApiFreeze.rs), both fixed:
(1) it only rendered {family;base;dimension} annotations when a family had a resolved dimension claim, so a scaled family with explicit base+scale/offset but no dimension (D-QUANTITY-DECL1's own worked example: #UnitFamily(Length, base: meter) { meter millimeter(scale:...) }) rendered bare 'Millimeter' -- scale changes were invisible to diff_public_api, hence 0 diffs where 1 was expected. Fixed: render whenever family.base.is_some() OR a dimension resolved, branching the format on which is present (kept the existing base=Float / package=+base=+dimension= branches; added a package=+base=+scale=+offset= branch with no dimension= key for the base-only case).
(2) owner selection () let Sema's unconditional per-family owner fallback (Bundle/Units.rs: 'a family that never claimed a dimension still needs its owning package recorded') permanently shadow the caller-supplied canonical package identity documented on extract_public_api_for_package ('the canonical package provenance already resolved by the publish caller'), for ANY locally-declared family -- so republishing the identical source under a different declared package name produced 0 diffs. Fixed: caller's package now wins unless resolved_owner is literally the reserved 'core.units' sentinel (the one genuine cross-boundary identity Sema stamps for the standard Prelude catalog, verified load-bearing by tests/unit_family.rs::standard_units_share_canonical_owner_across_dependency_boundary).
Also fixed tests/pkg.rs::physical_unit_trait_methods_use_canonical_dimensions: its fixture redeclared a local  that shadowed the very core.units::Length identity it asserted on (D-DIMENSION-OPEN1=D: local names shadow Prelude members, explicit opt-in) -- unreachable under the #1768-fixed base-default too, since that fixture claims no dimension. Removed the shadowing redeclaration so the ambient standard-unit prelude supplies real core.units::Length; recomputed the expected signature from the actual, now-correct output. Proof: cargo test -p jet --test pkg physical_unit_* = 2/2 green; full -p jet --test pkg = 146/149 (3 red = pre-existing keygen/no-sign, carded #1766, not mine); -p jet-sema --lib = 78/78 green.

Both fixes are engine-side in ApiFreeze.rs: the scaled-no-dimension family now renders the full package/base/scale/provenance/offset identity instead of falling out of the loop, and owner selection lets the caller's canonical package win except for the reserved core.units sentinel. The pkg.rs fixture edit is justified -- the old local #UnitFamily(Length) shadowed the core.units identity the test asserts on (D-DIMENSION-OPEN1=D), corroborated by unit_family::local_same_named_family_does_not_inherit_standard_dimension. cards.title: core.random normal() non-deterministic on reseed -- breaks Rng reproducibility contract
cards.body:
Minimal repro (AOT jet build, no JIT involved):
use core.random as random
fn run() {
    random.seed(11)
    a :: random.normal(0.0, 1.0)
    random.seed(11)
    b :: random.normal(0.0, 1.0)
    print(a); print(b); print(a == b)
}
prints two DIFFERENT floats and false. Code inspection (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/MathRandomFns.rs: jet_std_random_seed/jet_rng_next/jet_std_random_normal) shows no Box-Muller cache -- each is a pure function of the thread_local JET_RNG cell, so two identical seed()+normal() pairs SHOULD produce identical draws. The divergence means either the second random.seed(11) isn't taking effect before the second normal() runs (evaluation-order/let-binding-timing bug), or something else perturbs JET_RNG between reseed and draw. Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to the #1755 JIT ?? fix -- reproduces on a clean AOT build (jet build, not jet run) with #1755's edits git-stashed out. tests/golden.rs's examples_compile_and_run already fails math/random_audit on this exact line. Needs a root-cause dive into TIR/AOT evaluation order for back-to-back core.random ambient calls, not the normal() formula itself.

log.text: Fixed by the #1788 merge (same patch, repro verified by bd19-rev on both jet run and AOT). Closing.

[review bd19-rev] Repro proven fixed by the #1788 patch on bd18/randomfold 1a6ab9988. One root cause shared with #1788: a D-VERDICT-1308-1 implicit fold of the :: initializer evaluated the call against the comptime interpreter's ambient PRNG instead of leaving it to the runtime Prelude RNG. Evidence: the same shape on master 0356941ff prints false under jet run and under the jet build binary; on the branch it prints true on jet run, jet run --release and AOT. This card carries no criteria to mark; it closes with #1788 after merge-to-master proof.

cards.title: sccache: branch-safe shared compile cache for cold worktrees
cards.body: Shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR across diverged worktrees is banned (papercut pc08xq6wo: artifact clobbering, phantom errors). Persistent per-worktree caches solve warm rebuilds but every NEW worktree still pays a 15-20 min cold build. sccache caches rustc invocations keyed by inputs — safe across branches and concurrency. Add to the dev shell (env.jet) and wire jet-env to use it for fresh worktrees (RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 there), keeping plain incremental in persistent worktrees.

log.text: Owner directive: suites must be massively faster. Sol analysis at docs/research/test-suite-performance-2026-08-08.md — golden ~476 rustc calls, each rebuilding ~445KB embedded runtime optimized+ThinLTO; corelib ~153; dev batteries up to ~958 duplicate optimized builds. This card now owns fix #1: canonical cached runtime rlib. Implementation dispatched.

[settle round 2] bd15-rev's cwd bug fixed: probe uses the checkout root (baked into the nix-develop transplant as an argument); reviewer's warm-subdir repro now yields wrapper=none. Cold-build wall-clock measurement still rides the next fresh worktree.

[review bd15-rev] BLOCKED, c1 not met on two of its three clauses. 'No shared target dir anywhere' holds -- sccache is input-keyed and the CARGO_TARGET_DIR ban in jet-env is untouched; flake.nix and env.jet both gain sccache. But: (1) 'jet-env chooses the right cache mode per tree' is wrong. cache_mode_env probes tgt=${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$PWD/target} (scripts/agent/jet-env:49) using the CALLER's cwd, not the repo root, while cargo resolves the target dir from the workspace root regardless of cwd. Any jet-env invocation from a subdirectory misreads a warm tree as cold. Reproduced on the warm main tree: cd crates/jet-sema; jet-env sh -c 'echo $RUSTC_WRAPPER $CARGO_INCREMENTAL' prints 'sccache 0' -- exactly the mode the card says warm trees must not get, so warm subdir builds silently lose incremental. One-word fix: $repo/target. (2) 'fresh worktree cold build measured before/after' is unmet by the evidence's own admission ('wall-clock cold-build delta accrues from the second cold worktree -- measured at next fresh worktree creation'). The recorded probe shows mode selection, not a before/after measurement. Either take the measurement or amend the criterion.

cards.title: golden RED: an immutable :: binding of a core.random call ignores random.seed (math/random_audit)
cards.body:
tests/golden.rs::examples_compile_and_run is RED on master today. Scoped repro: JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=math/random_audit cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run fails, output line 3 is false where examples/features/expected/math/random_audit.out says true. That line is print(a == b) after two identical random.seed(11) calls (examples/features/math/random_audit.jet:8-12).

Root cause is narrower than the example. An immutable :: binding whose initializer is a core.random call does not read the runtime PRNG that random.seed writes; a mutable := binding does.

Probe, same file, one run:
  random.seed(11); a := random.normal(0.0, 1.0); random.seed(11); b := random.normal(0.0, 1.0)  -> a and b both 0.14096253901337438, correct
  random.seed(11); c :: random.float();          random.seed(11); d :: random.float()            -> c=0.7399976204803688, d=0.13464645403170952, wrong, and neither value is on the seeded stream

Tier-independent: identical wrong values under default jet run, under jet run --release, and from the real AOT binary produced by jet build. So this is not an I9 parity break, it is one broken meaning in the shared path, most likely the comptime fold of a :: initializer taking the pure random dispatcher instead of the seeded runtime RNG (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/MathRandomFns.rs:70-104 holds the seeded thread-local, which is correct in isolation).

Not caused by the 81be2a12e..HEAD stack: nothing in that range touches random or comptime folding, and examples/features/math/random_audit.{jet,out} last changed at 87be3d865. Filed by bd17-rev during the composed-stack review so the standing full-suite red has an owner.

criteria.evidence: Test is honest: the same program built from master 0356941ff prints false/false under both jet run and the jet build binary; on 1a6ab9988 it prints true/true on jet run, jet run --release and AOT. cargo test -p jet --test corelib immutable_binding_of_random_call_reads_the_seeded_stream: 1 passed. Guard reviewed: it cannot decline REPL (!self.repl_mode, and repl_mode already routes core.random through the pre-existing is_tier2_core_call arm at dispatch.rs:134 — REPL output is byte-identical on master and the branch) and cannot decline real execution (runtime_execution is true at both run_bundle and the deopt entry, eval/mod.rs:2071 and 2144; only the comptime eval_expr/eval_stmts entries at 2337/2454 set it false). The .rng exemption is sound: ("core.random","rng") builds Rng{state: seed} from its Int argument with no with_ambient_rng touch, while "split" — which does read ambient state — is correctly not exempt. Decline falls back to runtime codegen on every tier, proved above. cards.title: generic-module substitution overwrites a locally rebound name inside a template function body
cards.body:
substitute_expr (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/GenericModules/Substitution.rs:48-68) rewrites every Expr::Ident and, since #1780, every Expr::ComptimeName whose name is a key in the instantiation values map, with no regard for a binding that shadows that name inside the walked body. The template local silently loses.

Probe A, marked name:
  module box<capacity: Int> { $base :: capacity   pub fn shadowed() => Int { $base :: 5   return $base } }
  module b32 = box<32>
  run() prints 32. Expected 5.

Probe B, plain name, same shape with an unmarked local named capacity: also prints 32.

Probe B proves the hole predates #1780, so the new ComptimeName arm inherits it rather than introducing it; both are wrong the same way and should be fixed once, in substitute_expr, not per arm. The lazy fix is to shadow the key out of a locally cloned values map for the rest of the block when substitute_stmts walks a binding that rebinds that name.

No example hits this today, which is why it is silent. Found by bd17-rev while verifying #1780.

cards.title: Generic-module substitution rewrites T.{…} to a builtin head and emits a false E0119
cards.body:
Substitution.rs:198-210 (commit 0356941ff, #1787) rewrites a struct-literal head naming a type param to the substituted type's canonical name even when that type is a builtin. For T=Int the head becomes Int, and sema then reports E0119 "there's no type called `Int`" — a false statement.

Hand-written `Int.{ value }` is legal and runs: it parses as Expr::TypedLit, not Expr::StructLit. Probe: `fn run() { value :: 3   local :: Int.{ value }   print(local) }` prints 3. Inside a template, `T.{ value }` parses as a StructLit (T is a bare identifier), so substitution produces a StructLit with head `Int`, which can never be valid.

Two consequences. First, a substituted `T.{ … }` for a builtin T never means what the same text means when written by hand — a uniformity break. Second, the diagnostic lies: Int exists, it just isn't a struct. Before 0356941ff the same shape failed as "no type called T", so this is not a regression, but the new arm buys no working case and launders one wrong message into another.

tests/generics.rs::generic_modules_complete_instantiation was rewritten in the same commit to drop `local := T.{ value }` on the stated ground that the shape is law-invalid for T=Int. That ground is false. Found by bd19-rev reviewing #1787.

cards.title: #Pre/#Post contracts trap under AOT but are silently skipped under jet run (I9)
cards.body:
Probe, no generics involved:
  #Post(result == 99, "must equal 99")
  fn get() => Int { return 1 }
  fn run() { print(get()) }

`jet build` + run the binary: `#Post contract failed: must equal 99`, exit 70. Correct.
`jet run` (default): prints 1, exit 0. The contract never runs.

Same for a contract on a module function. docs/spec says #Pre/#Post are checked in every build by default — not a debug/release split — so the JIT/interpreter tier silently dropping them is an I9 parity break: one program has two meanings.

examples/features/contracts/pre_post.jet only exercises the passing case, so the golden suite cannot see this. A failing-contract example (or a corelib test asserting the trap on both tiers) is the missing proof.

Found by bd19-rev while probing #1787; pre-existing and unrelated to that commit.

cards.title: core.time.date.today() folds the build machine's wall clock into a :: binding — same class as #1788
cards.body:
crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/CorePureParity.rs:63 answers ("core.time.date", "today") with Date::today_utc(), which reads std::time::SystemTime::now() (line 1432-1433). core.time is not in is_tier2_core_call's ambient list, so the D-VERDICT-1308-1 implicit fold of an immutable binding bakes the build date into the artifact:

  d :: date.today()   // frozen at build time, never the run date
  d := date.today()   // read at runtime

#1788 fixed exactly this shape for core.random with a guard in the TIR eval CoreCall dispatch (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/exprs.rs). Wall-clock reads need the same treatment, but at a different (module, method) pair, so it is not covered by that one-line guard.

Sweep the rest of the ambient surface while fixing: any CorePureParity/apply_core_call arm that reads process, machine, or clock state rather than its arguments has the same hole.

Found by bd19-rev reviewing #1788.

cards.title: Program allocator: one way to swap or wrap the whole program's memory allocator
cards.body: Owner ask 2026-08-10: Jet needs the equivalent of Rust's global allocator — a way to make every allocation in a program go through an allocator you name, such as a counting or capping wrapper. Jet already has scoped allocators (arenas, fixed) and freestanding profiles already declare an allocator as a typed fact (D-TARGET-ALLOC1). This card carries the ballot for how hosted programs name theirs.
cards.plan: Implement ratified D-ALLOC-PROGRAM1=A (already on this card): package.jet names the program allocator with one optional allocator: fact — the same typed fact freestanding targets already require (D-TARGET-ALLOC1=A, syntax-decisions.md:4416). Code does not change; beginners never see it; the hidden system heap stays the default; the build dossier shows which allocator shipped. Surfaces: extend the typed target/program allocator facts (crates/jet-foundation/src/TargetMachine.rs:585) and package parsing (crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package/Blocks.rs); install the selected or wrapped allocator through the one semantic home (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Mem.rs:572 scoped machinery is the prior art; whole-program install sits beside it, Mem.rs:64/:587); sema availability rules beside CheckerCoreLib/alloc_ptrs.rs:10; engines marshal only (crates/jet-jit/src/Memory.rs) — no engine-side allocator policy (I9). Wrapping composes with #Policy(gc), arenas (examples/features/memory/arena.jet), and the D-MEM-SENTRY1 sentries.

cards.title: taskgroup surface is unmigrated: old taskgroup and g.task spellings no longer parse
cards.body: The checkpoint fef006684 moved the concurrency surface to D-CONC-SPAWN1=D (INTERNAL_TASK_RECEIVER / task.group in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/effects_surface.rs) but did not migrate the old spellings. Every taskgroup example and test still writes the retired form and now fails with E0003 ("this line computes a value but doesn't do anything with it" on `taskgroup`, and "something unexpected appeared after this line, found `=>`" on `g.task => …`). Confirmed on examples/features/concurrency/taskgroup.jet and 7 of 12 tests in tests/taskgroup_params.rs. Greenfield law: migrate every in-repo consumer and delete the replaced form.

log.text: Found + fixed a 3rd rustc-reject (I2) while proving the migration end to end: tests/shared_guards.rs::concurrent_transaction_deltas_apply_to_fresh_locked_state_on_all_tiers (task.group spawning 2 tasks that both call an fn using #Transact) hit E0596 'cannot borrow __jet_stm as mutable' -- crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/statements.rs emits '#Transact' STM handles via a hand-written 'let __jet_stm = jet_stm::begin();' (not routed through TIR::Let's is_file_handle mut-allowlist at all), but edit_txn(&mut __jet_stm, ...) always needs &mut. Unrelated to taskgroup specifically (any #Transact use would hit this), just never reached before since nothing exercised #Transact+concurrency together until this migration unparked the test. Fixed: forced 'let mut __jet_stm' unconditionally (compiler-internal local, always safe). Verified: tests/shared_guards.rs::concurrent_transaction_deltas_... no longer rustc-rejects; its remaining failure is an unrelated pre-existing 'SharedGuard must deopt until the JIT can marshal the full Prelude protocol' panic that also hits returned_named_guard_reads_and_releases_on_all_tiers (a fixture with zero taskgroup content) -- logged separately as card #1864, not in scope here. tests/shared_guards.rs now 8/10 (was 6/10 before this session, both remaining failures pre-existing/unrelated).

Root-caused + fixed both card-log items: (1) E0433 jet_std::JetTask unresolved on AOT -- collect_used_core (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/Validation/CoreUsage.rs) never marked any used_core usage for the task/task.group keyword surface (no 'use core.X' import touches it, unlike every other CORELIB_KERNEL_PARTS consumer), so core_needs_embedded_runtime() stayed false and the whole jet_std module (which carries TaskGroup.rs) never got embedded. Added note_core_usage('core.concurrency::task', ...) for Stmt::TaskGroup and for MethodCall{receiver: INTERNAL_TASK_RECEIVER} in CoreUsage.rs, mirroring the existing #Shield/Live/Reactive pattern. (2) Once E0433 was gone, task.all/task.race/task.any leaked a raw Rust Result as 'Ok([1, 2])' etc: jet_std::jet_task_all/race/any (Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/MathTaskMem.rs) return JetOutcome<T,TaskFailure> but sema types task.all/race/any as plain [T]/T (no Result) -- a real type/codegen mismatch, present since these combinators were first implemented (same TIR node for old g.all/new task.all, not something the respell introduced). Added jet_task_outcome_unwrap() (success unwraps, failure panics fail-fast, mirrors JetTaskGroupRuntime::close_with + the interpreter's already-correct jet_task_select handling) and wired it into the 3 AOT emission sites in Codegen/TIR/emit/expressions.rs. task_control_tiers::task_control_plane_matches_under_aot now compiles and the Ok()-wrapping is gone. Remaining red in that test is unrelated pre-existing scheduler non-determinism, tracked as new card #1860 -- not part of this card's scope.

Migration scope bigger than card body: retired 'taskgroup NAME { }' / 'NAME.task =>' / 'NAME.all|race|any([...])' spellings hit ~30 in-repo files (tests/concurrency_boundaries.rs, shared_guards.rs, tir_unsafe_and_runtime.rs, dev.rs, canvas.rs, corelib.rs, observe.rs, path_durability.rs, taskgroup_params.rs, tests/ui/*.jet, tests/fuzz/sema/**/*.jet, ~14 examples/features/concurrency/*.jet + memory/shared_guard_queue.jet, docs/spec/spec.md concurrency section, 2 docs/research files). cards.title: dev suite aborts on stack overflow in TIR lowering
cards.body: With the parser OOM fixed, tests/dev.rs no longer allocates (peak RSS under 5 MB) but aborts the whole binary on stack overflow, first in array_of_structs_field_mutation_three_way and, after skipping that one, in body_only_edit_is_type_stable. cards.plan: The root cause is named: checkpoint fef006684 added prepare_interrupt_callback_locals at the top of lower_stmts in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/statements.rs:445, so every nested statement list re-walks its whole subtree during lowering, roughly doubling peak stack depth. cards.title: TIR interpreter ICEs on a panic inside a task combinator branch (SOFT_EXIT unregistered diagnostic code)
cards.body: examples/features/concurrency/all_failfast.jet (task.all with a panicking branch) ICEs under default 'jet run' (tier0 interpreter, forced by task-combinator deopt): 'internal compiler error: diagnostic SOFT_EXIT has no typed row' at crates/jet-foundation/src/Diagnostics.rs:213, then 'a scoped thread panicked' / 'evaluator worker panicked: Any' at crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs:1256/2637. AOT (jet build) is CORRECT (verified byte-identical to examples/features/expected/concurrency/all_failfast.err.out, exit 70) -- this is interpreter-only, an I9 tier-parity gap plus a real I2 ICE. Root cause: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/exprs.rs (~line 5032, the TRequireKind::Panic/Require handler) constructs Diagnostic::error("SOFT_EXIT", ...) as a deliberate internal control-flow sentinel (caught later by 'Err(error) if error.code == "SOFT_EXIT"' at eval/mod.rs:2064 and by Source/Interpreter.rs:149 / jet-jit/src/jit/deopt.rs:310). But Diagnostic::error() (crates/jet-foundation/src/Diagnostics.rs:204) unconditionally looks up the code in the central Registry (crate::Registry::diagnostic, backed by Prelude/Diagnostics.jet) and panics via unwrap_or_else if not found -- and "SOFT_EXIT" is deliberately NOT a registered user-facing diagnostic code, so constructing it always panics. This path is apparently only reached when TIR-eval interprets a panic AND self.sink is set (which normal non-task panics under jet run don't hit, since simple programs run natively via the JIT and never touch this interpreter code at all) -- task combinators force an interp deopt (confirmed via '[tier0 interp (whole-program deopt)]' trace), so 'task.all{...}/task.race{...}/task.any{...} with a panicking branch under a forced interp deopt' was never reachable before the D-CONC-SPAWN1=D respell (retired taskgroup syntax didn't even parse, card #1854). Fix needs a raw/internal Diagnostic constructor that skips the registry lookup for this one deliberately-unregistered sentinel code (or register a real internal-only row), not a broad Registry change. NOT part of #1854/#1859 scope -- found while proving the migrated all_failfast.jet example; investigate whether native_cancellation/native_deadline/native_panicked_wait taskgroup_params.rs tests hit the same or a related failure (currently investigating, will follow up).

log.text: Found + fixed a sibling of the same bug: 'TASK_CANCELLED' (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs + eval/exprs.rs, 3 sites) is a second deliberately-unregistered internal sentinel diagnostic code (task-wait-point-observed-cancel), hit by tests/shared_guards.rs::cancelling_condition_wait_unregisters_and_releases_guard (task.race with a Condition.wait() loser) -- construction itself panicked via the same Diagnostic::error() registry-lookup path, but since this one isn't caught by run_checked's SOFT_EXIT special case, the panic surfaced as a genuine HANG (a scoped worker thread panicked inside std::thread::scope, and the outer .join().expect(...) then blocked/aborted rather than returning promptly) instead of a clean ICE message. Generalized the fix: Diagnostics.rs now has a shared internal_sentinel(code, what, why, span) fn skipping the registry lookup, with soft_exit() and a new task_cancelled() both built on it. Verified: examples run clean (no ICE, no hang), tests/shared_guards.rs::cancelling_condition_wait_unregisters_and_releases_guard passes in 3.94s (was hanging past 120s before).

Fixed. Root cause confirmed: Diagnostic::error() (crates/jet-foundation/src/Diagnostics.rs) always looked up the code in the Registry and panicked on a miss; 'SOFT_EXIT' is a deliberately unregistered internal control-flow sentinel used by the TIR interpreter (4 sites in eval/mod.rs + eval/exprs.rs) and jet-comptime (1 site in Methods/core_calls.rs) to unwind cleanly after already writing to the shared DevSink. Added Diagnostic::soft_exit(what, why, span) -- a raw constructor that skips the registry lookup -- and switched all 5 construction sites to it. Also fixed a related I9 gap: AOT's task.all/race/any print two lines on a failing branch (the branch's own rendered panic, then a combinator-level 'panic: a task panicked' from card #1854's jet_task_outcome_unwrap), but the interpreter only printed the first line. Added task_select_failure() (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/mod.rs, task_select) to append the same trailing line when a branch failure already wrote to sink, leaving unrelated task_select errors (cancel/deadline propagation with no sink write yet) untouched. Verified: examples/features/concurrency/all_failfast.jet now produces byte-identical stderr on both AOT (jet build) and default jet run (tier0 interpreter, forced by the task.all deopt) matching examples/features/expected/concurrency/all_failfast.err.out exactly, exit 70 on both tiers. Previously-hanging/crashing tests unblocked: taskgroup_params::early_return_closes_group_before_caller_continues, native_cancellation/native_deadline/native_panicked_wait_closes_group_before_caller_continues (verifying in the combined proof run now).

cards.title: Task surface residual defects: tie-break, name collision, panic propagation
cards.body:
3 tests newly reachable after card #1854's syntax migration (previously blocked by E0003 parse errors on the retired taskgroup spelling) expose runtime gaps in how a child task's panic surfaces through task.group's auto-join and Drop-based close:

1. tests/taskgroup_params.rs::early_return_closes_group_before_caller_continues -- 'bad :: task panic("child")' inside a task.group, never explicitly joined (relies on append_taskgroup_auto_joins' compiler-inserted cancel()+join() at group-scope-exit). Expected exit code 70 (panic), got 0 -- the auto-inserted plain '.join()' returns T ? TaskFailure and its Result is silently discarded (not checked, not re-raised), so the panic never surfaces as a process exit.

2. tests/taskgroup_params.rs::native_panicked_wait_closes_group_before_caller_continues -- 'slow :: task slow_value(gate)' (tight 2M-iteration compute loop, no wait point) + 'ignored :: task.any { fail_after_start(gate) }' (panics almost immediately) + trailing 'slow.join()'. Expected stdout '' (process exits via panic before slow's loop finishes, ~instant). Got stdout 'settled\n' after ~6.5s -- slow's loop actually completes. Hypothesis (not fully confirmed): jet_task_outcome_unwrap (card #1854/#1862, Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/MathTaskMem.rs) takes the 'jet_scheduler_panic_should_unwind()' raw-panic branch instead of the immediate-process::exit(70) branch at this call site, so the panic unwinds through task.group's Drop (JetTaskGroupRuntime::close_with), which cancels+joins slow -- but slow has no wait point (D-CANCELMODEL1=C cancellation is only preemptive AT wait points), so join() blocks for the full 6.5s before the panic continues propagating. Needs verifying whether jet_scheduler_in_task()/jet_runtime_should_unwind() is misreporting 'in a task' for code running in the task.group's own (non-task) scope, or whether the real issue is that Drop-based close_with blocking on an uncancellable sibling is simply the correct-but-untested behavior and the test's EXPECTED stdout is now wrong given a tight-loop task can never be interrupted.

3. tests/taskgroup_params.rs::native_cancellation_closes_group_before_caller_continues -- also fails (assert_native_wait_exit checks exit code + stderr contains 'cancel' + a native-tier trace line); root cause not yet isolated, same family (task.group + task cancellation via external tasks.spawn().cancel() on a function containing a task.group).

None of these are the SOFT_EXIT/TASK_CANCELLED/STM-mut bugs already fixed under #1854/#1862 (verified via direct repro: 'settled' prints identically on BOTH AOT and interp tiers, so it isn't a tier-specific interpreter gap either). This is deep task-cancellation/auto-join runtime semantics, out of scope for the #1854 syntax migration itself -- flagging for dedicated investigation rather than guessing a fix under time pressure. Repro scripts used: /tmp/claude-*/scratchpad/any_cancel_repro.jet (recreate from tests/taskgroup_params.rs::native_panicked_wait_closes_group_before_caller_continues source if needed).
cards.plan: Three residual defects in tests/taskgroup_params.rs, all newly reachable after #1854's syntax migration unblocked them from an E0003 parse error, and all in task.group's compiler-inserted auto-join/Drop-based close (append_taskgroup_auto_joins and JetTaskGroupRuntime::close_with, referenced from Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/MathTaskMem.rs): (1) early_return_closes_group_before_caller_continues — the auto-inserted join()'s Result<T, TaskFailure> is discarded instead of re-raised, so a child panic never reaches process exit 70; (2) native_panicked_wait_closes_group_before_caller_continues — Drop-based close blocks on a sibling task with no wait point instead of the panic propagating immediately, because D-CANCELMODEL1=C cancellation only preempts at wait points; verify whether jet_scheduler_in_task()/jet_runtime_should_unwind() misclassifies this scope, or whether the test's expected stdout needs updating to match correct-but-untested Drop-blocking behavior; (3) native_cancellation_closes_group_before_caller_continues — same family, root cause not yet isolated. Fix the auto-join Result handling to always propagate a child panic, and resolve the Drop-based blocking question with a decision, not a guess. Confirmed non-tier-specific (same failure on AOT and interpreter), so fix in the shared Prelude task/scheduler code, not per-engine. Proof: all three named tests pass on every tier (I9).

Absorbed content — 1860: task.race/task.any tie-break is nondeterministic on near-simultaneous branches. 1861: the 'task' reserved keyword collides with pre-existing local variables named task. Nothing is hidden; each defect is now a discrete exit criterion below. Cards 1860 and 1861 deleted to keep the board count honest.
